    # AI Workflows
    
    ## Project Architecture Change Workflow
    
    Use this workflow for changes to system architecture, technology choices, service or domain boundaries, persistence, runtime behavior, security boundaries, repository structure, deployment topology, or any decision documented in `docs/project-architecture/README.md`.
    
    `docs/project-architecture/README.md` is the source of truth for project architecture.
    
    1. Read `docs/project-architecture/README.md` in full before proposing or implementing an architecture change.
    2. Discuss the motivation, alternatives, tradeoffs, migration impact, and implementation boundaries with the user.
    3. Do not modify files or implement the change until the user explicitly confirms the agreed approach.
    4. After confirmation, update `docs/project-architecture/README.md` before changing implementation files.
    5. Update all affected sections so the document remains internally consistent; do not leave obsolete guidance in place.
    6. Add a dated entry to the document's `Changelog` describing the decision and its impact.
    7. Implement only the architecture described by the updated document and only within the approved scope.
    8. If implementation reveals a required deviation or new architectural choice, stop and return to user discussion and explicit confirmation.
    9. Keep code, configuration, tests, and operational documentation consistent with the architecture source of truth.
    10. Report both documentation and implementation changes when handing the task back to the user.
    
    If a request contains architecture and ordinary implementation work, this workflow takes precedence for the architecture portion. After the architecture is approved and documented, apply any relevant implementation workflow to the remaining work.
    
    ## UI Change Workflow
    
    Use this workflow for any user-interface change, including pages, components, layouts, visual styling, design tokens, colors, typography, icons, motion, responsive behavior, themes, user-facing copy, interaction feedback, and workflow-editor presentation.
    
    `docs/ui-design-system/README.md` is the source of truth for UI design principles and visual language. `ui-ux-design/README.md` is the source of truth for page structure, shared UI architecture, implementation sequencing, and page-level acceptance criteria.
    
    1. Read `docs/ui-design-system/README.md` and `ui-ux-design/README.md` in full before proposing or implementing a UI change. Then follow the design index and read every shared document and applicable `DESIGN.md` for the requested surface.
    2. Compare the requested change with the documented principles, tokens, shared patterns, page rules, interaction patterns, and product-specific guidance.
    3. Explain the proposed visual result, affected surfaces, relevant tradeoffs, and any required design-system changes to the user.
    4. Do not modify UI files or implement the change until the user explicitly confirms the proposed approach.
    5. If the proposal introduces or changes a design decision, update the affected `DESIGN.md`, applicable shared specification, and `ui-ux-design/README.md` index before changing implementation files. New pages require a page `DESIGN.md` before implementation.
    6. Implement only the confirmed approach. Use shared semantic design tokens and reusable components; do not introduce page-level hard-coded styles that duplicate or bypass the design system.
    7. Design and implement light and dark modes together. Neither mode may be treated as a fallback or simple color inversion.
    8. Preserve accessibility, including sufficient contrast, visible keyboard focus, non-color status cues, reduced-motion support, and accessible names for icon-only controls.
    9. If implementation reveals a conflict with the design system or requires a new design choice, stop and return to user discussion and explicit confirmation.
    10. Do not create or modify tests. After implementation, only a simple type check is permitted; do not package, build, or run test suites.
    11. Report the design-system basis, shared and page documents read or changed, affected UI surfaces, light and dark mode behavior, and type-check result when handing the task back to the user.
    
    If a request contains both architecture and UI changes, apply the Project Architecture Change Workflow first, then this workflow. This workflow takes precedence over the General Fallback Workflow for UI work.
    
    ## General Fallback Workflow
    
    Use this workflow only when no more specific workflow applies to the user's request.
    
    1. Do not execute the request immediately.
    2. Explain the proposed development approach, intended changes, and relevant implementation considerations to the user.
    3. Wait for the user's explicit confirmation before modifying files or performing any implementation action.
    4. After confirmation, implement only the approved approach and scope.
    5. Do not create or modify test cases for the implementation.
    6. After implementation, only a simple type check is permitted.
    7. Do not package or build the project.
    8. Do not run test cases or attempt other validation commands beyond the permitted simple type check.
    9. Report the implemented changes and the result of the type check, if one was available and performed.

    docs/project-architecture/README.md:143:`typesafe/systemone` is a credential-forwarding transport rather than a text-generation protocol. Its upstream contract accepts a `state` value and a typed `questions` collection and returns a typed `answers` collection, so it has no messages, system prompt, tool declarations, or streaming form. The Gateway does not translate this protocol into or out of any chat contract. It resolves the Provider from the public `<providerName>/<modelId>` namespace, replaces the namespaced `model` field with the upstream model id, attaches the stored API key and headers, forwards the request body unchanged, and returns the upstream response unchanged. Because the request never enters a Portkey provider handler, this transport records its own request statistics and request log directly; the upstream `input_tokens` and `output_tokens` values populate the existing token statistics without a separate accounting path. Providers using this protocol are excluded from Agent model selection, since an Agent node's system prompt and output format have no meaning in this contract. Its connection test sends one minimal typed question instead of the fixed chat prompt, and its model catalog is entered manually because the upstream publishes no model-discovery endpoint.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:145:Codex image generation is exposed through the unified Provider proxy route above and the first-party Workflow image node. The Codex adapter forwards an explicit generation allowlist consisting of `prompt`, `model`, `n`, `background`, `quality`, and `size`; standard OpenAI Images fields that Codex does not define, including `response_format`, `style`, and `user`, are not forwarded. The Provider protocol remains `codex/responses`, and the automatic Provider advertises `gpt-image-2` as `codex/gpt-image-2`. Requests use the Codex OAuth account pool and the same selected-account one-shot unauthorized refresh behavior as Responses transport. Upstream JSON, including each generated image in `data[].b64_json`, is returned to the original caller, while account entitlement and image-generation quota failures surface as upstream errors. Image edits and binary Artifact persistence remain unsupported.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:225:Workflow Agent nodes are the only user-configurable Agent capability. Each node owns its public model id, system prompt, output format, Skill selections, and MCP server selections inside the immutable WorkflowVersion. Workflows never reference standalone Agent or AgentVersion resources. Every Agent uses the protected `gateway-provider` binding; the binding is not a user-selectable Provider and is omitted from Provider listings and forms. Skill and MCP definitions remain reusable workspace resources, but their assignment is explicit inside each Workflow Agent node. Chat Bot configuration is protected and is not a user-managed Agent assignment. The API validates that every selected Skill and MCP server belongs to the same workspace.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:233:The first-party `typesafe/systemone@1` Node Type is the Workflow entry point for the credential-forwarding TypeSafe System One protocol. It accepts a required JSON-compatible `state` input and exposes the upstream System One response, including its required typed `answers` object, through `output`. For object state, the node retains the state's top-level JSON fields and overlays the upstream response so downstream nodes can keep using the original context while routing on typed answers; for primitive or array state, the original value is exposed under `state`. Its immutable configuration contains a public `<providerName>/<modelId>` model id and a JSON `questions` object; the node does not store credentials, base URLs, or Provider ids. Runtime execution resolves the public model against the Gateway-owned Provider catalog, requires the selected Provider to use `typesafe/systemone`, and calls the internal Gateway proxy with Workflow Run and Node Run correlation headers. The Gateway request and response remain System One bodies with `model`, `state`, and `questions`; the state pass-through is added at the Workflow node boundary, not in Gateway transport. Typed answer fields can be routed with the existing structured edge paths, such as `$.answers.articleType.choice`. Existing `typesafe/systemone` Providers remain excluded from Agent model selection.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:237:The initial plugin runtime includes two product-owned capabilities: the `codex-cli-chat` execution plugin and its optional `wechat-clawbot` transport. Both are registered by the API and stored as workspace plugin resources. Codex execution uses the existing Agent execution, message, SSE, cancellation, and audit contracts. A plugin execution is persisted against a protected system Agent identity so the browser can reuse the existing execution viewer without exposing the plugin as a configurable Agent. Each turn starts the plugin's persisted executable command with `exec --json` through the Commands process boundary, sends the prompt through stdin, parses the final Agent message from JSONL, and stores the response in the normal execution transcript. Conversation history is included in the next turn's prompt; the plugin does not depend on Codex session files or interactive TUI state.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:239:The `wechat-clawbot` capability is a server-owned iLink text transport. It keeps the bot token, base URL, QR login state, long-poll cursor, and connection status in SQLite; the token is encrypted using the existing secret-storage convention and is never returned to the browser. A background service performs QR login, `ilink/bot/getupdates` long polling, duplicate-safe cursor advancement, and `ilink/bot/sendmessage` replies. Each WeChat user is mapped to one WorkLite Codex Agent execution, allowing later messages to continue the same transcript. The first increment supports text messages only; media download/upload and group-routing policy remain deferred. The browser exposes login, disconnect, and connection status controls on the plugin configuration page, while polling and credentials remain entirely server-owned.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:241:The Codex CLI plugin owns an editable executable command configuration, defaulting to `codex`, in the persisted Plugin row. The value contains one executable name or path followed by optional fixed leading arguments. The API parses that value into an argument vector without shell operators, expansion, or environment-variable substitution, uses the same vector for availability probing and execution, and appends its product-owned `exec --json` arguments afterward. It never reads a command override from an environment variable. The command is executed through the existing shell command boundary with each parsed value quoted independently, using the API process working directory and inherited process environment to match the existing Host Command Interface. The browser exposes Plugins as a first-level workspace resource with a dedicated list and configuration page; saving and testing are server-owned operations. The same page owns WeChat QR login and connection controls for the transport capability. Skills and MCP servers remain capability resources, while Model Providers remain in the Providers destination. There is no user-uploaded plugin code, marketplace installation, or network authorization layer in this increment. Existing `codex` values remain valid without migration. Existing Workflow and execution records remain valid without migration; startup bootstrap adds or repairs the protected plugin row and Chat Bot configuration without removing user data.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:243:Agent is one Node Type rather than the Workflow Engine's universal primitive. The first-party `worklite/agent` adapter stores a public `<providerName>/<modelId>` model id, system prompt, Skill identifiers, and MCP server identifiers directly in its immutable WorkflowVersion configuration. Its configuration also owns `outputFormat` as `text` or `json`, with `text` as the default. JSON mode parses the final Agent response as JSON and accepts an optional fenced JSON block, but rejects surrounding prose; invalid JSON fails the Agent node. JSON mode additionally owns an optional `outputContract`: a non-empty array of unique non-empty strings naming top-level keys the parsed object must carry. When present, the parsed output must be a JSON object and every named key must exist with a value that is not `null`, an empty string, or an empty array; a missing or empty key fails the Agent node with an error naming the absent keys. Parsing alone accepts any valid JSON, so without a contract a node can commit a value that is well-formed but is not its intended result, such as a progress note or a tool-call object, and every downstream node then consumes that value as if the node had succeeded. Contract failures use the node's ordinary `errorPolicy` and the existing failed-node retry path and introduce no separate failure state. The contract is a presence check on top-level keys only; `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` remain capability metadata that the runtime does not enforce, and full JSON Schema validation for node inputs and outputs remains a separate architecture decision. For evidence-heavy Agent nodes, optional positive `maxToolCalls`, `maxToolRounds`, and `maxToolResultChars` limit actual script/MCP invocations, tool rounds, and text returned to the model and model tool rounds; after the budget is spent, the runtime removes tools and asks for a final answer from collected evidence, and does not execute excess calls in a batch. An optional `passthroughKeys` list on JSON-mode Agents copies the specified top-level keys from the input context into the parsed result after model output validation, so an editorial model cannot rewrite the writer's article or evidence. Its `context` input defines one isolated invocation. The adapter returns only text or parsed JSON through the generic node result without separate Workflow output persistence and does not create Artifacts. It reuses shared Agent Runtime infrastructure without creating or referencing Agent or AgentVersion records.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:338:The GitHub Technology Trend Research Workflow seed composes Workflow Input, read-only Artifact Query, four embedded Agent roles (topic, collector, writer, reviewer), a cover-prompt Agent, a deterministic `worklite/approved-article@1` extraction node, and two Artifact nodes. The seed resolves existing named Skills and public Gateway models in the target profile without copying credentials. Planning and cover use a fast model, research and writing use a capable writing model, and independent review uses a different provider family when available. A less reliable review provider may retain its ordinary retry policy.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:340:The collector uses bounded tool calls and rounds and compact research results; it gathers mechanism evidence from repositories, commits, issues, and relevant community sources, preserving historical candidate metadata from Artifact Query. Exhausted or failed tools require reporting evidence gaps rather than repeated calls. The writer produces a structured JSON draft containing title, topic, thesis, evidenceUsed, candidates, and the original Markdown article. The reviewer returns only `approved`, `duplicate`, `matchedArtifactIds`, and at most three actionable feedback items. The runtime carries the writer's article, title, topic, thesis, evidenceUsed, and candidates unchanged into the reviewer result. One rejection can return to the writer for one revision; a second rejection reaches the deterministic article gate and fails the Run without creating the final Article Artifact or WeChat draft.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:342:The `worklite/approved-article@1` node accepts the reviewer JSON at a required `context` port, requires an explicit true approval and false duplicate, and returns the original Markdown article only when its Markdown headings and fenced code blocks are structurally sound. It never repairs corrupted text or infers an approval. A failed gate uses the ordinary failed-node retry path. Research Notes Artifacts remain separate; the approved Markdown article fans out to the Article Artifact, cover-prompt Agent and WeChat v2 draft node. The cover prompt drives `worklite/image@1`; the generated PNG is passed to the draft node. Published Workflow versions remain immutable: existing versions and historical Runs are not rewritten, and the new seed requires an updated runtime and a newly published Workflow version before it takes effect. No compatibility node or migration is added.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:367:- `worklite/dashboard` accepts `data`, exposes the committed upstream value through `output`, and carries the immutable Home board layout. The board format is generic and compositional: `layout.header`, `layout.main`, and `layout.footer` each contain ordered elements of kind `text`, `count`, `metric`, or `list`. A `text` element carries static text; a `count` element carries a label and resolves to the output item total; a `metric` element carries a label plus a field key and type and reads that key from an object output; a `list` element carries a `titleKey` and display `{ key, label, type }` fields with `text`, `number`, `boolean`, `datetime`, or `url` types, and its items are the output array or the single object output. A `url` field is not rendered as a table column: when an item's value for it is an `http(s)` string, the row navigates to that value. The committed output must be a JSON object or an array of JSON objects. Home renders the board directly on its card; the first list element is the card's paginated table content. Unknown fields are ignored, missing fields display explicit empty values, and non-object list items render as bounded raw JSON. Rendering is tolerant: contract mismatches never fail the board or the node.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:369:Publication requires every `typesafe/systemone-map@1` node to contain a valid public model id, a non-empty `questions` object, and a non-empty `itemsPath`, and rejects a non-positive `concurrency`, a `rank` without a non-empty `path`, a non-positive `rank.limit`, and a non-numeric `rank.minimum`. Publication requires every Workflow Agent node to contain a valid public model id and to reference only Skills and MCP servers from the workspace. An Agent node that declares `outputContract` must set `outputFormat` to `json` and must supply a non-empty array of unique non-empty key names. Agent `context` is optional. It may receive one unbounded initial edge (an explicit Workflow Input edge must be unconditional) and one bounded feedback edge; when no unbounded incoming edge exists, the Agent uses the Workflow Run input for its initial invocation. A later bounded-loop traversal supplies its committed source output as the next context value. Context accepts arbitrary JSON-compatible values. Several conditional branches may converge on one `context` port because only the matching edge delivers a token. Merging two tokens into a single invocation is a distinct capability: port-level joining and concurrent branch scheduling require separate architecture decisions, and a single-value port that receives two tokens runs twice instead.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:409:Pending actions have a stable type, status, credential-safe display payload, expiry, and optional external-operation reference. The first action types are `wechat_login` and `wechat_publish_confirmation`. QR images and expiry metadata may be returned to the browser, but authenticated browser state, cookies, tokens, and private platform responses never are. An expired QR action remains recoverable: refreshing it replaces the display payload without rerunning successful predecessor nodes or creating a duplicate external draft.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:411:The built-in `wechat-official-account` Plugin owns WeChat Official Account connection state, Playwright browser contexts, session health checks, and publication records. It is separate from the `codex-cli-chat` iLink message transport. Version 1 remains immutable and accepts a Markdown `article` input plus optional publication `metadata`. Version 2 accepts required Markdown `article` and Workflow image `coverImage` inputs plus optional publication `metadata`, references one configured official account, and returns a publication reference. Version 2 waits for a generated PNG cover, uploads it through the real MP cover picker, and creates no Artifact. A Workflow may fan out the same Agent output to an Artifact node and the publication node. Existing version-1 published graphs retain their original node behavior; newly created editor and seed nodes use version 2.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:413:WeChat administration uses a dedicated Playwright session owned by the deployment profile. Authentication state is stored through the server secret-storage boundary and is never returned to Web. Browser automation uses the real `mp.weixin.qq.com` user interface for login, article editing, media upload, draft creation, publish initiation, and confirmation. Undocumented private HTTP request shapes are not a WorkLite contract. The API serializes operations per official account and uses the Workflow Run plus node identifier as the publication idempotency key. A resumed or retried node reopens its existing draft or returns its existing published result rather than creating or sending another article. A publication record that already holds a platform draft identifier therefore reopens that draft even when its own status is `failed`, so retrying a node that failed after the draft was saved cannot leave a second draft in the official account.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:635:Workflows support a versioned portable JSON envelope for moving editable definitions between WorkLite workspaces. Export reads the current draft and emits `format: "worklite.workflow"`, `version: 1`, the workflow name, and its graph definition. Database identifiers, workspace identifiers, run history, schedules, credentials, and secrets are excluded. Workflow Agent public model ids and system prompts remain embedded. Skill and MCP server identifiers in Agent node configuration are replaced by workspace-portable references using resource names. Import resolves those names in the current workspace, rejects missing references, creates a draft, and never publishes or enables schedules.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:674:- Excluded this protocol from Agent model selection, since an Agent node's system prompt and output format have no meaning in a contract with no message list. Its connection test sends one minimal typed question, and its model catalog is manual because the upstream publishes no model-discovery endpoint.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:696:### 2026-09-21 - Author-Controlled Edge Cardinality and Branched Research Article Kinds
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:700:- Branched the research workflow on a planner-declared article kind, giving survey and explanatory articles their own retrieval and writing nodes that reconverge on the shared review, approval, artifact, cover, and WeChat publication path instead of duplicating the whole chain.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:703:### 2026-09-21 - Fail-Closed Research Article Review
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:706:- Added optional bounded Workflow Agent tool calls and rounds and a deterministic approved-article gate that rejects unapproved, duplicate, or structurally malformed Markdown before Article Artifact and WeChat draft creation.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:707:- Limited research revisions to one, removed the model-based article finalizer and publication after exhausted feedback, and left historical immutable versions and existing drafts untouched. New behavior requires a new published Workflow version and updated runtime.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:716:- Added publication validation requiring `outputFormat: "json"` alongside `outputContract` and a well-formed key list. Per the compatibility policy there is no migration or adapter: a node that declares no contract behaves exactly as before, and existing published versions and historical runs are unaffected.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:783:### 2026-09-19 - GitHub Evidence Depth for Article Substance
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:785:- Identified the cause of empty article content: the `github-current-popularity` Skill queried only `search/repositories`, so every claim about a project could rest on nothing deeper than its one-line description. No prompt or model change can supply material the research step never retrieved.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:787:- Recorded in the Skill instructions and the research prompt that a repository description is a self-applied label, not evidence for mechanism, change, or user agreement, and required each article paragraph to trace to README, commit, release, or discussion evidence.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:788:- Ranked article substance above the stylistic rules in reviewer approval, so a draft assembled from descriptions and star counts is rejected however well it reads, and required at least one concretely falsifiable mechanism passage and one real disagreement drawn from project discussion.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:794:### 2026-09-18 - Per-Role Research Workflow Models and Reader-Facing Article Quality
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:798:- Made reader-facing writing quality an explicit reviewer approval requirement alongside publication formatting: a concrete, claim-bearing title with no formulaic decoration, an opening that states a finding instead of background, no self-referential narration, no section headings that mirror the research JSON fields, bounded section count, varied sentence and paragraph length, interpreted rather than enumerated data, and a references section limited to sources the body actually uses.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:799:- Kept structured evidence, counterexamples, and limitations in the Research Notes Artifact while forbidding their reproduction in the article as mirrored sections, so evidence rigor is unchanged and only its presentation is constrained.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:801:- Restored the reviewer-to-finalizer edge to a `fallback` condition. A bounded feedback edge plus a `$.approved === true` predicate strands the Run with no article once the traversal bound is exhausted, because the scheduler traverses a fallback edge only when no predicate edge matches.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:803:### 2026-09-18 - Failed Node Retry and WeChat Draft Failure Reasons
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:808:- Made a WeChat publication record with an existing platform draft identifier reopen that draft even while its own status is `failed`, so a retry cannot create a second official-account draft.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:810:- Required draft-save responses to be classified as accepted or rejected before any failure text is derived, since a WeChat success response carries both a zero status code and an `ok` message.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:821:### 2026-09-17 - Workflow Image Generation and WeChat AI Covers
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:824:- Added `wechat-official-account/publish@2` with required article and generated-cover inputs while preserving immutable version-1 execution for previously published graphs.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:825:- Kept generated base64 image data out of NodeRun records, event payloads, terminal Run results, Run detail views, and WeChat publication records while retaining it in persisted scheduler state only long enough for downstream execution and resume.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:826:- Updated newly created editor and seed WeChat nodes to use version 2 and upload the generated PNG through the real Playwright MP cover picker.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:827:- Deferred image edits, generic provider abstraction, binary Artifacts, image libraries, image conversion, direct WeChat APIs, no-cover fallback, and dynamic joins.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:848:- Updated the repeatable research seed with up to three bounded editorial feedback traversals, constrained article finalization, reference-only article links, and WeChat draft saving.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:869:- Added the built-in WeChat Official Account Plugin and its Playwright-backed publish node, including login and final-publish QR confirmation.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:884:- Kept research notes and the final article as separate successful-Run Artifacts instead of adding filesystem output behavior.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:928:### 2026-09-14 - Generic Board Output Format
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:930:- Defined the version 1 Dashboard board format: configured display fields plus a `titleField`, with object or object-array Dashboard output rendered generically as cards.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:932:- Kept rendering tolerant; output that does not match the format degrades to explicit empty or raw-JSON states instead of failing the node or board.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:936:- Added `worklite/agent` output-format configuration for text or JSON responses.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:1060:- Existing Codex records written by the earlier encrypted format are not migrated; those installations must complete OAuth login again after upgrading.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:1189:### 2026-08-30 - WeChat ClawBot transport

    ui-ux-design/pages/home/DESIGN.md:133:Board cards are `article` elements. The decorative Dashboard icon is `aria-hidden`. Board tables use `th scope="col"` headers. A row with a resolvable URL keeps its title cell as a real anchor so keyboard users reach the link without depending on the row click, and the anchor stops propagation so the row handler does not double-open it. Pagination is a `nav` labelled by the current page indicator, and its icon-only controls carry accessible names.
    ui-ux-design/pages/home/DESIGN.md:172:- Adopted the compositional Dashboard layout format and removed the Dashboard description.
    ui-ux-design/pages/logs/DESIGN.md:63:Captured bodies are untrusted recorded content. They render as plain preformatted text inside a height-bounded scroll container, never as markup and never as an executed or fetched resource. Each body offers `Copy`, which reports on the control that was activated. Long bodies stay bounded by that container rather than extending the page.
    ui-ux-design/pages/model-providers/DESIGN.md:48:`typesafe/systemone` is a credential-forwarding protocol whose upstream exchanges a state value and typed questions for typed answers. Its `Fetch models` control stays disabled because the upstream publishes no model-discovery endpoint, so its catalog is entered by hand. Its connection test sends one minimal typed question rather than the fixed chat prompt. Providers using it are omitted from Agent model selection, since an Agent node's system prompt and output format have no meaning in that contract.
    ui-ux-design/pages/model-providers/DESIGN.md:248:- Required captured bodies to render as plain preformatted text inside height-bounded scroll containers, never as markup, because a recorded body is untrusted content.
    ui-ux-design/pages/model-providers/DESIGN.md:318:- Changed the page structure to show Gateway information above the Model Provider list instead of switching between local views.
    ui-ux-design/pages/workflows/editor/DESIGN.md:33:The palette includes Timer, Workflow Input, Agent, Choice Branch, TypeSafe System One, TypeSafe System One Map, Dashboard, Artifact, Artifact Query, Image, and the trusted WeChat Official Account Publish node when its built-in Plugin is available.
    ui-ux-design/pages/workflows/editor/DESIGN.md:38:- **Agent** owns its immutable embedded configuration and has one optional `context` input plus one output. When `context` has no explicit Workflow Input edge and no unbounded incoming edge, the initial Agent invocation uses the Workflow Run input, while later bounded-loop traversals supply the next context value. Its inspector selects `Text` or `JSON` output format.
    ui-ux-design/pages/workflows/editor/DESIGN.md:40:- **TypeSafe System One** has one required JSON `state` input and one JSON `output` port. Its inspector selects a configured TypeSafe public model and edits the immutable typed `questions` object. The node forwards the upstream System One response, including `answers`, without chat or Agent adaptation, while retaining object state fields for downstream context; outgoing predicates may address paths such as `$.answers.articleType.choice`.
    ui-ux-design/pages/workflows/editor/DESIGN.md:45:- **WeChat Official Account Publish** accepts required Markdown `article` and generated cover-image inputs plus optional JSON `metadata`, and outputs a publication reference.
    ui-ux-design/pages/workflows/editor/DESIGN.md:75:**Publish.** Opens a confirmation explaining that publishing locks the embedded Agent configuration and that later draft edits do not change this Workflow or its historical runs. Publication validates bounded-cycle constraints, port rules, public model ids, TypeSafe questions, image generation settings, required WeChat cover connectivity, and selected Skill and MCP availability. Validation failures navigate directly to the affected content.
    ui-ux-design/pages/workflows/editor/DESIGN.md:77:**Export JSON.** Downloads the current draft in the portable WorkLite format. Unsaved new Workflows must be saved first. The action stays neutral in both themes and does not compete with save, run, or publish.
    ui-ux-design/pages/workflows/editor/DESIGN.md:87:**Agent** nodes are created without selecting a standalone Agent. Their inspector directly exposes a public model selector, system prompt, Skill multi-selection, MCP server multi-selection, output format, and error policy. Skill and MCP choices come only from real workspace resources.
    ui-ux-design/pages/workflows/editor/DESIGN.md:89:**Choice Branch** nodes expose no provider-specific configuration. Their inspector explains that the JSON value is passed through and that outgoing conditions are evaluated in connection order, with only the first match or first fallback traversed. Use the edge inspector to configure JSON paths such as `$.articleType` and their comparison values.
    ui-ux-design/pages/workflows/editor/DESIGN.md:101:**WeChat Official Account Publish** inspectors select the configured official account and `Save draft` or `Publish` mode. The required cover input is reserved for a Workflow Image output; the inspector explains that the generated PNG is uploaded through the real MP cover picker and never offers a placeholder fallback. Metadata may provide a title override, author, and digest; otherwise the node reads the first Markdown heading as the title. The inspector explains that Publish may pause the Run for login or final confirmation. Workflows containing both an enabled Timer and a Publish-mode WeChat node are invalid in the initial increment.

    ui-ux-design/pages/plugins/configuration/DESIGN.md:34:For `codex-cli-chat`, a WeChat ClawBot connection section converts the server-reported QR payload URL into a local QR image and keeps the raw URL as an accessible fallback link. The browser never receives or edits the bot token.
    ui-ux-design/pages/plugins/configuration/DESIGN.md:36:The built-in `wechat-official-account` Plugin uses the same focused surface for one official-account connection. It shows the credential-safe account label, connection health, and last verification time. Login runs in a server-owned Playwright browser context and the page renders only the returned QR image. Cookies, browser storage, platform tokens, and private responses never reach Web.

    ui-ux-design/pages/plugins/configuration/DESIGN.md:127:  The ClawBot connection reports no expiry in `WechatConnectionView`, so its staleness is not observable and it is replaced only by starting login again.     ui-ux-design/pages/plugins/configuration/DESIGN.md:128:- `wechatPending` is one flag shared by all four connection mutations across both sections, so starting an Official Account login also disables the ClawBot controls. Busy state must be per-control.

A Workflow Agent node is embedded and self-contained; its optional \`outputFormat\` selects \`text\` (default) or \`json\`, and JSON mode requires valid parseable final output. A JSON-mode node may also declare \`outputContract\`, a non-empty array of unique top-level key names its parsed object must carry; a parsed value that is not an object, or that omits a named key or carries it as \`null\`, an empty string, or an empty array, fails the node and names the missing keys. Run status can also be \`paused\`: \`POST /runs/:runId/pause\` accepts queued or running, \`POST /runs/:runId/resume\` accepts only paused, and resume reruns the active invocation without checkpointing it.

    import { BadRequestException, Inject, Injectable, Logger, NotFoundException } from '@nestjs/common';
    import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
    import { rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
    import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
    import { join } from 'node:path';
    import { Lexer, type Token, type Tokens } from 'marked';
    import { and, eq, ne } from 'drizzle-orm';
    import { chromium, type Browser, type BrowserContext, type Locator, type Page, type Response } from 'playwright';
    import type { NodeExecutionRequest, NodeExecutionResult, PendingNodeExecutionResult } from '@worklite/workflow-engine';
    import { wechatOfficialAccounts, wechatPublications, workflowPendingActions, type Database } from '@worklite/db';
    import type { WechatOfficialAccountView } from '@worklite/contracts';
    import { DATABASE } from '../../infrastructure/database.module';
    import { decryptSecret, encryptSecret, WECHAT_OFFICIAL_ACCOUNT_ID } from './plugins.service';
    
    type ActionListener = (actionId: string) => void;
    type BrowserSession = { browser: Browser; context: BrowserContext; page: Page };
    
    const LOGIN_URL = 'https://mp.weixin.qq.com/';
    const QR_LIFETIME_MS = 120_000;
    
    @Injectable()
    export class WechatOfficialAccountService {
      private readonly logger = new Logger(WechatOfficialAccountService.name);
      private readonly listeners = new Set<ActionListener>();
      private readonly sessions = new Map<string, BrowserSession>();
      private activeActionId: string | null = null;
    
      constructor(@Inject(DATABASE) private readonly db: Database) {}
    
      subscribe(listener: ActionListener): () => void {
        this.listeners.add(listener);
        return () => this.listeners.delete(listener);
      }
    
      async execute(request: NodeExecutionRequest, version: '1' | '2'): Promise<NodeExecutionResult> {
        const config = asRecord(request.config);
        const input = asRecord(request.input);
        const accountId = typeof config?.accountId === 'string' ? config.accountId : '';
        const mode = config?.mode;
        const article = typeof input?.article === 'string' ? input.article : '';
        const metadata = asRecord(input?.metadata) ?? {};
        if (!accountId || (mode !== 'draft' && mode !== 'publish')) throw new Error('WeChat Official Account node requires an account and mode.');
        if (!article.trim()) throw new Error('WeChat Official Account node requires Markdown article input.');
        const coverImage = version === '2' ? validateGeneratedCover(input?.coverImage) : null;
        const account = await this.getAccountRow(accountId);
        const idempotencyKey = `${request.context.workflowRunId}:${request.context.nodeRunId}`;
        const publication = await this.ensurePublication(request, accountId, mode, article, metadata, idempotencyKey);
        if (publication.status === 'published' || (mode === 'draft' && publication.status === 'draft_saved')) return { output: toPublicationOutput(publication) };
    
        if (!account.encryptedStorageState) {
          const pending = await this.startLogin(request.context.pendingActionId, account.id, true);
          return { status: 'waiting_for_input', pendingAction: pending };
        }
    
        if (publication.draftId) {
          if (mode === 'draft') {
            await this.db.update(wechatPublications).set({ status: 'draft_saved', lastError: null, updatedAt: new Date() }).where(eq(wechatPublications.id, publication.id));
            return { output: toPublicationOutput({ ...publication, status: 'draft_saved' }) };
          }
          return { status: 'waiting_for_input', pendingAction: await this.openDraftForConfirmation(request.context.pendingActionId, publication, account.encryptedStorageState) };
        }
    
        if (!coverImage) return this.compose(request.context.pendingActionId, publication, account.encryptedStorageState, request.signal);
        const coverPath = join(tmpdir(), `worklite-wechat-cover-${randomUUID()}.png`);
        await writeFile(coverPath, Buffer.from(coverImage.b64Json, 'base64'));
        try {
          return await this.compose(request.context.pendingActionId, publication, account.encryptedStorageState, request.signal, coverPath);
        } finally {
          await rm(coverPath, { force: true }).catch(() => undefined);
        }
      }
    
      async refresh(actionId: string): Promise<PendingNodeExecutionResult['pendingAction']> {
        const [action] = await this.db.select().from(workflowPendingActions).where(eq(workflowPendingActions.id, actionId)).limit(1);
        if (!action) throw new NotFoundException('Pending action not found.');
        await this.closeSession(actionId);
        if (action.type === 'wechat_login') {
          const [publication] = await this.db.select().from(wechatPublications).where(eq(wechatPublications.nodeRunId, action.nodeRunId)).limit(1);
          if (!publication) throw new NotFoundException('WeChat publication not found.');
          return this.startLogin(actionId, publication.accountId, true);
        }
        const [publication] = await this.db.select().from(wechatPublications).where(eq(wechatPublications.nodeRunId, action.nodeRunId)).limit(1);
        if (!publication?.draftId) throw new BadRequestException('The WeChat draft is not available.');
        const account = await this.getAccountRow(publication.accountId);
        if (!account.encryptedStorageState) return this.startLogin(actionId, account.id, true);
        return this.openDraftForConfirmation(actionId, publication, account.encryptedStorageState);
      }
    
      async startAccountLogin(): Promise<WechatOfficialAccountView> {
        const actionId = `wechat_login_${randomUUID()}`;
        await this.startLogin(actionId, WECHAT_OFFICIAL_ACCOUNT_ID);
        return this.getAccount();
      }
    
      async disconnect(): Promise<WechatOfficialAccountView> {
        if (this.activeActionId) await this.closeSession(this.activeActionId);
        await this.db.update(wechatOfficialAccounts).set({ status: 'disconnected', encryptedStorageState: null, qrCode: null, qrExpiresAt: null, lastError: null, updatedAt: new Date() }).where(eq(wechatOfficialAccounts.id, WECHAT_OFFICIAL_ACCOUNT_ID));
        return this.getAccount();
      }
    
      async getAccount(): Promise<WechatOfficialAccountView> {
        const account = await this.getAccountRow(WECHAT_OFFICIAL_ACCOUNT_ID);
        return {
          id: account.id,
          displayName: account.displayName,
          status: account.status,
          qrCode: account.qrCode,
          qrExpiresAt: account.qrExpiresAt?.toISOString() ?? null,
          lastVerifiedAt: account.lastVerifiedAt?.toISOString() ?? null,
          lastError: account.lastError,
          updatedAt: account.updatedAt.toISOString(),
        };
      }
    
      async cancel(actionId: string): Promise<void> {
        await this.closeSession(actionId);
      }
    
      private async startLogin(actionId: string, accountId: string, waitForPendingAction = false): Promise<PendingNodeExecutionResult['pendingAction']> {
        this.assertAccountAvailable(actionId);
        const session = await this.createSession();
        this.sessions.set(actionId, session);
        this.activeActionId = actionId;
        try {
          await session.page.goto(LOGIN_URL, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });
          await showScanLogin(session.page);
          const qrCode = await captureLoginQrCode(session.page);
          const expiresAt = new Date(Date.now() + QR_LIFETIME_MS);
          await this.db.update(wechatOfficialAccounts).set({ status: 'qr_pending', qrCode, qrExpiresAt: expiresAt, lastError: null, updatedAt: new Date() }).where(eq(wechatOfficialAccounts.id, accountId));
          void this.monitorLogin(actionId, accountId, session, expiresAt, waitForPendingAction);
          return { id: actionId, type: 'wechat_login', title: 'Scan to sign in to WeChat Official Account', description: 'Use the account administrator WeChat app to scan this QR code. The Workflow will resume automatically.', qrCode, expiresAt };
        } catch (error) {
          await this.failAccount(accountId, error);
          await this.closeSession(actionId);
          throw error;
        }
      }
    
      private async compose(actionId: string, publication: typeof wechatPublications.$inferSelect, encryptedStorageState: string, signal: AbortSignal, coverPath?: string): Promise<NodeExecutionResult> {
        this.assertAccountAvailable(actionId);
        const session = await this.createSession(encryptedStorageState);
        this.sessions.set(actionId, session);
        this.activeActionId = actionId;
        try {
          await session.page.goto(LOGIN_URL, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });
          if (isLoginPage(session.page)) {
            await this.closeSession(actionId);
            await this.db.update(wechatOfficialAccounts).set({ encryptedStorageState: null, status: 'disconnected', updatedAt: new Date() }).where(eq(wechatOfficialAccounts.id, publication.accountId));
            return { status: 'waiting_for_input', pendingAction: await this.startLogin(actionId, publication.accountId, true) };
          }
          const token = new URL(session.page.url()).searchParams.get('token');
          if (!token) throw new Error('WeChat Official Account session did not provide an editor token.');
          await session.page.goto(`https://mp.weixin.qq.com/cgi-bin/appmsg?t=media/appmsg_edit&action=edit&type=10&token=${encodeURIComponent(token)}&lang=en_US`, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });
          await fillArticle(session.page, publication.title, publication.article, coverPath);
          if (signal.aborted) throw new Error('Workflow run cancelled.');
          const draftId = await saveDraft(session.page);
          await this.db.update(wechatPublications).set({ status: 'draft_saved', draftId, lastError: null, updatedAt: new Date() }).where(eq(wechatPublications.id, publication.id));
          if (publication.mode === 'draft') {
            await this.closeSession(actionId);
            return { output: toPublicationOutput({ ...publication, status: 'draft_saved', draftId }) };
          }
          return { status: 'waiting_for_input', pendingAction: await this.beginPublishConfirmation(actionId, { ...publication, status: 'draft_saved', draftId }, session) };
        } catch (error) {
          await this.closeSession(actionId);
          await this.db.update(wechatPublications).set({ status: 'failed', lastError: errorMessage(error), updatedAt: new Date() }).where(eq(wechatPublications.id, publication.id));
          throw error;
        }
      }
    
      private async openDraftForConfirmation(actionId: string, publication: typeof wechatPublications.$inferSelect, encryptedStorageState: string): Promise<PendingNodeExecutionResult['pendingAction']> {
        this.assertAccountAvailable(actionId);
        const session = await this.createSession(encryptedStorageState);
        this.sessions.set(actionId, session);
        this.activeActionId = actionId;
        try {
          await session.page.goto(LOGIN_URL, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });
          const token = new URL(session.page.url()).searchParams.get('token');
          if (!token) throw new Error('WeChat Official Account session expired. Sign in again.');
          await session.page.goto(`https://mp.weixin.qq.com/cgi-bin/appmsg?t=media/appmsg_edit&action=edit&type=10&appmsgid=${encodeURIComponent(publication.draftId ?? '')}&token=${encodeURIComponent(token)}&lang=en_US`, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });
          return this.beginPublishConfirmation(actionId, publication, session);
        } catch (error) {
          await this.closeSession(actionId);
          throw error;
        }
      }
    
      private async beginPublishConfirmation(actionId: string, publication: typeof wechatPublications.$inferSelect, session: BrowserSession): Promise<PendingNodeExecutionResult['pendingAction']> {
        await clickByText(session.page, ['Publish', '\u53d1\u8868', '\u7fa4\u53d1']);
        await session.page.waitForFunction(
          `Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.weui-desktop-dialog')).some((dialog) => dialog.getBoundingClientRect().width > 100 && /Publish|\u53d1\u8868|\u7fa4\u53d1\u901a\u77e5|\u5b9a\u65f6\u53d1\u8868/.test(dialog.textContent ?? ''))`,
          undefined,
          { timeout: 10_000 },
        );
        const clickedDialogPublishButton = await session.page.evaluate<boolean>(`(() => {
          for (const dialog of document.querySelectorAll('.weui-desktop-dialog')) {
            if (dialog.getBoundingClientRect().width < 100) continue;
            for (const button of dialog.querySelectorAll('button')) {
              if (/^(Publish|\u53d1\u8868|\u53d1\u5e03)$/.test(button.textContent?.trim() ?? '') && !button.hasAttribute('disabled')) {
                button.click();
                return true;
              }
            }
          }
          return false;
        })()`);
        if (!clickedDialogPublishButton) {
          await session.page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/worklite-publish-dialog-button-timeout.png', fullPage: true });
          throw new Error('WeChat publish dialog confirmation is unavailable.');
        }
        await delay(2_000);
        const qrCode = await captureQrCode(session.page);
        const expiresAt = new Date(Date.now() + QR_LIFETIME_MS);
        await this.db.update(wechatPublications).set({ status: 'confirmation_pending', updatedAt: new Date() }).where(and(eq(wechatPublications.id, publication.id), ne(wechatPublications.status, 'published')));
        void this.monitorPublish(actionId, publication.id, session, expiresAt);
        return { id: actionId, type: 'wechat_publish_confirmation', title: 'Confirm WeChat publication', description: 'Scan with the account administrator WeChat app to confirm publication. The Workflow will resume automatically.', qrCode, expiresAt };
      }
    
      private async monitorLogin(actionId: string, accountId: string, session: BrowserSession, expiresAt: Date, waitForPendingAction: boolean): Promise<void> {
        let lastQrSource = await loginQrCode(session.page).getAttribute('src', { timeout: 1_000 }).catch(() => null);
        let lastDiagnostics = '';
        while (this.sessions.get(actionId) === session) {
          await delay(1_000);
          if (Date.now() >= expiresAt.getTime()) break;
          if (waitForPendingAction) {
            const actionStatus = await this.getPendingActionStatus(actionId);
            if (!actionStatus || actionStatus === 'expired') continue;
            if (actionStatus !== 'pending') return;
          }
          if (await isLoginConfirmed(session.context)) {
            const storageState = await session.context.storageState();
            await this.db.update(wechatOfficialAccounts).set({ status: 'connected', encryptedStorageState: encryptSecret(JSON.stringify(storageState)), qrCode: null, qrExpiresAt: null, lastVerifiedAt: new Date(), lastError: null, updatedAt: new Date() }).where(eq(wechatOfficialAccounts.id, accountId));
            await this.closeSession(actionId);
            this.complete(actionId);
            return;
          }
          const diagnostics = await loginDiagnostics(session);
          if (diagnostics !== lastDiagnostics) {
            lastDiagnostics = diagnostics;
            this.logger.debug(`WeChat login ${actionId}: ${diagnostics}`);
          }
          const currentQrSource = await loginQrCode(session.page).getAttribute('src', { timeout: 1_000 }).catch(() => null);
          if (currentQrSource && currentQrSource !== lastQrSource) {
            lastQrSource = currentQrSource;
            const refreshedQrCode = await captureLoginQrCode(session.page).catch(() => null);
            if (refreshedQrCode) {
              await this.db.update(wechatOfficialAccounts).set({ qrCode: refreshedQrCode, updatedAt: new Date() }).where(eq(wechatOfficialAccounts.id, accountId));
              await this.db.update(workflowPendingActions).set({ qrCode: refreshedQrCode, updatedAt: new Date() }).where(and(eq(workflowPendingActions.id, actionId), eq(workflowPendingActions.status, 'pending')));
            }
          }
        }
        if (this.sessions.get(actionId) === session) await this.expire(actionId, accountId);
      }

    function markdownToHtml(markdown: string): string {

      const context = createCitationContext(parseReferenceEntries(referencesMarkdown));

      const referencesHeading = containsChinese(markdown) ? '相关链接' : referenceHeading ?? generatedReferenceHeading(markdown);
      const referencesHtml = context.entries.length > 0 ? renderReferences(referencesHeading, context.entries) : '';
      return `<section style="${ARTICLE_ROOT_STYLE}">${articleHtml}${referencesHtml}</section>`;
    }
    
    function generatedReferenceHeading(markdown: string): string {
      return containsChinese(markdown) ? '相关链接' : 'Related Links';
    }
    
    function containsChinese(value: string): boolean {
      return /[一-鿿]/.test(value);
    }
    
    function splitReferences(markdown: string): { articleMarkdown: string; referenceHeading: string | null; referencesMarkdown: string } {
      const pattern = /\n?#{1,6}\s*(References|Reference List|Sources|Related Links|参考资料|引用资料|参考链接|相关链接)\s*(?=\n|$)/gi;
      let match: RegExpExecArray | null;
      let last: RegExpExecArray | null = null;
      while ((match = pattern.exec(markdown)) !== null) last = match;
      if (!last) return { articleMarkdown: markdown, referenceHeading: null, referencesMarkdown: '' };
      const headingStart = last.index + (last[0].startsWith('\n') ? 1 : 0);
      return {
        articleMarkdown: markdown.slice(0, headingStart),
        referenceHeading: last[1].trim(),
        referencesMarkdown: markdown.slice(last.index + last[0].length),
      };
    }
    
    function parseReferenceEntries(markdown: string): ReferenceEntry[] {
      const entries: ReferenceEntry[] = [];
      for (const originalLine of markdown.split(/\r?\n/)) {
        const line = originalLine.trim();
        if (!line) continue;
        const explicitNumber = Number(line.match(/^\[?(\d+)[.)\]]\s*/)?.[1] ?? null);
        const linkedSources = [...line.matchAll(/\[([^\]]*)\]\((https?:\/\/[^\s)]+)\)/g)];
        if (linkedSources.length > 0) {
          linkedSources.forEach((source, index) => {
            entries.push({ number: index === 0 ? explicitNumber : null, label: cleanReferenceLabel(source[1]), url: source[2] });
          });
          continue;
        }
        const urls = extractUrls(line);
        if (urls.length > 0) {
          urls.forEach((url, index) => {
            entries.push({ number: index === 0 ? explicitNumber : null, label: cleanReferenceLabel(line, url), url });

          continue;
        }
        entries.push({ number: explicitNumber, label: cleanReferenceLabel(line), url: null });

      return deduplicateReferences(entries);
    }
    
    function extractUrls(value: string): string[] {

        let url = match[0];

    function deduplicateReferences(entries: ReferenceEntry[]): ReferenceEntry[] {
      const seen = new Set<string>();
      const result: ReferenceEntry[] = [];
      for (const entry of entries) {
        const key = entry.url ?? entry.label.toLowerCase();
        if (seen.has(key)) continue;
        seen.add(key);

      return result;

    function cleanReferenceLabel(value: string, url?: string): string {

    function renderTokens(tokens: Token[], context: CitationContext): string {

    function renderBlockToken(token: Token, context: CitationContext): string {

        case 'hr':

        case 'em':

        case 'del':

        case 'br':

        }
        case 'image':

      const label = !plainText || token.autolink === true || plainText === url ? referenceSourceLabel(url) : plainText;
      citationNumberFor(url, label, context);

    function renderTextWithCitations(value: string, context: CitationContext): string {

    function plainInlineTokens(tokens: Token[]): string {
      return tokens.map((token) => {

          case 'em':

          case 'codespan':

    function validateGeneratedCover(value: unknown): { b64Json: string } | null {
      if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) throw new Error('WeChat Official Account v2 requires a generated cover image.');
      const cover = value as Record<string, unknown>;
      if (cover.type !== 'workflow_image' || cover.mediaType !== 'image/png' || !Array.isArray(cover.data) || cover.data.length === 0) throw new Error('WeChat Official Account v2 requires a generated PNG cover image.');
      const first = cover.data[0];
      if (!first || typeof first !== 'object' || Array.isArray(first) || typeof (first as Record<string, unknown>).b64Json !== 'string' || !(first as Record<string, unknown>).b64Json) throw new Error('WeChat Official Account v2 requires generated PNG image data.');

    }
    
    
    function extractTitle(article: string): string {
      const heading = article.match(/^#\s+(.+)$/m)?.[1]?.trim();
      if (heading) return heading;
      const firstLine = article.trim().split('\n')[0]?.trim();
      return firstLine ? firstLine.replace(/^#{1,6}\s+/, '').slice(0, 64) : 'Untitled article';

    function findString(value: unknown, keys: string[]): string | null {
      if (!value || typeof value !== 'object') return null;
      for (const [key, child] of Object.entries(value)) {
        if (keys.includes(key) && (typeof child === 'string' || typeof child === 'number')) return String(child);
        const nested = findString(child, keys);
        if (nested) return nested;
      }
      return null;
    }

    async function clickActionElement(page: Page, label: string): Promise<boolean> {
      return page.evaluate<boolean>(`(() => {
        const wanted = ${JSON.stringify(label)}.replace(/\\s+/g, '');
        const candidates = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('button, a, [role="button"], .weui-desktop-btn, .js_save, #js_submit'));
        const matches = candidates.filter((element) => {
          const rect = element.getBoundingClientRect();
          if (rect.width <= 0 || rect.height <= 0) return false;
          if (element.hasAttribute('disabled') || element.classList.contains('weui-desktop-btn_disabled')) return false;
          return (element.textContent ?? '').replace(/\\s+/g, '') === wanted;
        });
        const target = matches[matches.length - 1];

        target.scrollIntoView({ block: 'center' });
        target.click();

The runtime carries the writer's article, title, topic, thesis, evidenceUsed, and candidates unchanged into the reviewer result. One rejection can return to the writer for one revision; a second rejection reaches the deterministic article gate and fails the Run without creating the final Article Artifact or WeChat draft.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:342:The `worklite/approved-article@1` node accepts the reviewer JSON at a required `context` port, requires an explicit true approval and false duplicate, and returns the original Markdown article only when its Markdown headings and fenced code blocks are structurally sound. It never repairs corrupted text or infers an approval. A failed gate uses the ordinary failed-node retry path. Research Notes Artifacts remain separate; the approved Markdown article fans out to the Article Artifact, cover-prompt Agent and WeChat v2 draft node. The cover prompt drives `worklite/image@1`; the generated PNG is passed to the draft node. Published Workflow versions remain immutable: existing versions and historical Runs are not rewritten, and the new seed requires an updated runtime and a newly published Workflow version before it takes effect. No compatibility node or migration is added.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:411:The built-in `wechat-official-account` Plugin owns WeChat Official Account connection state, Playwright browser contexts, session health checks, and publication records. It is separate from the `codex-cli-chat` iLink message transport. Version 1 remains immutable and accepts a Markdown `article` input plus optional publication `metadata`. Version 2 accepts required Markdown `article` and Workflow image `coverImage` inputs plus optional publication `metadata`, references one configured official account, and returns a publication reference. Version 2 waits for a generated PNG cover, uploads it through the real MP cover picker, and creates no Artifact. A Workflow may fan out the same Agent output to an Artifact node and the publication node. Existing version-1 published graphs retain their original node behavior; newly created editor and seed nodes use version 2.
    docs/project-architecture/README.md:413:WeChat administration uses a dedicated Playwright session owned by the deployment profile. Authentication state is stored through the server secret-storage boundary and is never returned to Web. Browser automation uses the real `mp.weixin.qq.com` user interface for login, article editing, media upload, draft creation, publish initiation, and confirmation. Undocumented private HTTP request shapes are not a WorkLite contract. The API serializes operations per official account and uses the Workflow Run plus node identifier as the publication idempotency key. A resumed or retried node reopens its existing draft or returns its existing published result rather than creating or sending another article. A publication record that already holds a platform draft identifier therefore reopens that draft even when its own status is `failed`, so retrying a node that failed after the draft was saved cannot leave a second draft in the official account.

    async function fillArticle(page: Page, title: string, article: string, coverPath?: string): Promise<void> {
      const titleEditor = page.locator('.ProseMirror').first();
      await titleEditor.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 20_000 });
      await titleEditor.click();
      await titleEditor.fill(title.slice(0, 64));
    
      const bodyEditor = page.locator('.ProseMirror').nth(1);
      await bodyEditor.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 20_000 });
      await bodyEditor.click();
      const html = markdownToHtml(article.replace(/^#\s+.+$/m, '').trim() || article);
      await bodyEditor.evaluate((element, value) => {
        const view = element.ownerDocument.defaultView;
        if (!view) throw new Error('Missing editor window.');
        const data = new view.DataTransfer();
        data.setData('text/html', value);
        const paste = new view.ClipboardEvent('paste', { bubbles: true, cancelable: true });
        Object.defineProperty(paste, 'clipboardData', { value: data });
        element.dispatchEvent(paste);
      }, html);
      // Version 1 nodes have no cover input. Leave the cover unset rather than
      // uploading a substitute image the author never asked for.
      if (coverPath) await setCoverImage(page, coverPath);
    }

      async list(request: Request, workspaceSlug: string): Promise<WorkflowView[]> {
        const workspace = await this.workspaces.getWorkspace(request, workspaceSlug);
        const rows = await this.db.select().from(workflows).where(eq(workflows.workspaceId, workspace.id));
        return Promise.all(rows.map((row) => this.toView(row, workspaceSlug)));
      }
    
      async get(request: Request, workspaceSlug: string, workflowId: string): Promise<WorkflowDetailView> {
        const workspace = await this.workspaces.getWorkspace(request, workspaceSlug);
        const row = await this.findWorkflow(workspace.id, workflowId);
        if (!row) throw new NotFoundException('Workflow not found');
        await this.ensureDraft(row);
        return this.toDetail(row, workspaceSlug);
      }
    
      async create(request: Request, workspaceSlug: string, input: CreateWorkflowRequest): Promise<WorkflowDetailView> {
        const workspace = await this.workspaces.getWorkspace(request, workspaceSlug);
        const name = input.name?.trim();
        if (!name) throw new BadRequestException('Workflow name is required.');
        const workflowId = `wf_${randomUUID()}`;
        const draftId = `wfd_${randomUUID()}`;
        const revisionId = `wfr_${randomUUID()}`;
        const definition = normalizeDefinition(input.definition ?? emptyWorkflowDefinition);
        validateDefinition(definition, false);
        await this.validateWorkspaceReferences(workspace.id, definition);
        await this.db.transaction((transaction) => {
          transaction.insert(workflows).values({ id: workflowId, workspaceId: workspace.id, name, state: 'draft' }).run();
          transaction.insert(workflowDrafts).values({ id: draftId, workspaceId: workspace.id, workflowId, currentRevisionId: revisionId, definition }).run();
          transaction.insert(workflowEditRevisions).values({ id: revisionId, workspaceId: workspace.id, workflowId, draftId, parentRevisionId: null, source: 'manual', operations: [], snapshot: definition }).run();
        });
        return this.get(request, workspaceSlug, workflowId);
      }
    
      async exportWorkflow(request: Request, workspaceSlug: string, workflowId: string): Promise<PortableWorkflowDocument> {
        const workspace = await this.workspaces.getWorkspace(request, workspaceSlug);
        const workflow = await this.findWorkflow(workspace.id, workflowId);
        if (!workflow) throw new NotFoundException('Workflow not found');
        await this.ensureDraft(workflow);
        const draft = await this.loadDraft(workspace.id, workflowId);
        if (!draft) throw new NotFoundException('Workflow draft not found');
        const skillIds = collectWorkflowResourceIds(draft.definition, 'skillIds');
        const mcpServerIds = collectWorkflowResourceIds(draft.definition, 'mcpServerIds');
        const [skillRows, mcpRows] = await Promise.all([
          skillIds.length === 0 ? [] : this.db.select({ id: skills.id, name: skills.name }).from(skills).where(and(eq(skills.workspaceId, workspace.id), inArray(skills.id, skillIds))),
          mcpServerIds.length === 0 ? [] : this.db.select({ id: mcpServers.id, name: mcpServers.name }).from(mcpServers).where(and(eq(mcpServers.workspaceId, workspace.id), inArray(mcpServers.id, mcpServerIds))),
        ]);
        if (skillRows.length !== skillIds.length) throw new BadRequestException('Every Workflow Agent Skill must belong to this workspace before export.');
        if (mcpRows.length !== mcpServerIds.length) throw new BadRequestException('Every Workflow Agent MCP server must belong to this workspace before export.');
        const skillsById = new Map(skillRows.map((row) => [row.id, row.name]));
        const mcpById = new Map(mcpRows.map((row) => [row.id, row.name]));
        const definition = structuredClone(draft.definition) as WorkflowDefinition;
        definition.nodes = definition.nodes.map((node) => {
          const config = isRecord(node.config) ? { ...node.config } : {};
          if (node.type === 'worklite/agent') {
            config.skills = readStringArray(config.skillIds).map((id) => ({ name: skillsById.get(id)! }));
            config.mcpServers = readStringArray(config.mcpServerIds).map((id) => ({ name: mcpById.get(id)! }));
            delete config.skillIds;
            delete config.mcpServerIds;
          }
          return { ...node, config };
        });
        return { format: 'worklite.workflow', version: 1, workflow: { name: workflow.name, definition: definition as PortableWorkflowDocument['workflow']['definition'] } };
      }
    
      async importWorkflow(request: Request, workspaceSlug: string, input: ImportWorkflowRequest): Promise<WorkflowDetailView> {
        if (!isRecord(input) || input.format !== 'worklite.workflow' || input.version !== 1 || !isRecord(input.workflow)) throw new BadRequestException('WorkLite workflow JSON version 1 is required.');
        const name = typeof input.workflow.name === 'string' ? input.workflow.name.trim() : '';
        if (!name || !isRecord(input.workflow.definition)) throw new BadRequestException('The imported workflow name and definition are required.');
        const workspace = await this.workspaces.getWorkspace(request, workspaceSlug);
        const definition = normalizeDefinition(input.workflow.definition as unknown as WorkflowDefinition);
        for (const node of definition.nodes) {
          const config = isRecord(node.config) ? { ...node.config } : {};
          if (node.type === 'worklite/agent') {
            const skillNames = readPortableNames(config.skills, 'Skill');
            const mcpNames = readPortableNames(config.mcpServers, 'MCP server');
            const [skillRows, mcpRows] = await Promise.all([
              skillNames.length === 0 ? [] : this.db.select({ id: skills.id, name: skills.name }).from(skills).where(and(eq(skills.workspaceId, workspace.id), inArray(skills.name, skillNames))),
              mcpNames.length === 0 ? [] : this.db.select({ id: mcpServers.id, name: mcpServers.name }).from(mcpServers).where(and(eq(mcpServers.workspaceId, workspace.id), inArray(mcpServers.name, mcpNames))),
            ]);
            config.skillIds = resolvePortableNames(skillNames, skillRows, 'Skill');
            config.mcpServerIds = resolvePortableNames(mcpNames, mcpRows, 'MCP server');
            delete config.skills;
            delete config.mcpServers;
          }
          node.config = config;
        }
        validateDefinition(definition, false);
        return this.create(request, workspaceSlug, { name, definition });

        });

    import { Body, Controller, Get, Header, Headers, Param, Post, Req, Res } from '@nestjs/common';
    import type { Request, Response } from 'express';
    import type { CreateRunRequest, RunProgressEvent } from '@worklite/contracts';
    import { RunsService } from './runs.service';
    
    @Controller()
    export class RunsController {
      constructor(private readonly runs: RunsService) {}
    
      @Get('runs')
      list(@Req() request: Request) {
        return this.runs.list(request, 'personal');
      }
    
      @Get('runs/:runId')
      get(@Req() request: Request, @Param('runId') runId: string) {
        return this.runs.get(request, 'personal', runId);
      }
    
      @Get('runs/:runId/events')
      @Header('Cache-Control', 'no-cache, no-transform')
      async events(@Req() request: Request, @Param('runId') runId: string, @Headers('last-event-id') lastEventId: string | undefined, @Res() response: Response): Promise<void> {
        const afterSequence = parseLastEventId(lastEventId);
        await this.runs.get(request, 'personal', runId);
        response.status(200);
        response.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/event-stream');
        response.setHeader('Connection', 'keep-alive');
        response.setHeader('X-Accel-Buffering', 'no');
        response.flushHeaders();
        let lastSequence = afterSequence;
        let replaying = true;
        let closed = false;
        const pending: RunProgressEvent[] = [];
        const send = (event: RunProgressEvent) => {
          if (closed || event.runId !== runId || event.sequence <= lastSequence) return;
          lastSequence = event.sequence;
          response.write(`id: ${event.sequence}\ndata: ${JSON.stringify(event)}\n\n`);
        };
        const unsubscribe = this.runs.subscribe((event) => {
          if (event.runId !== runId) return;
          if (replaying) pending.push(event);
          else send(event);
        });
        const heartbeat = setInterval(() => response.write(': keep-alive\n\n'), 15_000);
        const cleanup = () => {
          if (closed) return;
          closed = true;
          clearInterval(heartbeat);
          unsubscribe();
        };
        request.once('close', cleanup);
        const replay = await this.runs.events(request, 'personal', runId, afterSequence);
        replay.forEach(send);
        replaying = false;
        pending.sort((left, right) => left.sequence - right.sequence).forEach(send);
        const latest = await this.runs.get(request, 'personal', runId);
        if (latest.status === 'succeeded' || latest.status === 'failed' || latest.status === 'cancelled' || latest.status === 'timed_out') {
          cleanup();
          response.end();
        }
      }

    function parseLastEventId(value: string | undefined): number {
      const parsed = Number(value ?? 0);
      return Number.isSafeInteger(parsed) && parsed > 0 ? parsed : 0;

      private async getPendingActionStatus(actionId: string): Promise<string | null> {

      private async expire(actionId: string, accountId?: string): Promise<void> {

        if (accountId) await this.db.update(wechatOfficialAccounts).set({ status: 'disconnected', qrCode: null, qrExpiresAt: null, updatedAt: new Date() }).where(eq(wechatOfficialAccounts.id, accountId));
        await this.db.update(workflowPendingActions).set({ status: 'expired', qrCode: null, updatedAt: new Date() }).where(and(eq(workflowPendingActions.id, actionId), eq(workflowPendingActions.status, 'pending')));
      }
    
      private async createSession(encryptedStorageState?: string): Promise<BrowserSession> {
        const browser = await chromium.launch({ headless: process.env.WECHAT_HEADED !== '1' });
        const context = await browser.newContext(encryptedStorageState ? { storageState: JSON.parse(decryptSecret(encryptedStorageState)) } : undefined);
        const page = await context.newPage();
        return { browser, context, page };
      }
    
      private assertAccountAvailable(actionId: string): void {

      private async closeSession(actionId: string): Promise<void> {
        const session = this.sessions.get(actionId);
        this.sessions.delete(actionId);
        if (this.activeActionId === actionId) this.activeActionId = null;
        await session?.browser.close().catch(() => undefined);
      }

    import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core';

    import { NestExpressApplication } from '@nestjs/platform-express';
    import { AppModule } from './app.module';
    
    async function bootstrap() {
      const port = Number(process.env.API_PORT ?? 3391);
      const host = process.env.API_HOST?.trim() || '127.0.0.1';
      process.env.WORKLITE_API_URL = `http://127.0.0.1:${port}/api`;
      process.env.WORKLITE_WORKSPACE_SLUG = 'personal';
      const app = await NestFactory.create<NestExpressApplication>(AppModule, { bodyParser: false });
      app.useBodyParser('json', { limit: Infinity });
      app.useBodyParser('urlencoded', { extended: true, limit: Infinity });
      app.setGlobalPrefix('api');
    
      await app.listen(port, host);
      Logger.log(`WorkLite API listening on http://${host}:${port}`, 'Bootstrap');
    }
    
    void bootstrap();
