Workflow Agent nodes own prompts and Skill/MCP selections; their \`context\` input is optional and may combine one unbounded initial upstream edge with one bounded feedback edge; a Workflow Input edge remains unconditional and unbounded. Artifact nodes own Artifact creation, and Agent and WeChat nodes never create Artifacts.
    
    The first-party \`worklite/branch@1\` Choice Branch node requires JSON on \`value\`, returns the unchanged value on \`output\`, and selects exactly one outgoing route: the first matching predicate in edge-definition order, or the first fallback when no predicate matches. It is reusable with any JSON-producing node and does not depend on a particular Provider protocol.
    
    The first-party \`typesafe/systemone-map@1\` node evaluates one typed question set against every element of an array inside its committed \`state\`. It stores \`model\`, \`questions\`, a required \`itemsPath\`, an optional \`contextPath\`, an optional positive \`concurrency\`, and an optional \`rank\` of \`path\`, \`order\`, \`limit\`, and \`minimum\` in the Workflow version. Each element becomes one upstream request whose state is \`{ item, context }\`, so an element carries only its own content plus the addressed shared context. The node preserves input order, commits \`results\` as the elements with their typed \`answers\` merged in, exposes a non-object element under \`item\`, and retains object state fields beside \`results\` and \`usage\`. A configured \`rank\` orders and truncates deterministically after evaluation and drops an element whose answer path holds no number when \`minimum\` is set. A failed element fails the node under its error policy, so a partially evaluated array is never committed.
    
    The first-party \`typesafe/systemone@1\` node requires JSON on \`state\`, stores \`model\` and \`questions\` in the Workflow version, retains object state fields alongside the upstream response with \`answers\`, exposes primitive or array state under \`state\`, and supports structured answer paths such as \`$.answers.articleType.choice\`. Use a TypeSafe Provider/model from the current snapshot and never add credentials or connection details to a plan.
    
    TypeSafe Workflow node output retains object state fields alongside the upstream typed response; primitive and array state is exposed under \`state\`. This lets a typed classification route the original Workflow context without adding a merge node. Gateway transport remains unchanged.
    
    Workflow node capabilities are dynamic. Always use the current snapshot's \`capabilities.workflow.supportedNodeTypes\` list, including each type, version, purpose, ports, and configuration schema. Do not assume a node exists when it is absent from the snapshot. A logical plan uses model-chosen node keys and edges between those keys; the server generates durable ids and positions.
    
    Published Workflows are executable from workspace chat through \`@Workflow\` mentions. The remaining message text is the Workflow Input, execution uses the latest immutable published version, and Run progress and Artifacts appear in the chat transcript. Draft Workflows are excluded. This chat dispatcher does not turn Workflows into Agents or create Agent sessions.
    
    Workflow Run lifecycle supports pause for queued or running Runs through \`POST /runs/:runId/pause\` and resume for paused Runs through \`POST /runs/:runId/resume\`. Pause has no checkpoint inside the active invocation; resume reruns that invocation from its start without rerunning successful predecessors. Pause does not apply to \`waiting_for_input\` Runs. A paused Run keeps its event stream open, survives an API restart as paused, remains cancellable, and scheduler overlap prevention treats it as active.
    
    Workflow List is the user-facing access point for per-Workflow Run history. Expanded Run rows expose ordered node execution logs with failure reasons, and a failed Run offers a retry control on the single node entry the server marks retryable. They expose Artifacts inline only when the immutable Workflow version contains an Artifact node, and an individual Artifact detail is directly addressable without a standalone Artifact collection destination.
    
    The Logs destination owns Gateway transport observability: request statistics and captured Provider request details, read over one explicit time range shared by both views. Providers configures what the Gateway dispatches to; Logs reads what it did. Statistics are retained indefinitely while captured request details expire after three days, so the same range can legitimately cover more statistics than details. Settings keeps Usage and Audit Log, which are WorkLite business records rather than Gateway transport records.

              "example": "# 把一篇文章写得更好读\n\n读一篇长文时，读者通常不是从头到尾匀速阅读。清楚的重点、舒适的段落和可信的细节，能帮助他们很快找到有用信息。\n\n## 先把最重要的话说清楚\n\n与其在开头铺陈很多背景，不如先告诉读者这篇文章要回答什么问题。这样，读者可以判断内容是否与自己有关，也能更容易跟上后面的解释。\n\n**阅读体验来自清晰的层次，而不是更多装饰。**\n\n> 好的排版让读者更快看懂内容，也让重要信息更容易被记住。\n\n## 把内容拆成可扫描的部分\n\n长段落会让手机阅读变得费力。把一个主要意思放进一个自然段，再用小标题标出话题变化，读者就能按自己的节奏阅读。\n\n### 一段只承担一个主要意思\n\n当一个段落同时解释原因、步骤和结论时，读者需要反复回看。拆开之后，每一段的作用更清楚，重点也不容易被埋住。\n\n- 每个段落围绕一个意思展开。\n- 重要结论用简短句子表达。\n- 背景和例子放在最相关的位置。\n\n### 用顺序帮助读者行动\n\n需要说明流程时，编号列表能把先后关系直接展示出来：\n\n1. 先说明要解决的问题。\n2. 给出具体、可执行的做法。\n3. 用结果或判断标准收尾。\n\n| 排版方式 | 读者更容易做到 |\n| --- | --- |\n| 短段落 | 快速扫读 |\n| 小标题 | 定位主题 |\n| 列表 | 比较步骤 |\n\n## 把重点留给真正重要的信息\n\n粗体适合标出关键结论，但如果每句话都加粗，重点反而会消失。选择少量需要记住的信息，能让读者一眼找到文章主线。\n\n读完之后，读者应该能说出文章回答了什么问题，以及下一步可以做什么。"

    {"id":"wfv_58db4e40-cf32-472f-83da-0c4e1cb515f9","workflowId":"wf_35c6132e-5bb9-4621-a9d1-d0f49d43d925","version":1,"schemaVersion":4,"definition":{"schemaVersion":4,"input":{"example":"# 把一篇文章写得更好读\n\n读一篇长文时，读者通常不是从头到尾匀速阅读。清楚的重点、舒适的段落和可信的细节，能帮助他们很快找到有用信息。\n\n## 先把最重要的话说清楚\n\n与其在开头铺陈很多背景，不如先告诉读者这篇文章要回答什么问题。这样，读者可以判断内容是否与自己有关，也能更容易跟上后面的解释。\n\n**阅读体验来自清晰的层次，而不是更多装饰。**\n\n> 好的排版让读者更快看懂内容，也让重要信息更容易被记住。\n\n## 把内容拆成可扫描的部分\n\n长段落会让手机阅读变得费力。把一个主要意思放进一个自然段，再用小标题标出话题变化，读者就能按自己的节奏阅读。\n\n### 一段只承担一个主要意思\n\n当一个段落同时解释原因、步骤和结论时，读者需要反复回看。拆开之后，每一段的作用更清楚，重点也不容易被埋住。\n\n- 每个段落围绕一个意思展开。\n- 重要结论用简短句子表达。\n- 背景和例子放在最相关的位置。\n\n### 用顺序帮助读者行动\n\n需要说明流程时，编号列表能把先后关系直接展示出来：\n\n1. 先说明要解决的问题。\n2. 给出具体、可执行的做法。\n3. 用结果或判断标准收尾。\n\n| 排版方式 | 读者更容易做到 |\n| --- | --- |\n| 短段落 | 快速扫读 |\n| 小标题 | 定位主题 |\n| 列表 | 比较步骤 |\n\n## 把重点留给真正重要的信息\n\n粗体适合标出关键结论，但如果每句话都加粗，重点反而会消失。选择少量需要记住的信息，能让读者一眼找到文章主线。\n\n读完之后，读者应该能说出文章回答了什么问题，以及下一步可以做什么。"},"defaults":{"errorPolicy":"stop"},"nodes":[{"id":"sample-input","position":{"x":100,"y":180},"type":"worklite/input","typeVersion":"1","config":{},"errorPolicy":"stop"},{"id":"save-draft","position":{"x":440,"y":180},"type":"wechat-official-account/publish","typeVersion":"1","config":{"accountId":"wechat_official_account_personal","mode":"draft"},"errorPolicy":"stop"}],"edges":[{"id":"article-to-draft","sourceNodeId":"sample-input","sourcePort":"output","targetNodeId":"save-draft","targetPort":"article"}]},"sourceRevisionId":"wfr_6b69b5bb-01af-4688-8f66-8a2335901d6a","publishedAt":"2026-09-23T07:09:55.773Z","publishedBy":"You"}

    async function captureLoginQrCode(page: Page): Promise<string> {
      const qr = loginQrCode(page);
      try {
        await qr.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 20_000 });
      } catch (error) {
        await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/worklite-login-qr-timeout.png', fullPage: true }).catch(() => undefined);
        throw error;
      }
      return `data:image/png;base64,${(await qr.screenshot()).toString('base64')}`;
    }
    
    async function showScanLogin(page: Page): Promise<void> {
      const qr = loginQrCode(page);
      const toggle = page.locator('a.login__type__container__link_text').first();
      await qr.or(toggle).first().waitFor({ state: 'attached', timeout: 20_000 });
      if (await qr.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 3_000 }).then(() => true).catch(() => false)) return;
      // WeChat sometimes renders the scan-login toggle as hidden even while it is
      // the only control exposed. Dispatch its DOM click so the QR can appear.
      await toggle.evaluate(`element => { if (element instanceof HTMLElement) element.click(); }`);
      await qr.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 20_000 });
    }

    function findDraftIdInText(value: string): string | null {
      return value.match(/"(?:appMsgId|appmsgid|appmsgId)"\s*:\s*"?([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)/i)?.[1] ?? null;
    }
    
    function platformAcceptedSave(body: unknown): boolean {
      const code = findString(body, ['ret', 'errcode', 'err_code']);
      const message = findString(body, ['err_msg', 'errmsg', 'msg']);
      return code === '0' || (code === null && message === 'ok');
    }
    
    function platformRejection(body: unknown, responseText: string): string | null {
      if (platformAcceptedSave(body)) return null;
      const message = findString(body, ['err_msg', 'errmsg', 'msg']);
      const code = findString(body, ['ret', 'errcode', 'err_code']);
      if (message && code) return `${message} (${code})`;
      if (message) return message;
      if (code) return `status ${code}`;
      return body === null && responseText.trim() ? responseText.trim().slice(0, 300) : null;
    }
    
    const DRAFT_SAVE_SUB_ACTIONS = new Set(['save', 'create', 'update', 'copy']);
    
    function isDraftSaveRequest(response: Response): boolean {
      const url = response.url();
      if (!url.includes('operate_appmsg')) return false;
      const sub = draftSaveSubAction(url) ?? draftSaveSubAction(`?${response.request().postData() ?? ''}`);
      return sub !== null && DRAFT_SAVE_SUB_ACTIONS.has(sub);
    }
    
    function draftSaveSubAction(value: string): string | null {
      try {
        const query = value.startsWith('?') ? new URLSearchParams(value.slice(1)) : new URL(value).searchParams;
        return query.get('sub');
      } catch {
        return null;
      }
    }
    
    async function waitForDraftIdInUrl(page: Page): Promise<string | null> {
      await page.waitForURL((url) => Boolean(draftIdFromUrl(url.toString())), { timeout: 30_000 }).catch(() => undefined);
      return draftIdFromUrl(page.url());
    }
    
    function draftIdFromUrl(value: string): string | null {
      try {
        const id = new URL(value).searchParams.get('appmsgid');
        return id && /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/.test(id) && !/^0+$/.test(id) ? id : null;
      } catch {
        return null;
      }
    }

    $ cat AGENTS_WORKFLOW.md
    # AI Workflows
    
    ## Project Architecture Change Workflow
    
    Use this workflow for changes to system architecture, technology choices, service or domain boundaries, persistence, runtime behavior, security boundaries, repository structure, deployment topology, or any decision documented in `docs/project-architecture/README.md`.
    
    `docs/project-architecture/README.md` is the source of truth for project architecture.
    
    1. Read `docs/project-architecture/README.md` in full before proposing or implementing an architecture change.
    2. Discuss the motivation, alternatives, tradeoffs, migration impact, and implementation boundaries with the user.
    3. Do not modify files or implement the change until the user explicitly confirms the agreed approach.
    4. After confirmation, update `docs/project-architecture/README.md` before changing implementation files.
    5. Update all affected sections so the document remains internally consistent; do not leave obsolete guidance in place.
    6. Add a dated entry to the document's `Changelog` describing the decision and its impact.
    7. Implement only the architecture described by the updated document and only within the approved scope.
    8. If implementation reveals a required deviation or new architectural choice, stop and return to user discussion and explicit confirmation.
    9. Keep code, configuration, tests, and operational documentation consistent with the architecture source of truth.
    10. Report both documentation and implementation changes when handing the task back to the user.
    
    If a request contains architecture and ordinary implementation work, this workflow takes precedence for the architecture portion. After the architecture is approved and documented, apply any relevant implementation workflow to the remaining work.
    
    ## UI Change Workflow
    
    Use this workflow for any user-interface change, including pages, components, layouts, visual styling, design tokens, colors, typography, icons, motion, responsive behavior, themes, user-facing copy, interaction feedback, and workflow-editor presentation.
    
    `docs/ui-design-system/README.md` is the source of truth for UI design principles and visual language. `ui-ux-design/README.md` is the source of truth for page structure, shared UI architecture, implementation sequencing, and page-level acceptance criteria.
    
    1. Read `docs/ui-design-system/README.md` and `ui-ux-design/README.md` in full before proposing or implementing a UI change. Then follow the design index and read every shared document and applicable `DESIGN.md` for the requested surface.
    2. Compare the requested change with the documented principles, tokens, shared patterns, page rules, interaction patterns, and product-specific guidance.
    3. Explain the proposed visual result, affected surfaces, relevant tradeoffs, and any required design-system changes to the user.
    4. Do not modify UI files or implement the change until the user explicitly confirms the proposed approach.
    5. If the proposal introduces or changes a design decision, update the affected `DESIGN.md`, applicable shared specification, and `ui-ux-design/README.md` index before changing implementation files. New pages require a page `DESIGN.md` before implementation.
    6. Implement only the confirmed approach. Use shared semantic design tokens and reusable components; do not introduce page-level hard-coded styles that duplicate or bypass the design system.
    7. Design and implement light and dark modes together. Neither mode may be treated as a fallback or simple color inversion.
    8. Preserve accessibility, including sufficient contrast, visible keyboard focus, non-color status cues, reduced-motion support, and accessible names for icon-only controls.
    9. If implementation reveals a conflict with the design system or requires a new design choice, stop and return to user discussion and explicit confirmation.
    10. Do not create or modify tests. After implementation, only a simple type check is permitted; do not package, build, or run test suites.
    11. Report the design-system basis, shared and page documents read or changed, affected UI surfaces, light and dark mode behavior, and type-check result when handing the task back to the user.
    
    If a request contains both architecture and UI changes, apply the Project Architecture Change Workflow first, then this workflow. This workflow takes precedence over the General Fallback Workflow for UI work.
    
    ## General Fallback Workflow
    
    Use this workflow only when no more specific workflow applies to the user's request.
    
    1. Do not execute the request immediately.
    2. Explain the proposed development approach, intended changes, and relevant implementation considerations to the user.
    3. Wait for the user's explicit confirmation before modifying files or performing any implementation action.
    4. After confirmation, implement only the approved approach and scope.
    5. Do not create or modify test cases for the implementation.
    6. After implementation, only a simple type check is permitted.
    7. Do not package or build the project.
    8. Do not run test cases or attempt other validation commands beyond the permitted simple type check.
    9. Report the implemented changes and the result of the type check, if one was available and performed.

      subscribe(listener: ActionListener): () => void {

      async execute(request: NodeExecutionRequest, version: '1' | '2'): Promise<NodeExecutionResult> {
        const config = asRecord(request.config);
        const input = asRecord(request.input);
        const accountId = typeof config?.accountId === 'string' ? config.accountId : '';
        const mode = config?.mode;
        const article = typeof input?.article === 'string' ? input.article : '';
        const metadata = asRecord(input?.metadata) ?? {};
        if (!accountId || (mode !== 'draft' && mode !== 'publish')) throw new Error('WeChat Official Account node requires an account and mode.');
        if (!article.trim()) throw new Error('WeChat Official Account node requires Markdown article input.');
        const coverImage = version === '2' ? validateGeneratedCover(input?.coverImage) : null;
        const account = await this.getAccountRow(accountId);
        const idempotencyKey = `${request.context.workflowRunId}:${request.context.nodeRunId}`;
        const publication = await this.ensurePublication(request, accountId, mode, article, metadata, idempotencyKey);
        if (publication.status === 'published' || (mode === 'draft' && publication.status === 'draft_saved')) return { output: toPublicationOutput(publication) };
    
        if (!account.encryptedStorageState) {
          const pending = await this.startLogin(request.context.pendingActionId, account.id, true);
          return { status: 'waiting_for_input', pendingAction: pending };
        }
    
        if (publication.draftId) {
          if (mode === 'draft') {
            await this.db.update(wechatPublications).set({ status: 'draft_saved', lastError: null, updatedAt: new Date() }).where(eq(wechatPublications.id, publication.id));
            return { output: toPublicationOutput({ ...publication, status: 'draft_saved' }) };
          }
          return { status: 'waiting_for_input', pendingAction: await this.openDraftForConfirmation(request.context.pendingActionId, publication, account.encryptedStorageState) };
        }
    
        if (!coverImage) return this.compose(request.context.pendingActionId, publication, account.encryptedStorageState, request.signal);
        const coverPath = join(tmpdir(), `worklite-wechat-cover-${randomUUID()}.png`);
        await writeFile(coverPath, Buffer.from(coverImage.b64Json, 'base64'));
        try {
          return await this.compose(request.context.pendingActionId, publication, account.encryptedStorageState, request.signal, coverPath);
        } finally {
          await rm(coverPath, { force: true }).catch(() => undefined);
        }
      }
    
      async refresh(actionId: string): Promise<PendingNodeExecutionResult['pendingAction']> {
        const [action] = await this.db.select().from(workflowPendingActions).where(eq(workflowPendingActions.id, actionId)).limit(1);
        if (!action) throw new NotFoundException('Pending action not found.');
        await this.closeSession(actionId);
        if (action.type === 'wechat_login') {
          const [publication] = await this.db.select().from(wechatPublications).where(eq(wechatPublications.nodeRunId, action.nodeRunId)).limit(1);
          if (!publication) throw new NotFoundException('WeChat publication not found.');
          return this.startLogin(actionId, publication.accountId, true);
        }
        const [publication] = await this.db.select().from(wechatPublications).where(eq(wechatPublications.nodeRunId, action.nodeRunId)).limit(1);
        if (!publication?.draftId) throw new BadRequestException('The WeChat draft is not available.');
        const account = await this.getAccountRow(publication.accountId);
        if (!account.encryptedStorageState) return this.startLogin(actionId, account.id, true);
        return this.openDraftForConfirmation(actionId, publication, account.encryptedStorageState);
      }

      async createForVersion(request: Request, workflowVersionId: string, input: CreateRunRequest): Promise<{ runId: string }> {
        const workspace = await this.workspaces.getWorkspace(request, 'personal');
        const [version] = await this.db.select({ version: workflowVersions, workflow: workflows })
          .from(workflowVersions)
          .innerJoin(workflows, eq(workflowVersions.workflowId, workflows.id))
          .where(and(eq(workflowVersions.id, workflowVersionId), eq(workflowVersions.workspaceId, workspace.id), eq(workflowVersions.published, true))).limit(1);
        if (!version) throw new NotFoundException('Published workflow version not found');
        return this.createScheduledRun(version.workflow.workspaceId, version.workflow.id, workflowVersionId, input?.input ?? null);
      }
    
      async createScheduledRun(workspaceId: string, workflowId: string, workflowVersionId: string, input: unknown): Promise<{ runId: string }> {
        const runId = `run_${randomUUID()}`;
        await this.db.insert(workflowRuns).values({ id: runId, workspaceId, workflowId, workflowVersionId, input: sanitizeWorkflowImages(input ?? null), status: 'queued' });
        await this.publish(runId, 'run.status', { status: 'queued' });
        this.schedule(runId);
        return { runId };
      }

        await this.db.update(workflowNodeRuns).set({ status: 'cancelled', error: 'Workflow run cancelled.', finishedAt }).where(and(eq(workflowNodeRuns.runId, runId), inArray(workflowNodeRuns.status, ['queued', 'running', 'waiting_for_input'])));

    import { Body, Controller, Get, Header, Headers, Param, Post, Req, Res } from '@nestjs/common';
    import type { Request, Response } from 'express';
    import type { CreateRunRequest, RunProgressEvent } from '@worklite/contracts';
    import { RunsService } from './runs.service';
    
    @Controller()
    export class RunsController {
      constructor(private readonly runs: RunsService) {}
    
      @Get('runs')
      list(@Req() request: Request) {
        return this.runs.list(request, 'personal');
      }
    
      @Get('runs/:runId')
      get(@Req() request: Request, @Param('runId') runId: string) {
        return this.runs.get(request, 'personal', runId);
      }
    
      @Get('runs/:runId/events')
      @Header('Cache-Control', 'no-cache, no-transform')
      async events(@Req() request: Request, @Param('runId') runId: string, @Headers('last-event-id') lastEventId: string | undefined, @Res() response: Response): Promise<void> {
        const afterSequence = parseLastEventId(lastEventId);
        await this.runs.get(request, 'personal', runId);
        response.status(200);
        response.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/event-stream');
        response.setHeader('Connection', 'keep-alive');
        response.setHeader('X-Accel-Buffering', 'no');
        response.flushHeaders();
        let lastSequence = afterSequence;
        let replaying = true;
        let closed = false;
        const pending: RunProgressEvent[] = [];
        const send = (event: RunProgressEvent) => {
          if (closed || event.runId !== runId || event.sequence <= lastSequence) return;
          lastSequence = event.sequence;
          response.write(`id: ${event.sequence}\ndata: ${JSON.stringify(event)}\n\n`);
        };
        const unsubscribe = this.runs.subscribe((event) => {
          if (event.runId !== runId) return;
          if (replaying) pending.push(event);
          else send(event);
        });
        const heartbeat = setInterval(() => response.write(': keep-alive\n\n'), 15_000);
        const cleanup = () => {
          if (closed) return;
          closed = true;
          clearInterval(heartbeat);
          unsubscribe();
        };
        request.once('close', cleanup);
        const replay = await this.runs.events(request, 'personal', runId, afterSequence);
        replay.forEach(send);
        replaying = false;
        pending.sort((left, right) => left.sequence - right.sequence).forEach(send);
        const latest = await this.runs.get(request, 'personal', runId);
        if (latest.status === 'succeeded' || latest.status === 'failed' || latest.status === 'cancelled' || latest.status === 'timed_out') {
          cleanup();
          response.end();
        }
      }
    
      @Post('workflow-versions/:workflowVersionId/runs')
      createForVersion(@Req() request: Request, @Param('workflowVersionId') workflowVersionId: string, @Body() body: CreateRunRequest) {
        return this.runs.createForVersion(request, workflowVersionId, body);
      }
    
      @Post('runs/:runId/cancel')

    packages/db/src/client.ts:52:Workflow automation and Home are WorkLite's primary product services. Workflows are the only user-configurable execution capability; Chat Bot is the protected workspace entry for guided operations. A Workflow never selects or references a standalone Agent or Agent version; its Agent nodes own their configuration inside immutable Workflow versions. Home has no global Workflow data source. A Workflow appears on Home only when its latest published version contains its one \`worklite/dashboard\` node, and its selected board reads that node's object or object-array output from the latest successful Run of that version. Boards render the Dashboard layout's header, main, and footer elements; list elements define row titles through \`titleKey\` and their display fields, and board titles use the Workflow name. Eligible boards default to Uncategorized; users can move each board into at most one database-backed category, and those records only organize references. Platform-defined Workflow boards are removed. Workflow scheduling is represented by one first-party \`worklite/timer\` node. The first-party node types are Input, Timer, Agent, Choice Branch, TypeSafe System One, TypeSafe System One Map, Dashboard, Artifact, Artifact Query, Approved Article, and Image. The TypeSafe System One node is \`typesafe/systemone@1\`: it requires JSON \`state\`, stores a public Provider/model id and typed \`questions\`, forwards the response unchanged through the Gateway, and exposes typed \`answers\`; it is not an Agent node and has no Workflow-owned credentials. The Image node is \`worklite/image@1\`: it requires a text prompt, fixes the model to \`codex/gpt-image-2\`, returns generated PNG data only inside scheduler execution state, and public Run payloads expose summaries. Its output may connect only to WeChat v2 \`coverImage\`. The built-in \`wechat-official-account/publish\` node has immutable v1 versions that accept Markdown article and optional metadata, while v2 additionally requires a generated \`coverImage\`. Both versions save drafts or publish through a product-owned Playwright browser session. Draft mode succeeds once WeChat accepts the save and exposes a draft id in either the save response or the editor URL's appmsgid parameter; a rejected save reports WeChat's own status text, an accepted save with no exposed id reports that distinct condition, and non-WeChat article links are rendered in the final Related Links section rather than as body links. Login and final confirmation are durable pending actions with QR-only client payloads; completed predecessors are not rerun on resume, and a retried node reopens an existing draft instead of creating a second one. Enabled Timer nodes may use draft mode but cannot use publish mode. Workflow Agent nodes own prompts and Skill/MCP selections; their \`context\` input is optional and may combine one unbounded initial upstream edge with one bounded feedback edge; a Workflow Input edge remains unconditional and unbounded. Artifact nodes own Artifact creation, and Agent and WeChat nodes never create Artifacts.

    packages/db/src/client.ts-271-
    packages/db/src/client.ts-272-Workflows never reference standalone Agent or AgentVersion records. Published Workflows may be invoked from workspace chat with an \`@Workflow\` mention; the remaining text is supplied as Workflow Input and the existing latest published WorkflowVersion Run endpoint is used. Draft Workflows are not runnable mentions. A Workflow Agent node is embedded and self-contained; its optional \`outputFormat\` selects \`text\` (default) or \`json\`, and JSON mode requires valid parseable final output. A JSON-mode node may also declare \`outputContract\`, a non-empty array of unique top-level key names its parsed object must carry; a parsed value that is not an object, or that omits a named key or carries it as \`null\`, an empty string, or an empty array, fails the node and names the missing keys. Without a contract any valid JSON is committed, so a node can succeed while returning a progress note instead of its intended result. A JSON-mode Agent can additionally use \`passthroughKeys\` to carry input fields without model rewriting; optional positive \`maxToolCalls\`, \`maxToolRounds\`, and \`maxToolResultChars\` bound tool use and returned context. Detailed Run responses include \`hasArtifactNode\`, ordered \`nodeRuns\`, and each node run's status, timing, retry count, failure text, and \`retryable\` flag. At most one node run of a failed Run is \`retryable\`, and \`POST /runs/:runId/nodes/:nodeRunId/retry\` re-enters exactly that node run. Run status can also be \`paused\`: \`POST /runs/:runId/pause\` accepts queued or running, \`POST /runs/:runId/resume\` accepts only paused, and resume reruns the active invocation without checkpointing it.
    packages/db/src/client.ts-273-
    packages/db/src/client.ts:274:The platform Skill scripts/inspect-workspace.mjs reports current capability metadata; scripts/edit-workflow.mjs can connect worklite/approved-article@1 as a required context-input gate, and must not route a rejected review directly to Article Artifact or WeChat. The current capability contract is returned by inspect-workspace.mjs at \`capabilities.workflow.supportedNodeTypes\`. Each entry includes its public type, version, purpose, input and output ports, and configuration schema. Use only entries present in that snapshot, and set \`typeVersion: "2"\` when a plan needs a WeChat v2 node. An Artifact node requires a \`data\` input and owns a non-empty \`name\` plus \`text\`, \`markdown\`, or \`json\` type; a successful Run stores its Artifact and its node output is an Artifact reference. Multiple Artifact nodes are allowed. An Artifact Query node requires a \`request\` input, a JSON Artifact \`name\`, a \`titleField\`, and non-empty \`descriptionFields\`; it searches all matching workspace history, including detached Artifacts, skips records without a usable title and description, and returns the original request plus ordered candidate ids, titles, descriptions, and creation times without mutating Artifacts. Empty history returns an empty candidates array. A predicate on the duplicate-screening Agent output \`$.duplicate\` equal to \`false\` can gate downstream research; Agent semantic judgments are not guaranteed reproducible. An Approved Article node requires JSON on \`context\`, verifies explicit approval and Markdown structure, and returns the original article text; route only approved results to final Article Artifacts and WeChat. An Image node requires text on \`prompt\`, fixes the model to \`codex/gpt-image-2\`, and may send its generated PNG output only to WeChat v2 \`coverImage\`; public Run payloads expose image summaries rather than base64 data. The v1 WeChat node requires Markdown on \`article\`, accepts optional JSON \`metadata\`, and configures \`accountId\` plus \`draft\` or \`publish\` mode. The v2 WeChat node additionally requires generated cover JSON on \`coverImage\`. Human login and final publish confirmation suspend the Run as \`waiting_for_input\`; QR refresh continues the same Node Run, and WeChat nodes never create an Artifact. Draft mode resolves its draft id from the accepted save response or the editor URL's appmsgid parameter, reports a rejected save with WeChat's own status text, distinguishes an accepted save whose id is never exposed, and collects non-WeChat links from article input in the final Related Links section rather than rendering them as body links. Do not combine an enabled Timer with publish mode.

    import { Body, Controller, Delete, Get, Param, Patch, Post, Req } from '@nestjs/common';
    import type { Request } from 'express';
    import type { ApplyWorkflowDraftOperationsRequest, CreateWorkflowRequest, ImportWorkflowRequest } from '@worklite/contracts';
    import { WorkflowSchedulesService } from './workflow-schedules.service';
    import { WorkflowsService } from './workflows.service';
    
    @Controller('workflows')
    export class WorkflowsController {
      constructor(private readonly workflows: WorkflowsService, private readonly schedules: WorkflowSchedulesService) {}
    
      @Get()
      list(@Req() request: Request) {
        return this.workflows.list(request, 'personal');
      }
    
      @Get(':workflowId')
      get(@Req() request: Request, @Param('workflowId') workflowId: string) {
        return this.workflows.get(request, 'personal', workflowId);
      }
    
      @Post()
      create(@Req() request: Request, @Body() body: CreateWorkflowRequest) {
        return this.workflows.create(request, 'personal', body);
      }
    
      @Post('import')
      importWorkflow(@Req() request: Request, @Body() body: ImportWorkflowRequest) {
        return this.workflows.importWorkflow(request, 'personal', body);
      }
    
      @Get(':workflowId/export')
      exportWorkflow(@Req() request: Request, @Param('workflowId') workflowId: string) {
        return this.workflows.exportWorkflow(request, 'personal', workflowId);
      }
    
      @Patch(':workflowId')
      update(@Req() request: Request, @Param('workflowId') workflowId: string, @Body() body: Partial<CreateWorkflowRequest>) {
        return this.workflows.update(request, 'personal', workflowId, body);
      }
    
      @Delete(':workflowId')
      delete(@Req() request: Request, @Param('workflowId') workflowId: string) {
        return this.workflows.delete(request, 'personal', workflowId);
      }
    
      @Get(':workflowId/schedule')
      getSchedule(@Req() request: Request, @Param('workflowId') workflowId: string) {
        return this.schedules.get(request, workflowId);
      }
    
      @Post(':workflowId/draft/operations')
      applyOperations(@Req() request: Request, @Param('workflowId') workflowId: string, @Body() body: ApplyWorkflowDraftOperationsRequest) {
        return this.workflows.applyOperations(request, 'personal', workflowId, body);
      }
    
      @Post(':workflowId/draft/undo')
      undo(@Req() request: Request, @Param('workflowId') workflowId: string) {
        return this.workflows.undo(request, 'personal', workflowId);
      }
    
      @Post(':workflowId/draft/redo')
      redo(@Req() request: Request, @Param('workflowId') workflowId: string) {
        return this.workflows.redo(request, 'personal', workflowId);
      }
    
      @Post(':workflowId/publish')
      publish(@Req() request: Request, @Param('workflowId') workflowId: string) {
        return this.workflows.publish(request, 'personal', workflowId);
      }
    
      @Get(':workflowId/versions')
      versions(@Req() request: Request, @Param('workflowId') workflowId: string) {
        return this.workflows.versions(request, 'personal', workflowId);
      }
    }

    $ git show 1ad21fc -- apps/api/src/modules/plugins/wechat-official-account.service.ts
    commit 1ad21fc95ae95b7571b39ab68f5c3d9a7d0b088c
    Author: ccjr1120 <qianaiwuyu@gmail.com>
    Date:   Fri Sep 18 20:27:20 2026 +0800
    
        🔨 fix: set the generated WeChat cover instead of a placeholder
    
        Draft covers were left unset. The empty cover area renders an add-cover plus
        icon, which reads as a grey image, so the failure looked like a placeholder
        being published. Three defects stacked up behind it.
    
        Selection never found the upload. WeChat renders material thumbnails as CSS
        background images on <i> and <div> elements, not <img>, so an img[src] scan
        saw an empty picker. Read src, data-src and background-image, and match the
        new material by identity difference: a new upload shifts every following item,
        so positional comparison selects a pre-existing thumbnail.
    
        Crop confirmation clicked a hidden control. The picker keeps every step's
        buttons in one dialog and hides inactive ones at zero size, so matching on
        text alone locked onto the picker's own hidden 确认 rather than the crop
        step's, which exists only after its image loads. Poll each visible dialog for
        a confirmation that has real layout, clearing the content structure warning
        between attempts.
    
        Verification rejected successful runs. WeChat re-keys a material between the
        upload preview, the library entry and the applied cover, including a
        /mmbiz_png/ to /sz_mmbiz_png/ prefix change, so matching that id across
        stages could never succeed. Verify that a real uploaded material replaced the
        placeholder instead, still failing the node when the cover stays unset.
    
        Removed the grey placeholder generator: version 1 nodes, which have no cover
        input, now leave the cover unset rather than uploading a substitute image the
        author never asked for. Added WECHAT_HEADED=1 to launch a headed browser when
        a cover issue needs to be observed directly.
    
        Verified against the deployment profile: draft 100000229 saved with the
        generated cover, confirmed visually in a headed run.

    commit 6606ef6990a6b7958c6cab176bdb74d394af88fc
    Author: ccjr1120 <qianaiwuyu@gmail.com>
    Date:   Fri Sep 18 19:09:17 2026 +0800
    
        🔨 fix: save WeChat drafts through the real editor control
    
        Draft mode never issued a save request. clickByText matched the text span
        inside the editor button and force:true skipped Playwright's hit-target
        checks, so the click landed on the span without triggering the button
        handler. Click the nearest real control instead.
    
        The failure was also misreported. The save-response matcher accepted any
        operate_appmsg POST, including the unrelated pre_load_sentence preload, and
        error text was derived without first classifying the response, so WeChat's
        own success payload (ret:0, err_msg:"ok") surfaced as a rejection. Match
        only save, create, update and copy sub-actions, classify before reporting,
        and resolve the draft id from the editor URL's appmsgid when an accepted
        save omits it.
    
        Cover selection picked the wrong material. The material library truncates
        long file names, so the hasText filter matched every previous
        worklite-wechat-cover-<uuid>.png upload and .last() selected a stale item.
        Wait for the grid to grow and select the added item.
    
        Verified against the deployment profile: draft 100000191 saved with the
        generated cover on the first attempt.

    async function saveDraft(page: Page): Promise<string> {
      const matchingResponses: Response[] = [];
      const captures: unknown[] = [];
      const observed: string[] = [];
      const onResponse = (response: Response): void => {
        if (!response.url().includes('operate_appmsg') || response.request().method() !== 'POST') return;
        observed.push(response.url());
        if (isDraftSaveRequest(response)) matchingResponses.push(response);
      };
      page.on('response', onResponse);
      try {
        await clickByText(page, ['Save as draft', 'Save', '\u4fdd\u5b58\u4e3a\u8349\u7a3f', '\u4fdd\u5b58']);
        await confirmContentStructureWarning(page);
    
        const deadline = Date.now() + 45_000;
        let acceptedWithoutId = false;
        while (Date.now() < deadline) {
          const response = matchingResponses.shift();
          if (!response) {
            if (acceptedWithoutId) break;
            await delay(250);
            continue;
          }
          const responseText = await response.text().catch(() => '');
          let body: unknown = null;
          try {
            body = JSON.parse(responseText);
          } catch {
            body = null;
          }
          captures.push({
            url: response.url(),
            status: response.status(),
            postData: response.request().postData(),
            body: body ?? responseText,
          });
          const draftId = findString(body, ['appMsgId', 'appmsgid', 'appmsgId']) ?? findDraftIdInText(responseText);
          if (draftId) {
            await waitForDraftIdInUrl(page);
            await page.waitForTimeout(2_000);
            return draftId;
          }
          const rejection = platformRejection(body, responseText);
          if (rejection) throw new Error(`WeChat rejected the draft: ${rejection}`);
          if (platformAcceptedSave(body)) acceptedWithoutId = true;
        }
        if (acceptedWithoutId) {
          const urlDraftId = await waitForDraftIdInUrl(page);
          if (urlDraftId) {
            await page.waitForTimeout(2_000);
            return urlDraftId;
          }
          throw new Error('WeChat accepted the draft but never exposed its draft id.');
        }
        const blockingDialog = await blockingDialogText(page);
        if (blockingDialog) throw new Error(`WeChat blocked the draft with a dialog: ${blockingDialog}`);
        throw new Error('WeChat never answered the draft save request after the editor action was clicked.');
      } catch (error) {
        await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/worklite-save-draft-timeout.png', fullPage: true }).catch(() => undefined);
        await writeFile('/tmp/worklite-save-draft-responses.json', JSON.stringify({ pageUrl: page.url(), observedOperateAppmsgUrls: observed, saveResponses: captures }, null, 2), 'utf8').catch(() => undefined);
        throw error;
      } finally {
        page.off('response', onResponse);
      }
    }
    
    function findDraftIdInText(value: string): string | null {
      return value.match(/"(?:appMsgId|appmsgid|appmsgId)"\s*:\s*"?([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)/i)?.[1] ?? null;
    }
    
    function platformAcceptedSave(body: unknown): boolean {
      const code = findString(body, ['ret', 'errcode', 'err_code']);
      const message = findString(body, ['err_msg', 'errmsg', 'msg']);
      return code === '0' || (code === null && message === 'ok');
    }
    }
    
    async function fillArticle(page: Page, title: string, article: string, coverPath?: string): Promise<void> {
      const titleEditor = page.locator('.ProseMirror').first();
      await titleEditor.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 20_000 });
      await titleEditor.click();
      await titleEditor.fill(title.slice(0, 64));
    
      const bodyEditor = page.locator('.ProseMirror').nth(1);
      await bodyEditor.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 20_000 });
      await bodyEditor.click();
      const html = markdownToHtml(article.replace(/^#\s+.+$/m, '').trim() || article);
      await bodyEditor.evaluate((element, value) => {
        const view = element.ownerDocument.defaultView;
        if (!view) throw new Error('Missing editor window.');
        const data = new view.DataTransfer();
        data.setData('text/html', value);
        const paste = new view.ClipboardEvent('paste', { bubbles: true, cancelable: true });
        Object.defineProperty(paste, 'clipboardData', { value: data });
        element.dispatchEvent(paste);
      }, html);
      // Version 1 nodes have no cover input. Leave the cover unset rather than
      // uploading a substitute image the author never asked for.
      if (coverPath) await setCoverImage(page, coverPath);
    }

    async function fillArticle(page: Page, title: string, article: string, coverPath?: string): Promise<void> {
      const titleEditor = page.locator('.ProseMirror').first();
      await titleEditor.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 20_000 });
      await titleEditor.click();
      await titleEditor.fill(title.slice(0, 64));
    
      const bodyEditor = page.locator('.ProseMirror').nth(1);
      await bodyEditor.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 20_000 });
      await page.context().grantPermissions(['clipboard-read', 'clipboard-write'], { origin: new URL(page.url()).origin });
      await bodyEditor.click();
      const html = markdownToHtml(article.replace(/^#\s+.+$/m, '').trim() || article);
      await bodyEditor.evaluate(async (element, value) => {
        const view = element.ownerDocument.defaultView;
        if (!view?.navigator.clipboard || typeof view.ClipboardItem !== 'function') throw new Error('Browser clipboard is unavailable.');
        const plainText = value.replace(/<[^>]*>/g, ' ').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
        await view.navigator.clipboard.write([new view.ClipboardItem({
          'text/html': new view.Blob([value], { type: 'text/html' }),
          'text/plain': new view.Blob([plainText], { type: 'text/plain' }),
        })]);
      }, html);
      await bodyEditor.press('ControlOrMeta+V');
      await titleEditor.click();
      const expectedLine = article.replace(/^#\s+.+$/m, '').split(/\r?\n/).map((line) => line.trim()).find((line) => line && !line.startsWith('#'));
      const expectedExcerpt = expectedLine?.replace(/^>\s*/, '').replace(/[*_`]/g, '').slice(0, 32);
      const bodyText = (await bodyEditor.textContent())?.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim() ?? '';
      if (!expectedExcerpt || !bodyText.includes(expectedExcerpt)) {
        const editorState = await bodyEditor.evaluate((element) => ({
          className: element.className,
          contentEditable: element.getAttribute('contenteditable'),
          textContent: element.textContent,
          innerHTML: element.innerHTML,
          parentHTML: element.parentElement?.outerHTML.slice(0, 5000),
        })).catch(() => null);
        await writeFile('/tmp/worklite-wechat-body-editor-debug.json', JSON.stringify({ expectedExcerpt, editorState }, null, 2), 'utf8').catch(() => undefined);
        await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/worklite-wechat-body-editor-debug.png', fullPage: true }).catch(() => undefined);
        throw new Error('WeChat article body did not retain its first paragraph after leaving the editor.');
      }
      // Version 1 nodes have no cover input. Leave the cover unset rather than
      // uploading a substitute image the author never asked for.
      if (coverPath) await setCoverImage(page, coverPath);
    }

    async function fillArticle(page: Page, title: string, article: string, coverPath?: string): Promise<void> {
      const titleEditor = page.locator('.ProseMirror').first();
      await titleEditor.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 20_000 });
      await titleEditor.click();
      await titleEditor.fill(title.slice(0, 64));
    
      const bodyEditor = page.locator('.ProseMirror').nth(1);
      await bodyEditor.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 20_000 });
      await bodyEditor.click();
      const html = markdownToHtml(article.replace(/^#\s+.+$/m, '').trim() || article);
      const insertHtmlResult = await bodyEditor.evaluate((element, value) => {
        element.focus();
        return element.ownerDocument.execCommand('insertHTML', false, value);
      }, html);
      await titleEditor.click();
      const expectedLine = article.replace(/^#\s+.+$/m, '').split(/\r?\n/).map((line) => line.trim()).find((line) => line && !line.startsWith('#'));
      const expectedExcerpt = expectedLine?.replace(/^>\s*/, '').replace(/[*_`]/g, '').slice(0, 32);
      const bodyText = (await bodyEditor.textContent())?.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim() ?? '';
      if (!expectedExcerpt || !bodyText.includes(expectedExcerpt)) {
        const editorState = await bodyEditor.evaluate((element) => ({
          className: element.className,
          contentEditable: element.getAttribute('contenteditable'),
          textContent: element.textContent,
          innerHTML: element.innerHTML,
          parentHTML: element.parentElement?.outerHTML.slice(0, 5000),
        })).catch(() => null);
        const keyEvent = await page.locator('html').getAttribute('data-worklite-key-event');
        await writeFile('/tmp/worklite-wechat-body-editor-debug.json', JSON.stringify({ expectedExcerpt, insertHtmlResult, editorState }, null, 2), 'utf8').catch(() => undefined);
        await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/worklite-wechat-body-editor-debug.png', fullPage: true }).catch(() => undefined);
        throw new Error('WeChat article body did not retain its first paragraph after leaving the editor.');
      }
      // Version 1 nodes have no cover input. Leave the cover unset rather than
      // uploading a substitute image the author never asked for.
      if (coverPath) await setCoverImage(page, coverPath);
    }

    # WorkLite UI Design System
    
    This document is the source of truth for WorkLite user-interface principles and visual language. `ui-ux-design/README.md` defines page structure, shared UI architecture, implementation sequencing, and page-level acceptance criteria. Every UI proposal and implementation must follow both documents through the UI Change Workflow in `AGENTS_WORKFLOW.md`.
    
    ## Product Character
    
    WorkLite is a professional personal workspace for creating and running AI agents and workflows. Its interface should feel calm, precise, focused, and warm.
    
    The visual direction is inspired by the clarity and efficiency of Linear without copying its brand. WorkLite establishes its own identity through a clear blue accent, execution-oriented interaction patterns, and a consistent visual language for agents, workflows, and runs.
    
    The interface must:
    
    - Prioritize clarity, scanability, and control over decoration.
    - Support efficient, sustained use at moderate-to-high information density.
    - Communicate AI behavior through observable state and feedback rather than visual spectacle.
    - Feel lighter than a traditional enterprise dashboard and more dependable than a novelty AI interface.
    - Treat light and dark modes as equally important, deliberately designed experiences.
    
    The WorkLite brand mark is the orange robot outline in `apps/web/public/brand/worklite-logo.png`. Use the transparent asset through the shared `WorkLiteMark` component for product-owned branding, onboarding, and browser icons. Do not recreate the mark with a substitute icon or apply a background that reduces its legibility.
    
    ## Design Principles
    
    1. **Calm by default.** Neutral surfaces dominate; color is reserved for meaning and action.
    2. **Precise hierarchy.** Typography, spacing, borders, and surface contrast establish structure before shadows or decoration.
    3. **Visible execution.** Users can understand what is running, waiting, completed, or failed.
    4. **Progressive disclosure.** Common actions remain immediate while advanced configuration stays available without overwhelming the primary flow.
    5. **Consistent semantics.** The same color, component, and motion meaning applies throughout the product.
    6. **Accessible interaction.** Keyboard access, visible focus, sufficient contrast, and non-color cues are baseline requirements.
    7. **One action per goal.** A goal has a single activation point. The product does not ask for a step it can take itself, and it recovers from staleness it can observe rather than offering a refresh control. `ui-ux-design/shared/interaction-contract.md` governs the details.
    8. **Text earns its place.** Every string is an action, a state, a constraint, or a recovery. Text that restates a heading, repeats what a component already shows, or explains automation the user cannot act on is removed. `ui-ux-design/shared/copy-standards.md` governs the details.
    
    ## Color System
    
    All implementation colors must be exposed through semantic design tokens. Raw color values must not be repeated in page or feature code.
    
    ### Core Neutrals and Brand
    
    | Token | Light mode | Dark mode | Purpose |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | `background` | `#F7F8FA` | `#101216` | Application background |
    | `surface` | `#FFFFFF` | `#171A20` | Primary content surface |
    | `surface-raised` | `#FFFFFF` | `#1C2027` | Menus, dialogs, and elevated panels |
    | `surface-subtle` | `#F1F3F5` | `#1D2128` | Secondary and selected-neutral surfaces |
    | `text-primary` | `#202126` | `#ECEEF2` | Primary text |
    | `text-secondary` | `#6F747E` | `#989FAA` | Supporting text |
    | `border` | `#E4E6EA` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.09)` | Standard boundaries |
    | `brand` | `#4F6F9F` | `#8EA8CF` | Primary action and brand emphasis |
    | `brand-hover` | `#415F8B` | `#A5B9D7` | Brand control hover |
    | `brand-active` | `#344D73` | `#7893BD` | Brand control active state |
    | `brand-subtle` | `#F1F2F4` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08)` | Selection and restrained emphasis |
    
    The blue brand color is the signature accent. It represents primary action and current focus. It must not be applied indiscriminately to headings, icons, large backgrounds, or ordinary content.
    
    ### Semantic Status Colors
    
    Brand color must not replace status meaning.
    
    - **Running:** blue brand accent plus a text or icon cue.
    - **Success and completed:** green.
    - **Warning and paused:** amber or yellow, visually distinct from brand orange.
    - **Error and failed:** red.
    - **Information:** cool blue.
    - **Queued, cancelled, and inactive:** neutral gray.
    
    Every status must use at least one non-color cue, such as an icon, label, shape, or motion pattern.
    
    ## Themes
    
    WorkLite supports `System`, `Light`, and `Dark` appearance settings. The default is `System`, and an explicit user selection must persist.
    
    - Resolve the theme before initial paint to prevent a light-theme flash.
    - Set the browser `color-scheme` to match the active theme.
    - Theme shared editors, charts, scrollbars, diagrams, illustrations, and floating surfaces with the application.
    - Preserve the same hierarchy and semantic meanings across themes.
    - Do not create dark mode through automatic color inversion.
    - Use subtle transition timing and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
    
    Light mode should feel crisp and open. Dark mode should feel focused and deep, using dark blue-gray rather than pure black.
    
    ## Typography
    
    Use `Inter`, `Geist`, or a compatible modern system sans-serif stack. Use a monospace stack for code, identifiers, variables, model parameters, and logs. Enable tabular numbers for changing metrics and aligned numeric data.
    
    | Role | Size | Weight |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Page title | `24px` | `600` |
    | Section title | `16px` | `600` |
    | Component title | `14px` | `600` |
    | Body | `14px` | `400` |
    | Secondary text | `13px` | `400` |
    | Label | `12px` | `500` |
    | Code and data | `12px` to `13px` | `400` or `500` |
    
    Use concise, direct source copy and preserve the same meaning and tone in every supported locale. Avoid promotional language inside the application. Labels must describe actions or content without relying on placeholder text. Every string must qualify as an action, a state, a constraint, or a recovery under `ui-ux-design/shared/copy-standards.md`; section and page descriptions are optional and exist only to state a constraint or bound a scope. Use the fixed Chinese resource set for all product copy and locale-aware formatting.
    
    ## Spacing and Layout
    
    Use a `4px` base spacing grid.
    
    - Page padding: `24px`.
    - Major section gap: `24px`.
    - Standard panel padding: `16px`.
    - Form-field gap: `16px`.
    - Compact element gap: `8px`.
    - Icon-to-label gap: `6px` to `8px`.
    - Standard control height: `36px`.
    - Compact control height: `28px` to `32px`.
    - Top context bar height: `48px` to `52px`.
    - Primary sidebar width: `220px` to `240px`.
    
    The default application shell uses a stable sidebar, a compact context bar, a primary content region, and an optional contextual inspector. Logs or execution output may use a resizable lower panel when persistent visibility is valuable.
    
    Responsive layouts must preserve task priority. Secondary inspectors may collapse into drawers, while primary actions and current state remain accessible.
    
    ## Shape, Borders, and Elevation
    
    - Small controls: `6px` radius.
    - Buttons and inputs: `8px` radius.
    - Cards and panels: `10px` radius.
    - Dialogs: `12px` radius.
    - Status badges may use a pill shape.
    - Standard borders are `1px`.
    
    Use cards only when content is a distinct object or group. Avoid placing every section in a rounded container. Use shadows primarily for menus, dialogs, drag previews, and genuinely elevated content; prefer surface contrast and borders for ordinary hierarchy.
    
    ## Components
    
    ### Navigation
    
    Keep navigation neutral and grouped by task. Keep the first-level menu concise and direct; related views owned by a destination use stable in-page tabs instead of child sidebar menus. The selected item uses a subtle brand surface, stronger text, and a narrow blue indicator. Do not fill the entire sidebar with brand color.
    
    ### Buttons
    
    - **Primary:** solid blue for the most important action in the current context.
    - **Secondary:** neutral fill or restrained border for supporting actions.
    - **Ghost:** toolbars, inline actions, and low-emphasis controls.
    - **Destructive:** red and reserved for genuinely destructive actions.
    
    Prefer one primary action per visible region. Loading actions must respond immediately and preserve enough label context to explain what is happening. Progress belongs on the activated control, not on the region around it.
    
    Do not pair a preparation control with a commit control for one goal. When a step is always required before committing, the commit performs it. A manual refresh control is permitted only when the product cannot observe that the value is stale.
    
    ### Forms
    
    Keep labels visible above fields. Placeholder text provides examples only. Place help and validation messages next to the relevant field. Clearly communicate `Saving`, `Saved`, and `Unsaved changes` states. Group advanced configuration and disclose it progressively. Use dedicated editors for prompts, code, and structured data.
    
    Form controls use one crisp boundary at rest. Hover may strengthen that boundary with neutral contrast, while keyboard focus replaces it with the brand-colored boundary and one soft, translucent halo without a gap. Do not stack an outline, border, and offset ring into multiple hard focus borders. Invalid controls use the same treatment with the error color. Disabled controls keep their boundary and surface legible without hover or active feedback.
    
    Apply the same focus language to buttons, selection controls, tabs, menu items, and custom interactive rows. Borderless or inset interactions use one contained focus indicator that follows the component shape. Pointer, hover, active, focus, disabled, and invalid states must remain consistent across local and shared controls.
    
    ### Tables and Lists
    
    Prefer compact lists or tables for agents, workflows, and runs when scanability matters. Use row heights around `44px` to `48px`, subdued headers, predictable sorting, visible filter chips, and on-hover secondary actions. Keep status near the object name. Truncated identifiers must be copyable. Distinguish an empty collection from a filtered result with no matches.
    
    ### Overlays and Feedback
    
    Dialogs are for focused decisions, not routine navigation. Toasts communicate transient outcomes; important results and errors must remain visible in the page. Error feedback should explain the problem and provide a recovery action when one exists.
    
    ### Icons
    
    Use Lucide icons consistently, normally at `16px` and at `18px` in primary navigation. Icon-only controls require an accessible name, tooltip, and an adequate interaction target. Emoji are not product icons.
    
    ## Product-Specific Patterns
    
    ### Chat Workflow Mentions
    
    The embedded Chat Bot mention menu supports published Workflows only. Keep the selected Workflow chip compact and removable so users understand that the mention creates a Workflow Run. Workflow progress uses the existing queued, running, completed, failed, and cancelled status semantics, with text and icon cues in addition to color. Successful Workflow Artifacts appear as restrained transcript cards with a direct details action. Draft Workflows are not listed as runnable mentions.
    
    ### Agents
    
    Present agents as configurable work units, not cartoon characters. Identity comes from a restrained geometric symbol or letter mark, name, responsibility, model, available skills or tools, ownership, version, and recent run state.
    
    ### AI Response Content
    
    Use one shared streaming Markdown renderer for model-generated text across Chat Bot and future Agent response surfaces. It must handle incomplete Markdown during streaming, GitHub Flavored Markdown, long words, tables, links, lists, quotations, and fenced code without executing embedded HTML or scripts. Product styling wraps the renderer and uses semantic tokens in both themes; transport parsing and conversation state do not belong inside the renderer.
    
    In conversational layouts, user messages align to the right in compact neutral bubbles and remain plain text. Agent responses align to the left with a wider, unframed reading column so structured output remains scannable. Alignment, accessible labels, and optional identity marks distinguish speakers without relying on color. Streaming updates follow the end only when the reader was already at the end, and a return-to-end control appears while they are not.
    
    One Agent turn is one block with one identity mark, however many message segments and Skill calls it contains. Its segments and Skill-call rows share that block's content column, so a turn that answers, runs a script, and answers again reads as one reply instead of as several speakers. Working, cancelled, and failure cues render as inline notes without identity marks, because a status is not a speaker; they remain independent status regions for assistive technology.
    
    Create a Chat Bot response placeholder in the transcript as soon as a turn starts. Show restrained inline progress there instead of replacing or disabling the composer. While a turn is running, keep the draft input editable and replace the send control with a familiar square Stop icon; stopping is a neutral execution control rather than a destructive action. Preserve the draft after completion or cancellation, and use text plus icon cues for working and cancelled states.
    
    A message submitted during a running turn joins a visible removable queue and sends when that turn completes. A composer that accepts a keystroke and silently discards it reports work the product did not do, so queuing is the honest behavior for input the reader has already committed. Queue rows are restrained neutral transcript entries with a count and a per-row remove control, not a second execution surface. The queue pauses in place — keeping every entry and its order — when the turn fails, when the reader stops it, and while a clarification question is pending, and it says that it is paused.
    
    Present inline Skill calls as compact disclosure rows by default. The collapsed row keeps the Skill identity, script name, execution status, and exit code visible without allowing arguments, host details, or raw output to dominate the transcript. A keyboard-accessible disclosure control reveals the complete metadata, warning, and a height-bounded internally scrollable output region. Failed calls remain collapsed unless the user opens them.
    
    Treat `@` selection in the Chat Bot composer as structured dispatch, not decorated message text. Opening `@` presents a searchable keyboard-accessible published Workflow menu with pointer selection, arrow navigation, `Enter`, and `Escape`. A selection becomes one removable mention token before the task text inside the same bordered input surface; it must not appear as a separate adjacent field or region. Only one Workflow may be selected for a task, and its identity remains visible until dispatch or removal. The token and task text may wrap together within that shared surface on narrow screens. Chat Bot does not expose Agent mentions or child sessions.
    
    ### Workflow Editor
    
    - Represent workflows on a focused React Flow node canvas with explicit input and output handles, directional edges, and persisted spatial layout.
    - Use a canvas with one right-side contextual panel. The panel shows the searchable node palette when nothing is selected and replaces it with the selected node or edge inspector.
    - Keep nodes visually consistent and expose essential node-owned parameters, including editable Text content, without requiring the inspector for common work.
    - Add nodes through the searchable palette at a predictable viewport position and allow direct node dragging for spatial organization.
    - Provide familiar icon controls for zoom in, zoom out, fit view, and deletion.
    - Keep edge direction and handle compatibility visible through shape, persistent port labels, and valid or invalid interaction state rather than color alone.
    - Preserve a keyboard-accessible inspector path for reviewing configuration and removing selected nodes or edges, with an explicit return to the node palette.
    - Keep the contextual panel available at every breakpoint; collapse the combined palette and inspector to one drawer or bottom sheet when the layout cannot support a side panel.
    - Use blue borders or indicators for the selected and currently executing node or edge. Selection belongs to the graph and must remain synchronized with contextual panel content and keyboard focus.
    - Represent successful and failed states through compact green or red markers rather than filling the whole node.
    - Render edges with restrained neutral strokes and reserve stronger treatment for selection and execution.
    - Present AI-assisted edits in a side panel and make proposed structured operations understandable and reviewable.
    - Group workflow-level settings into General, Inputs, Execution, and Versioning sections, with advanced fields disclosed progressively.
    
    Persimmon progression through the graph is a distinctive WorkLite motif. It communicates selection and active execution while neutral surfaces and edges keep dense workflows readable. The initial graph supports acyclic data fan-out; conditional branches, joins, loops, and parallel execution remain outside the current product scope.
    
    ### Runs and Logs
    
    Workflow List exposes Run records through a per-Workflow dialog. Use the following canonical run labels: `Queued`, `Running`, `Waiting for input`, `Completed`, `Failed`, and `Cancelled`.
    
    A Run waiting on a human-gated browser action presents a compact amber pending-action panel before its node logs. The panel names the required action and shows the QR image. An expired code is replaced automatically, so the panel shows neither an expiry time nor an instruction to refresh: during replacement the current image dims and a status line reports that a new code is arriving. `Cancel run` remains, because abandoning the Run is a separate intent rather than a recovery from staleness. Authentication state is communicated with text and icon cues; the QR is not the only explanation. Completion updates through the existing Run event stream and does not require a separate “I scanned it” control.
    
    Show the current step and continuing progress for long operations. Expanded Workflow Run records present ordered node execution logs with node identity, status, timing, duration, and retry context. Failed Runs surface the credential-safe failure reason before the log list and repeat it on the failed node entry. Append logs without forcing disruptive scrolling. Use monospace text for identifiers and raw output, and allow users to distinguish timestamps, severity, source, and content. Successful completion should be clear but restrained; failure must include context and a next step where possible. Artifact disclosure is absent when the immutable Workflow version has no Artifact node; an empty Artifact state is reserved for eligible versions that produced none.
    
    Failure is the one node log state that carries a recovery action. When the server reports a failed node entry as retryable, that entry offers a single neutral secondary `Retry node` control beside its failure reason. Retry is an ordinary execution control, not a destructive or primary action, so it uses neutral styling with an icon and text label rather than brand fill or red. Only the retryable entry exposes it; other failed, cancelled, and successful entries show none, and the control never appears at the Run level where it could be mistaken for rerunning the whole Workflow. Activating it shows a local busy state on that control alone, leaves the surrounding log list in place, and keeps any failure text visible until the Run event stream replaces it with continued execution. A retry that the server rejects preserves the original failure reason and explains the rejection in the same entry.
    
    ## Motion
    
    - Hover feedback: approximately `120ms`.
    - Tooltips and menus: approximately `150ms`.
    - Panels and dialogs: `180ms` to `220ms`.
    - Prefer natural ease-out curves.
    - Avoid decorative page transitions, bounce effects, strong zoom, and large animated gradients.
    - Use motion to clarify execution, selection, expansion, and state changes.
    - Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` and retain static state cues when animation is disabled.
    
    ## Accessibility
    
    - Meet WCAG AA contrast for standard text and essential controls.
    - Keep a visible keyboard focus ring in both themes.
    - Do not communicate state using color alone.
    - Provide interaction targets of at least approximately `32px` for compact desktop controls.
    - Associate validation messages with their fields.
    - Make icon controls and complex editor controls accessible by name and keyboard.
    - Preserve a keyboard-accessible alternative for canvas operations.
    
    ## Anti-Patterns
    
    Do not introduce:
    
    - Large areas of blue or decorative AI gradients.
    - Glassmorphism, excessive glow, or pervasive shadows.
    - Oversized marketing typography inside the application workspace.
    - Excessive card nesting or large consumer-style rounded corners.
    - Chat interfaces as the default representation of every AI capability.
    - Decorative robot imagery as the identity of agents.
    - Theme-specific functionality or an unpolished secondary theme.
    - Page-local colors, spacing, or radii that duplicate shared tokens.
    
    ## UI Decision Checklist
    
    Before confirming a UI proposal, verify that it:
    
    - Supports the product character and user task.
    - Uses existing semantic tokens and patterns where possible.
    - Defines both light and dark behavior.
    - Preserves clear information hierarchy at the intended density.
    - Uses blue only for brand, focus, selection, or execution.
    - Includes loading, empty, error, disabled, and long-content states where relevant.
    - Meets keyboard, focus, contrast, reduced-motion, and non-color-cue requirements.
    - Introduces a documented design-system decision before implementation when no existing rule applies.
    
    ## Changelog
    
    ### 2026-09-22 - Paused Workflow Run
    
    - Added `paused` as a warning status with a non-color pause cue, visually distinct from durable `waiting_for_input` and neutral cancelled execution.
    - Added reversible Run pause and resume controls with control-local progress and retained Run-detail cancellation for paused Runs.
    
    ### 2026-09-21 - Conversational turn and queue
    
    - Defined one Agent turn as one identity block containing its own Skill-call rows, and reduced working, cancelled, and failure cues to inline notes without identity marks while keeping them independent status regions.
    - Replaced the discarded-draft behavior with a visible removable message queue for input submitted during a running turn, on the grounds that accepting a keystroke and dropping it reports work the product did not do. This supersedes the 2026-08-27 omission of message queuing.
    - Required a return-to-end control on streaming conversational surfaces whenever the reader is away from the end.
    - Replaced the remaining `System Helper Chat` references with `Chat Bot`.
    
    ### 2026-09-19 - Implementation
    
    - Applied the single-action rule to the surfaces that violated it: the Run pending-action QR and the WeChat Official Account QR now replace themselves, provider testing starts without a second confirmation when the model is resolvable, MCP `Save` absorbs its connection handshake, and the duplicated Codex quota refresh is gone.
    - Recorded two documented exceptions where staleness is not observable: the WeChat ClawBot connection exposes no expiry, and per-account Codex refresh forces an OAuth token refresh rather than re-reading a polled snapshot.
    - Applied the copy standards across both locales, removing restated headings, component-duplicating hints, and the strings that only supported the manual paths now automated.
    
    ### 2026-09-19
    
    - Added the One action per goal and Text earns its place principles, governed in detail by `ui-ux-design/shared/interaction-contract.md` and `ui-ux-design/shared/copy-standards.md`.
    - Prohibited preparation-plus-commit control pairs for a single goal and restricted manual refresh controls to values whose staleness the product cannot observe.
    - Required action progress to appear on the activated control rather than on the surrounding region.
    - Replaced the pending-action panel's QR expiry time and manual refresh with automatic replacement and a status line, keeping `Cancel run` as a separate intent.
    - Required page and section descriptions to justify themselves as a constraint or a scope bound rather than existing by default.
    
    ### 2026-09-18
    
    - Added a neutral per-node `Retry node` recovery control to retryable failed node log entries, scoped to the single retryable entry rather than the Run level.
    - Kept retry non-destructive and non-primary: neutral styling with icon and text cues, a control-local busy state, and preserved failure text until execution continues.
    
    ### 2026-09-16
    
    - Added the pending Workflow authentication panel for login and publish-confirmation QR actions.
    - Kept waiting states amber and neutral, reserving brand blue for the active refresh action and focus.
    
    ### 2026-09-15
    
    - Added the Chat Workflow Mentions pattern for distinguishing Agent turns from published Workflow Runs and for presenting Run progress and Artifacts in the embedded chat transcript.
    
    ### 2026-09-15
    
    - Added ordered node execution logs and directly visible failure reasons to expanded Workflow Run records.
    - Limited Artifact disclosure and its empty state to immutable Workflow versions that contain an Artifact node.
