    # WorkLite UI/UX Design Index
    
    ## Governance
    
    This directory is the source of truth for page structure, shared UI architecture, implementation sequencing, and page-level acceptance criteria. `docs/ui-design-system/README.md` remains the source of truth for visual language.
    
    Interface specifications follow the page structure rather than a flat filename list:
    
    - Route pages use `pages/<area>/<page>/DESIGN.md`.
    - Multi-page flows use `flows/<flow>/DESIGN.md`.
    - Non-route surfaces use `surfaces/<domain>/<surface>/DESIGN.md`.
    - Shared patterns use `shared/<topic>.md`.
    
    Every `DESIGN.md` follows [TEMPLATE.md](TEMPLATE.md) and keeps its sections in that order. A specification records its route or surface scope, design source, implementation locations, purpose, primary task with a declared action budget, layout, per-action interaction contract, per-state behavior, copy inventory, accessibility, and coverage status. New or changed interfaces must update the affected `DESIGN.md` and this index. Do not maintain a parallel page-specification document system.
    
    A page's Coverage Status is a verification result, not a placeholder. It states the date the document was checked against its implementation and lists the differences found.
    
    The router supplies the shell-level pending and error boundaries through `apps/web/src/components/route-boundaries.tsx`, so a page that has not yet resolved shows a content-shaped skeleton and a page that throws shows a recoverable failure instead of an empty region. A page's own `DESIGN.md` states only what it adds beyond those defaults.
    
    ## Shared Specifications
    
    - [Workspace shell](shared/workspace-shell.md)
    - [Page patterns](shared/page-patterns.md)
    - [Shared states](shared/shared-states.md)
    - [Interaction contract](shared/interaction-contract.md)
    - [Copy standards](shared/copy-standards.md)
    - [Responsive behavior](shared/responsive-behavior.md)
    
    ## Page and Surface Specifications
    
    - [Home](pages/home/DESIGN.md), including the server-derived first-use sequence
    - [Workspace Chat Bot](surfaces/workspace/chat-bot/DESIGN.md)
    - Providers: [Model providers and Portkey Gateway](pages/model-providers/DESIGN.md), including the dedicated Codex Account Pool
    - Logs: [Gateway statistics and request logs](pages/logs/DESIGN.md), including the shared time range
    - Workflows: [List](pages/workflows/list/DESIGN.md), [Editor](pages/workflows/editor/DESIGN.md), [Versions](pages/workflows/versions/DESIGN.md)
    - Runs: [Detail](pages/runs/detail/DESIGN.md), [Node logs](surfaces/workflow-run/node-logs/DESIGN.md)
    - Skills: [List](pages/skills/list/DESIGN.md), [Editor](pages/skills/editor/DESIGN.md)
    - MCP servers: [List](pages/mcp-servers/list/DESIGN.md), [Configuration](pages/mcp-servers/configuration/DESIGN.md)
    - Plugins: [List](pages/plugins/list/DESIGN.md), [Configuration](pages/plugins/configuration/DESIGN.md)
    - Artifacts: [Run artifacts](surfaces/workflow-run/artifacts/DESIGN.md), [Details](pages/artifacts/details/DESIGN.md)
    - Settings: [Usage](pages/settings/usage/DESIGN.md), [Audit log](pages/settings/audit-log/DESIGN.md), [Appearance](pages/settings/appearance/DESIGN.md)
    
    ## Route Map
    
    ```text
    /home
    /model-providers
    /logs
    /workflows/{new,:workflowId,:workflowId/versions}
    /skills/{new,:skillId}
    /mcp-servers/{new,:serverId}
    /plugins
    /plugins/:pluginId
    /artifacts/:artifactId
    /runs/:runId
    /settings/{usage,audit-log,appearance}
    ```
    
    The root route opens Home. `/settings/` opens Appearance. Route layouts and redirects are governed by the shared Workspace shell rather than separate page specifications.
    
    There is no `/onboarding` route family. First use is a server-derived sequence inside Home, so a separate browser-state onboarding flow would duplicate it with a less reliable completion signal.
    
    The `/model-providers` page is the top-level Providers destination. It uses page-level tabs for Model Providers and the dedicated Codex Account Pool; the Gateway summary remains on the Model Providers view.
    
    `/logs` is the top-level Logs destination for Gateway transport observability. It uses page-level tabs for Statistics and Requests over one shared time range. Providers configures what the Gateway dispatches to; Logs reads what it did.
    
    `/runs/:runId` is a Run log-reading destination reached from a Workflow's Run records dialog, not a top-level collection. There is no Run list route: Runs are reached through their Workflow. Provider request observability is not a Settings page: `/settings` keeps the WorkLite-owned Usage and Audit Log read models, which are business records over Runs and resource mutations rather than Gateway transport records.
    
    ## Shared Component Inventory
    
    Theme provider and appearance selector; application shell; router pending and error boundaries; sidebar; context bar; personal preferences menu; command menu; shell-level Chat Bot with plugin picker; shared streaming Markdown response renderer; page heading; form controls and messages; status badge; search, filters, object rows and tables; dialogs and sheets; save indicator; inspector; resizable log panel; React Flow workflow graph canvas; workflow run history dialog; run timeline; node log entry with payload and activity disclosure; plugin configuration; viewers for captured request bodies, run output and artifacts; skeletons, errors, offline banner.
    
    Domain-neutral reusable components belong in the shared UI package. Feature composition remains near its feature. Abstract only demonstrated repeated patterns.
    
    ## Implementation Sequence
    
    1. Foundations: semantic dual-theme tokens, initial theme resolution, typography, focus, motion, controls and feedback.
    2. Personal workspace shell: navigation, context bar, menus and responsive behavior.
    3. Home and collections: Home states and shared collection grammar.
    4. Editors and execution: Agent editor, Workflow graph editor, Workflow run history, logs and artifacts.
    5. Integrations and preferences: Skills, MCP servers and Settings.
    
    Every phase includes both themes, keyboard behavior, loading and failure states.

    # WorkLite UI Design System
    
    This document is the source of truth for WorkLite user-interface principles and visual language. `ui-ux-design/README.md` defines page structure, shared UI architecture, implementation sequencing, and page-level acceptance criteria. Every UI proposal and implementation must follow both documents through the UI Change Workflow in `AGENTS_WORKFLOW.md`.
    
    ## Product Character
    
    WorkLite is a professional personal workspace for creating and running AI agents and workflows. Its interface should feel calm, precise, focused, and warm.
    
    The visual direction is inspired by the clarity and efficiency of Linear without copying its brand. WorkLite establishes its own identity through a clear blue accent, execution-oriented interaction patterns, and a consistent visual language for agents, workflows, and runs.
    
    The interface must:
    
    - Prioritize clarity, scanability, and control over decoration.
    - Support efficient, sustained use at moderate-to-high information density.
    - Communicate AI behavior through observable state and feedback rather than visual spectacle.
    - Feel lighter than a traditional enterprise dashboard and more dependable than a novelty AI interface.
    - Treat light and dark modes as equally important, deliberately designed experiences.
    
    The WorkLite brand mark is the orange robot outline in `apps/web/public/brand/worklite-logo.png`. Use the transparent asset through the shared `WorkLiteMark` component for product-owned branding, onboarding, and browser icons. Do not recreate the mark with a substitute icon or apply a background that reduces its legibility.
    
    ## Design Principles
    
    1. **Calm by default.** Neutral surfaces dominate; color is reserved for meaning and action.
    2. **Precise hierarchy.** Typography, spacing, borders, and surface contrast establish structure before shadows or decoration.
    3. **Visible execution.** Users can understand what is running, waiting, completed, or failed.
    4. **Progressive disclosure.** Common actions remain immediate while advanced configuration stays available without overwhelming the primary flow.
    5. **Consistent semantics.** The same color, component, and motion meaning applies throughout the product.
    6. **Accessible interaction.** Keyboard access, visible focus, sufficient contrast, and non-color cues are baseline requirements.
    7. **One action per goal.** A goal has a single activation point. The product does not ask for a step it can take itself, and it recovers from staleness it can observe rather than offering a refresh control. `ui-ux-design/shared/interaction-contract.md` governs the details.
    8. **Text earns its place.** Every string is an action, a state, a constraint, or a recovery. Text that restates a heading, repeats what a component already shows, or explains automation the user cannot act on is removed. `ui-ux-design/shared/copy-standards.md` governs the details.
    
    ## Color System
    
    All implementation colors must be exposed through semantic design tokens. Raw color values must not be repeated in page or feature code.
    
    ### Core Neutrals and Brand
    
    | Token | Light mode | Dark mode | Purpose |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | `background` | `#F7F8FA` | `#101216` | Application background |
    | `surface` | `#FFFFFF` | `#171A20` | Primary content surface |
    | `surface-raised` | `#FFFFFF` | `#1C2027` | Menus, dialogs, and elevated panels |
    | `surface-subtle` | `#F1F3F5` | `#1D2128` | Secondary and selected-neutral surfaces |
    | `text-primary` | `#202126` | `#ECEEF2` | Primary text |
    | `text-secondary` | `#6F747E` | `#989FAA` | Supporting text |
    | `border` | `#E4E6EA` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.09)` | Standard boundaries |
    | `brand` | `#4F6F9F` | `#8EA8CF` | Primary action and brand emphasis |
    | `brand-hover` | `#415F8B` | `#A5B9D7` | Brand control hover |
    | `brand-active` | `#344D73` | `#7893BD` | Brand control active state |
    | `brand-subtle` | `#F1F2F4` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08)` | Selection and restrained emphasis |
    
    The blue brand color is the signature accent. It represents primary action and current focus. It must not be applied indiscriminately to headings, icons, large backgrounds, or ordinary content.
    
    ### Semantic Status Colors
    
    Brand color must not replace status meaning.
    
    - **Running:** blue brand accent plus a text or icon cue.
    - **Success and completed:** green.
    - **Warning and paused:** amber or yellow, visually distinct from brand orange.
    - **Error and failed:** red.
    - **Information:** cool blue.
    - **Queued, cancelled, and inactive:** neutral gray.
    
    Every status must use at least one non-color cue, such as an icon, label, shape, or motion pattern.
    
    ## Themes
    
    WorkLite supports `System`, `Light`, and `Dark` appearance settings. The default is `System`, and an explicit user selection must persist.
    
    - Resolve the theme before initial paint to prevent a light-theme flash.
    - Set the browser `color-scheme` to match the active theme.
    - Theme shared editors, charts, scrollbars, diagrams, illustrations, and floating surfaces with the application.
    - Preserve the same hierarchy and semantic meanings across themes.
    - Do not create dark mode through automatic color inversion.
    - Use subtle transition timing and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
    
    Light mode should feel crisp and open. Dark mode should feel focused and deep, using dark blue-gray rather than pure black.
    
    ## Typography
    
    Use `Inter`, `Geist`, or a compatible modern system sans-serif stack. Use a monospace stack for code, identifiers, variables, model parameters, and logs. Enable tabular numbers for changing metrics and aligned numeric data.
    
    | Role | Size | Weight |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Page title | `24px` | `600` |
    | Section title | `16px` | `600` |
    | Component title | `14px` | `600` |
    | Body | `14px` | `400` |
    | Secondary text | `13px` | `400` |
    | Label | `12px` | `500` |
    | Code and data | `12px` to `13px` | `400` or `500` |
    
    Use concise, direct source copy and preserve the same meaning and tone in every supported locale. Avoid promotional language inside the application. Labels must describe actions or content without relying on placeholder text. Every string must qualify as an action, a state, a constraint, or a recovery under `ui-ux-design/shared/copy-standards.md`; section and page descriptions are optional and exist only to state a constraint or bound a scope. Use the fixed Chinese resource set for all product copy and locale-aware formatting.
    
    ## Spacing and Layout
    
    Use a `4px` base spacing grid.
    
    - Page padding: `24px`.
    - Major section gap: `24px`.
    - Standard panel padding: `16px`.
    - Form-field gap: `16px`.
    - Compact element gap: `8px`.
    - Icon-to-label gap: `6px` to `8px`.
    - Standard control height: `36px`.
    - Compact control height: `28px` to `32px`.
    - Top context bar height: `48px` to `52px`.
    - Primary sidebar width: `220px` to `240px`.
    
    The default application shell uses a stable sidebar, a compact context bar, a primary content region, and an optional contextual inspector. Logs or execution output may use a resizable lower panel when persistent visibility is valuable.
    
    Responsive layouts must preserve task priority. Secondary inspectors may collapse into drawers, while primary actions and current state remain accessible.
    
    ## Shape, Borders, and Elevation
    
    - Small controls: `6px` radius.
    - Buttons and inputs: `8px` radius.
    - Cards and panels: `10px` radius.
    - Dialogs: `12px` radius.
    - Status badges may use a pill shape.
    - Standard borders are `1px`.
    
    Use cards only when content is a distinct object or group. Avoid placing every section in a rounded container. Use shadows primarily for menus, dialogs, drag previews, and genuinely elevated content; prefer surface contrast and borders for ordinary hierarchy.
    
    ## Components
    
    ### Navigation
    
    Keep navigation neutral and grouped by task. Keep the first-level menu concise and direct; related views owned by a destination use stable in-page tabs instead of child sidebar menus. The selected item uses a subtle brand surface, stronger text, and a narrow blue indicator. Do not fill the entire sidebar with brand color.
    
    ### Buttons
    
    - **Primary:** solid blue for the most important action in the current context.
    - **Secondary:** neutral fill or restrained border for supporting actions.
    - **Ghost:** toolbars, inline actions, and low-emphasis controls.
    - **Destructive:** red and reserved for genuinely destructive actions.
    
    Prefer one primary action per visible region. Loading actions must respond immediately and preserve enough label context to explain what is happening. Progress belongs on the activated control, not on the region around it.

    Do not pair a preparation control with a commit control for one goal. When a step is always required before committing, the commit performs it. A manual refresh control is permitted only when the product cannot observe that the value is stale.
    
    ### Forms
    
    Keep labels visible above fields. Placeholder text provides examples only. Place help and validation messages next to the relevant field. Clearly communicate `Saving`, `Saved`, and `Unsaved changes` states. Group advanced configuration and disclose it progressively. Use dedicated editors for prompts, code, and structured data.
    
    Form controls use one crisp boundary at rest. Hover may strengthen that boundary with neutral contrast, while keyboard focus replaces it with the brand-colored boundary and one soft, translucent halo without a gap. Do not stack an outline, border, and offset ring into multiple hard focus borders. Invalid controls use the same treatment with the error color. Disabled controls keep their boundary and surface legible without hover or active feedback.
    
    Apply the same focus language to buttons, selection controls, tabs, menu items, and custom interactive rows. Borderless or inset interactions use one contained focus indicator that follows the component shape. Pointer, hover, active, focus, disabled, and invalid states must remain consistent across local and shared controls.
    
    ### Tables and Lists
    
    Prefer compact lists or tables for agents, workflows, and runs when scanability matters. Use row heights around `44px` to `48px`, subdued headers, predictable sorting, visible filter chips, and on-hover secondary actions. Keep status near the object name. Truncated identifiers must be copyable. Distinguish an empty collection from a filtered result with no matches.
    
    ### Overlays and Feedback
    
    Dialogs are for focused decisions, not routine navigation. Toasts communicate transient outcomes; important results and errors must remain visible in the page. Error feedback should explain the problem and provide a recovery action when one exists.
    
    ### Icons
    
    Use Lucide icons consistently, normally at `16px` and at `18px` in primary navigation. Icon-only controls require an accessible name, tooltip, and an adequate interaction target. Emoji are not product icons.
    
    ## Product-Specific Patterns
    
    ### Chat Workflow Mentions
    
    The embedded Chat Bot mention menu supports published Workflows only. Keep the selected Workflow chip compact and removable so users understand that the mention creates a Workflow Run. Workflow progress uses the existing queued, running, completed, failed, and cancelled status semantics, with text and icon cues in addition to color. Successful Workflow Artifacts appear as restrained transcript cards with a direct details action. Draft Workflows are not listed as runnable mentions.
    
    ### Agents
    
    Present agents as configurable work units, not cartoon characters. Identity comes from a restrained geometric symbol or letter mark, name, responsibility, model, available skills or tools, ownership, version, and recent run state.
    
    ### AI Response Content
    
    Use one shared streaming Markdown renderer for model-generated text across Chat Bot and future Agent response surfaces. It must handle incomplete Markdown during streaming, GitHub Flavored Markdown, long words, tables, links, lists, quotations, and fenced code without executing embedded HTML or scripts. Product styling wraps the renderer and uses semantic tokens in both themes; transport parsing and conversation state do not belong inside the renderer.
    
    In conversational layouts, user messages align to the right in compact neutral bubbles and remain plain text. Agent responses align to the left with a wider, unframed reading column so structured output remains scannable. Alignment, accessible labels, and optional identity marks distinguish speakers without relying on color. Streaming updates follow the end only when the reader was already at the end, and a return-to-end control appears while they are not.
    
    One Agent turn is one block with one identity mark, however many message segments and Skill calls it contains. Its segments and Skill-call rows share that block's content column, so a turn that answers, runs a script, and answers again reads as one reply instead of as several speakers. Working, cancelled, and failure cues render as inline notes without identity marks, because a status is not a speaker; they remain independent status regions for assistive technology.
    
    Create a Chat Bot response placeholder in the transcript as soon as a turn starts. Show restrained inline progress there instead of replacing or disabling the composer. While a turn is running, keep the draft input editable and replace the send control with a familiar square Stop icon; stopping is a neutral execution control rather than a destructive action. Preserve the draft after completion or cancellation, and use text plus icon cues for working and cancelled states.
    
    A message submitted during a running turn joins a visible removable queue and sends when that turn completes. A composer that accepts a keystroke and silently discards it reports work the product did not do, so queuing is the honest behavior for input the reader has already committed. Queue rows are restrained neutral transcript entries with a count and a per-row remove control, not a second execution surface. The queue pauses in place — keeping every entry and its order — when the turn fails, when the reader stops it, and while a clarification question is pending, and it says that it is paused.
    
    Present inline Skill calls as compact disclosure rows by default. The collapsed row keeps the Skill identity, script name, execution status, and exit code visible without allowing arguments, host details, or raw output to dominate the transcript. A keyboard-accessible disclosure control reveals the complete metadata, warning, and a height-bounded internally scrollable output region. Failed calls remain collapsed unless the user opens them.
    
    Treat `@` selection in the Chat Bot composer as structured dispatch, not decorated message text. Opening `@` presents a searchable keyboard-accessible published Workflow menu with pointer selection, arrow navigation, `Enter`, and `Escape`. A selection becomes one removable mention token before the task text inside the same bordered input surface; it must not appear as a separate adjacent field or region. Only one Workflow may be selected for a task, and its identity remains visible until dispatch or removal. The token and task text may wrap together within that shared surface on narrow screens. Chat Bot does not expose Agent mentions or child sessions.
    
    ### Workflow Editor
    
    - Represent workflows on a focused React Flow node canvas with explicit input and output handles, directional edges, and persisted spatial layout.
    - Use a canvas with one right-side contextual panel. The panel shows the searchable node palette when nothing is selected and replaces it with the selected node or edge inspector.
    - Keep nodes visually consistent and expose essential node-owned parameters, including editable Text content, without requiring the inspector for common work.
    - Add nodes through the searchable palette at a predictable viewport position and allow direct node dragging for spatial organization.
    - Provide familiar icon controls for zoom in, zoom out, fit view, and deletion.
    - Keep edge direction and handle compatibility visible through shape, persistent port labels, and valid or invalid interaction state rather than color alone.
    - Preserve a keyboard-accessible inspector path for reviewing configuration and removing selected nodes or edges, with an explicit return to the node palette.
    - Keep the contextual panel available at every breakpoint; collapse the combined palette and inspector to one drawer or bottom sheet when the layout cannot support a side panel.
    - Use blue borders or indicators for the selected and currently executing node or edge. Selection belongs to the graph and must remain synchronized with contextual panel content and keyboard focus.
    - Represent successful and failed states through compact green or red markers rather than filling the whole node.
    - Render edges with restrained neutral strokes and reserve stronger treatment for selection and execution.
    - Present AI-assisted edits in a side panel and make proposed structured operations understandable and reviewable.
    - Group workflow-level settings into General, Inputs, Execution, and Versioning sections, with advanced fields disclosed progressively.
    
    Persimmon progression through the graph is a distinctive WorkLite motif. It communicates selection and active execution while neutral surfaces and edges keep dense workflows readable. The initial graph supports acyclic data fan-out; conditional branches, joins, loops, and parallel execution remain outside the current product scope.
    
    ### Runs and Logs
    
    Workflow List exposes Run records through a per-Workflow dialog. Use the following canonical run labels: `Queued`, `Running`, `Waiting for input`, `Completed`, `Failed`, and `Cancelled`.
    
    A Run waiting on a human-gated browser action presents a compact amber pending-action panel before its node logs. The panel names the required action and shows the QR image. An expired code is replaced automatically, so the panel shows neither an expiry time nor an instruction to refresh: during replacement the current image dims and a status line reports that a new code is arriving. `Cancel run` remains, because abandoning the Run is a separate intent rather than a recovery from staleness. Authentication state is communicated with text and icon cues; the QR is not the only explanation. Completion updates through the existing Run event stream and does not require a separate “I scanned it” control.
    
    Show the current step and continuing progress for long operations. Expanded Workflow Run records present ordered node execution logs with node identity, status, timing, duration, and retry context. Failed Runs surface the credential-safe failure reason before the log list and repeat it on the failed node entry. Append logs without forcing disruptive scrolling. Use monospace text for identifiers and raw output, and allow users to distinguish timestamps, severity, source, and content. Successful completion should be clear but restrained; failure must include context and a next step where possible. Artifact disclosure is absent when the immutable Workflow version has no Artifact node; an empty Artifact state is reserved for eligible versions that produced none.
    
    Failure is the one node log state that carries a recovery action. When the server reports a failed node entry as retryable, that entry offers a single neutral secondary `Retry node` control beside its failure reason. Retry is an ordinary execution control, not a destructive or primary action, so it uses neutral styling with an icon and text label rather than brand fill or red. Only the retryable entry exposes it; other failed, cancelled, and successful entries show none, and the control never appears at the Run level where it could be mistaken for rerunning the whole Workflow. Activating it shows a local busy state on that control alone, leaves the surrounding log list in place, and keeps any failure text visible until the Run event stream replaces it with continued execution. A retry that the server rejects preserves the original failure reason and explains the rejection in the same entry.
    
    ## Motion
    
    - Hover feedback: approximately `120ms`.
    - Tooltips and menus: approximately `150ms`.
    - Panels and dialogs: `180ms` to `220ms`.
    - Prefer natural ease-out curves.
    - Avoid decorative page transitions, bounce effects, strong zoom, and large animated gradients.
    - Use motion to clarify execution, selection, expansion, and state changes.
    - Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` and retain static state cues when animation is disabled.
    
    ## Accessibility
    
    - Meet WCAG AA contrast for standard text and essential controls.
    - Keep a visible keyboard focus ring in both themes.
    - Do not communicate state using color alone.
    - Provide interaction targets of at least approximately `32px` for compact desktop controls.
    - Associate validation messages with their fields.
    - Make icon controls and complex editor controls accessible by name and keyboard.
    - Preserve a keyboard-accessible alternative for canvas operations.
    
    ## Anti-Patterns
    
    Do not introduce:
    
    - Large areas of blue or decorative AI gradients.
    - Glassmorphism, excessive glow, or pervasive shadows.
    - Oversized marketing typography inside the application workspace.
    - Excessive card nesting or large consumer-style rounded corners.
    - Chat interfaces as the default representation of every AI capability.
    - Decorative robot imagery as the identity of agents.
    - Theme-specific functionality or an unpolished secondary theme.
    - Page-local colors, spacing, or radii that duplicate shared tokens.
    
    ## UI Decision Checklist
    
    Before confirming a UI proposal, verify that it:
    
    - Supports the product character and user task.
    - Uses existing semantic tokens and patterns where possible.
    - Defines both light and dark behavior.
    - Preserves clear information hierarchy at the intended density.
    - Uses blue only for brand, focus, selection, or execution.
    - Includes loading, empty, error, disabled, and long-content states where relevant.
    - Meets keyboard, focus, contrast, reduced-motion, and non-color-cue requirements.
    - Introduces a documented design-system decision before implementation when no existing rule applies.

    # WorkLite UI/UX Design Index
    
    ## Governance
    
    This directory is the source of truth for page structure, shared UI architecture, implementation sequencing, and page-level acceptance criteria. `docs/ui-design-system/README.md` remains the source of truth for visual language.
    
    Interface specifications follow the page structure rather than a flat filename list:
    
    - Route pages use `pages/<area>/<page>/DESIGN.md`.
    - Multi-page flows use `flows/<flow>/DESIGN.md`.
    - Non-route surfaces use `surfaces/<domain>/<surface>/DESIGN.md`.
    - Shared patterns use `shared/<topic>.md`.
    
    Every `DESIGN.md` follows [TEMPLATE.md](TEMPLATE.md) and keeps its sections in that order. A specification records its route or surface scope, design source, implementation locations, purpose, primary task with a declared action budget, layout, per-action interaction contract, per-state behavior, copy inventory, accessibility, and coverage status. New or changed interfaces must update the affected `DESIGN.md` and this index. Do not maintain a parallel page-specification document system.
    
    A page's Coverage Status is a verification result, not a placeholder. It states the date the document was checked against its implementation and lists the differences found.
    
    The router supplies the shell-level pending and error boundaries through `apps/web/src/components/route-boundaries.tsx`, so a page that has not yet resolved shows a content-shaped skeleton and a page that throws shows a recoverable failure instead of an empty region. A page's own `DESIGN.md` states only what it adds beyond those defaults.
    
    ## Shared Specifications
    
    - [Workspace shell](shared/workspace-shell.md)
    - [Page patterns](shared/page-patterns.md)
    - [Shared states](shared/shared-states.md)
    - [Interaction contract](shared/interaction-contract.md)
    - [Copy standards](shared/copy-standards.md)
    - [Responsive behavior](shared/responsive-behavior.md)
    
    ## Page and Surface Specifications
    
    - [Home](pages/home/DESIGN.md), including the server-derived first-use sequence
    - [Workspace Chat Bot](surfaces/workspace/chat-bot/DESIGN.md)
    - Providers: [Model providers and Portkey Gateway](pages/model-providers/DESIGN.md), including the dedicated Codex Account Pool
    - Logs: [Gateway statistics and request logs](pages/logs/DESIGN.md), including the shared time range
    - Workflows: [List](pages/workflows/list/DESIGN.md), [Editor](pages/workflows/editor/DESIGN.md), [Versions](pages/workflows/versions/DESIGN.md)
    - Runs: [Detail](pages/runs/detail/DESIGN.md), [Node logs](surfaces/workflow-run/node-logs/DESIGN.md)
    - Skills: [List](pages/skills/list/DESIGN.md), [Editor](pages/skills/editor/DESIGN.md)
    - MCP servers: [List](pages/mcp-servers/list/DESIGN.md), [Configuration](pages/mcp-servers/configuration/DESIGN.md)
    - Plugins: [List](pages/plugins/list/DESIGN.md), [Configuration](pages/plugins/configuration/DESIGN.md)
    - Artifacts: [Run artifacts](surfaces/workflow-run/artifacts/DESIGN.md), [Details](pages/artifacts/details/DESIGN.md)
    - Settings: [Usage](pages/settings/usage/DESIGN.md), [Audit log](pages/settings/audit-log/DESIGN.md), [Appearance](pages/settings/appearance/DESIGN.md)
    
    ## Route Map
    
    ```text
    /home
    /model-providers
    /logs
    /workflows/{new,:workflowId,:workflowId/versions}
    /skills/{new,:skillId}
    /mcp-servers/{new,:serverId}
    /plugins
    /plugins/:pluginId
    /artifacts/:artifactId
    /runs/:runId
    /settings/{usage,audit-log,appearance}
    ```
    
    The root route opens Home. `/settings/` opens Appearance. Route layouts and redirects are governed by the shared Workspace shell rather than separate page specifications.
    
    There is no `/onboarding` route family. First use is a server-derived sequence inside Home, so a separate browser-state onboarding flow would duplicate it with a less reliable completion signal.
    
    The `/model-providers` page is the top-level Providers destination. It uses page-level tabs for Model Providers and the dedicated Codex Account Pool; the Gateway summary remains on the Model Providers view.
    
    `/logs` is the top-level Logs destination for Gateway transport observability. It uses page-level tabs for Statistics and Requests over one shared time range. Providers configures what the Gateway dispatches to; Logs reads what it did.
    
    `/runs/:runId` is a Run log-reading destination reached from a Workflow's Run records dialog, not a top-level collection. There is no Run list route: Runs are reached through their Workflow. Provider request observability is not a Settings page: `/settings` keeps the WorkLite-owned Usage and Audit Log read models, which are business records over Runs and resource mutations rather than Gateway transport records.
    
    ## Shared Component Inventory
    
    Theme provider and appearance selector; application shell; router pending and error boundaries; sidebar; context bar; personal preferences menu; command menu; shell-level Chat Bot with plugin picker; shared streaming Markdown response renderer; page heading; form controls and messages; status badge; search, filters, object rows and tables; dialogs and sheets; save indicator; inspector; resizable log panel; React Flow workflow graph canvas; workflow run history dialog; run timeline; node log entry with payload and activity disclosure; plugin configuration; viewers for captured request bodies, run output and artifacts; skeletons, errors, offline banner.
    
    Domain-neutral reusable components belong in the shared UI package. Feature composition remains near its feature. Abstract only demonstrated repeated patterns.
    
    ## Implementation Sequence
    
    1. Foundations: semantic dual-theme tokens, initial theme resolution, typography, focus, motion, controls and feedback.
    2. Personal workspace shell: navigation, context bar, menus and responsive behavior.
    3. Home and collections: Home states and shared collection grammar.
    4. Editors and execution: Agent editor, Workflow graph editor, Workflow run history, logs and artifacts.
    5. Integrations and preferences: Skills, MCP servers and Settings.
    
    Every phase includes both themes, keyboard behavior, loading and failure states.

    Do not pair a preparation control with a commit control for one goal. When a step is always required before committing, the commit performs it. A manual refresh control is permitted only when the product cannot observe that the value is stale.
    
    ### Forms
    
    Keep labels visible above fields. Placeholder text provides examples only. Place help and validation messages next to the relevant field. Clearly communicate `Saving`, `Saved`, and `Unsaved changes` states. Group advanced configuration and disclose it progressively. Use dedicated editors for prompts, code, and structured data.
    
    Form controls use one crisp boundary at rest. Hover may strengthen that boundary with neutral contrast, while keyboard focus replaces it with the brand-colored boundary and one soft, translucent halo without a gap. Do not stack an outline, border, and offset ring into multiple hard focus borders. Invalid controls use the same treatment with the error color. Disabled controls keep their boundary and surface legible without hover or active feedback.
    
    Apply the same focus language to buttons, selection controls, tabs, menu items, and custom interactive rows. Borderless or inset interactions use one contained focus indicator that follows the component shape. Pointer, hover, active, focus, disabled, and invalid states must remain consistent across local and shared controls.
    
    ### Tables and Lists
    
    Prefer compact lists or tables for agents, workflows, and runs when scanability matters. Use row heights around `44px` to `48px`, subdued headers, predictable sorting, visible filter chips, and on-hover secondary actions. Keep status near the object name. Truncated identifiers must be copyable. Distinguish an empty collection from a filtered result with no matches.
    
    ### Overlays and Feedback
    
    Dialogs are for focused decisions, not routine navigation. Toasts communicate transient outcomes; important results and errors must remain visible in the page. Error feedback should explain the problem and provide a recovery action when one exists.
    
    ### Icons
    
    Use Lucide icons consistently, normally at `16px` and at `18px` in primary navigation. Icon-only controls require an accessible name, tooltip, and an adequate interaction target. Emoji are not product icons.
    
    ## Product-Specific Patterns
    
    ### Chat Workflow Mentions
    
    The embedded Chat Bot mention menu supports published Workflows only. Keep the selected Workflow chip compact and removable so users understand that the mention creates a Workflow Run. Workflow progress uses the existing queued, running, completed, failed, and cancelled status semantics, with text and icon cues in addition to color. Successful Workflow Artifacts appear as restrained transcript cards with a direct details action. Draft Workflows are not listed as runnable mentions.
    
    ### Agents
    
    Present agents as configurable work units, not cartoon characters. Identity comes from a restrained geometric symbol or letter mark, name, responsibility, model, available skills or tools, ownership, version, and recent run state.
    
    ### AI Response Content
    
    Use one shared streaming Markdown renderer for model-generated text across Chat Bot and future Agent response surfaces. It must handle incomplete Markdown during streaming, GitHub Flavored Markdown, long words, tables, links, lists, quotations, and fenced code without executing embedded HTML or scripts. Product styling wraps the renderer and uses semantic tokens in both themes; transport parsing and conversation state do not belong inside the renderer.
    
    In conversational layouts, user messages align to the right in compact neutral bubbles and remain plain text. Agent responses align to the left with a wider, unframed reading column so structured output remains scannable. Alignment, accessible labels, and optional identity marks distinguish speakers without relying on color. Streaming updates follow the end only when the reader was already at the end, and a return-to-end control appears while they are not.
    
    One Agent turn is one block with one identity mark, however many message segments and Skill calls it contains. Its segments and Skill-call rows share that block's content column, so a turn that answers, runs a script, and answers again reads as one reply instead of as several speakers. Working, cancelled, and failure cues render as inline notes without identity marks, because a status is not a speaker; they remain independent status regions for assistive technology.
    
    Create a Chat Bot response placeholder in the transcript as soon as a turn starts. Show restrained inline progress there instead of replacing or disabling the composer. While a turn is running, keep the draft input editable and replace the send control with a familiar square Stop icon; stopping is a neutral execution control rather than a destructive action. Preserve the draft after completion or cancellation, and use text plus icon cues for working and cancelled states.
    
    A message submitted during a running turn joins a visible removable queue and sends when that turn completes. A composer that accepts a keystroke and silently discards it reports work the product did not do, so queuing is the honest behavior for input the reader has already committed. Queue rows are restrained neutral transcript entries with a count and a per-row remove control, not a second execution surface. The queue pauses in place — keeping every entry and its order — when the turn fails, when the reader stops it, and while a clarification question is pending, and it says that it is paused.
    
    Present inline Skill calls as compact disclosure rows by default. The collapsed row keeps the Skill identity, script name, execution status, and exit code visible without allowing arguments, host details, or raw output to dominate the transcript. A keyboard-accessible disclosure control reveals the complete metadata, warning, and a height-bounded internally scrollable output region. Failed calls remain collapsed unless the user opens them.
    
    Treat `@` selection in the Chat Bot composer as structured dispatch, not decorated message text. Opening `@` presents a searchable keyboard-accessible published Workflow menu with pointer selection, arrow navigation, `Enter`, and `Escape`. A selection becomes one removable mention token before the task text inside the same bordered input surface; it must not appear as a separate adjacent field or region. Only one Workflow may be selected for a task, and its identity remains visible until dispatch or removal. The token and task text may wrap together within that shared surface on narrow screens. Chat Bot does not expose Agent mentions or child sessions.
    
    ### Workflow Editor
    
    - Represent workflows on a focused React Flow node canvas with explicit input and output handles, directional edges, and persisted spatial layout.
    - Use a canvas with one right-side contextual panel. The panel shows the searchable node palette when nothing is selected and replaces it with the selected node or edge inspector.
    - Keep nodes visually consistent and expose essential node-owned parameters, including editable Text content, without requiring the inspector for common work.
    - Add nodes through the searchable palette at a predictable viewport position and allow direct node dragging for spatial organization.
    - Provide familiar icon controls for zoom in, zoom out, fit view, and deletion.
    - Keep edge direction and handle compatibility visible through shape, persistent port labels, and valid or invalid interaction state rather than color alone.
    - Preserve a keyboard-accessible inspector path for reviewing configuration and removing selected nodes or edges, with an explicit return to the node palette.
    - Keep the contextual panel available at every breakpoint; collapse the combined palette and inspector to one drawer or bottom sheet when the layout cannot support a side panel.
    - Use blue borders or indicators for the selected and currently executing node or edge. Selection belongs to the graph and must remain synchronized with contextual panel content and keyboard focus.
    - Represent successful and failed states through compact green or red markers rather than filling the whole node.
    - Render edges with restrained neutral strokes and reserve stronger treatment for selection and execution.
    - Present AI-assisted edits in a side panel and make proposed structured operations understandable and reviewable.
    - Group workflow-level settings into General, Inputs, Execution, and Versioning sections, with advanced fields disclosed progressively.
    
    Persimmon progression through the graph is a distinctive WorkLite motif. It communicates selection and active execution while neutral surfaces and edges keep dense workflows readable. The initial graph supports acyclic data fan-out; conditional branches, joins, loops, and parallel execution remain outside the current product scope.
    
    ### Runs and Logs
    
    Workflow List exposes Run records through a per-Workflow dialog. Use the following canonical run labels: `Queued`, `Running`, `Waiting for input`, `Completed`, `Failed`, and `Cancelled`.
    
    A Run waiting on a human-gated browser action presents a compact amber pending-action panel before its node logs. The panel names the required action and shows the QR image. An expired code is replaced automatically, so the panel shows neither an expiry time nor an instruction to refresh: during replacement the current image dims and a status line reports that a new code is arriving. `Cancel run` remains, because abandoning the Run is a separate intent rather than a recovery from staleness. Authentication state is communicated with text and icon cues; the QR is not the only explanation. Completion updates through the existing Run event stream and does not require a separate “I scanned it” control.
    
    Show the current step and continuing progress for long operations. Expanded Workflow Run records present ordered node execution logs with node identity, status, timing, duration, and retry context. Failed Runs surface the credential-safe failure reason before the log list and repeat it on the failed node entry. Append logs without forcing disruptive scrolling. Use monospace text for identifiers and raw output, and allow users to distinguish timestamps, severity, source, and content. Successful completion should be clear but restrained; failure must include context and a next step where possible. Artifact disclosure is absent when the immutable Workflow version has no Artifact node; an empty Artifact state is reserved for eligible versions that produced none.
    
    Failure is the one node log state that carries a recovery action. When the server reports a failed node entry as retryable, that entry offers a single neutral secondary `Retry node` control beside its failure reason. Retry is an ordinary execution control, not a destructive or primary action, so it uses neutral styling with an icon and text label rather than brand fill or red. Only the retryable entry exposes it; other failed, cancelled, and successful entries show none, and the control never appears at the Run level where it could be mistaken for rerunning the whole Workflow. Activating it shows a local busy state on that control alone, leaves the surrounding log list in place, and keeps any failure text visible until the Run event stream replaces it with continued execution. A retry that the server rejects preserves the original failure reason and explains the rejection in the same entry.
    
    ## Motion
    
    - Hover feedback: approximately `120ms`.
    - Tooltips and menus: approximately `150ms`.
    - Panels and dialogs: `180ms` to `220ms`.
    - Prefer natural ease-out curves.
    - Avoid decorative page transitions, bounce effects, strong zoom, and large animated gradients.
    - Use motion to clarify execution, selection, expansion, and state changes.
    - Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` and retain static state cues when animation is disabled.
    
    ## Accessibility
    
    - Meet WCAG AA contrast for standard text and essential controls.
    - Keep a visible keyboard focus ring in both themes.
    - Do not communicate state using color alone.
    - Provide interaction targets of at least approximately `32px` for compact desktop controls.
    - Associate validation messages with their fields.
    - Make icon controls and complex editor controls accessible by name and keyboard.
    - Preserve a keyboard-accessible alternative for canvas operations.
    
    ## Anti-Patterns
    
    Do not introduce:
    
    - Large areas of blue or decorative AI gradients.
    - Glassmorphism, excessive glow, or pervasive shadows.
    - Oversized marketing typography inside the application workspace.
    - Excessive card nesting or large consumer-style rounded corners.
    - Chat interfaces as the default representation of every AI capability.
    - Decorative robot imagery as the identity of agents.
    - Theme-specific functionality or an unpolished secondary theme.
    - Page-local colors, spacing, or radii that duplicate shared tokens.
    
    ## UI Decision Checklist
    
    Before confirming a UI proposal, verify that it:
    
    - Supports the product character and user task.
    - Uses existing semantic tokens and patterns where possible.
    - Defines both light and dark behavior.
    - Preserves clear information hierarchy at the intended density.
    - Uses blue only for brand, focus, selection, or execution.
    - Includes loading, empty, error, disabled, and long-content states where relevant.
    - Meets keyboard, focus, contrast, reduced-motion, and non-color-cue requirements.

    # WorkLite UI/UX Design Index
    
    ## Governance
    
    This directory is the source of truth for page structure, shared UI architecture, implementation sequencing, and page-level acceptance criteria. `docs/ui-design-system/README.md` remains the source of truth for visual language.
    
    Interface specifications follow the page structure rather than a flat filename list:
    
    - Route pages use `pages/<area>/<page>/DESIGN.md`.
    - Multi-page flows use `flows/<flow>/DESIGN.md`.
    - Non-route surfaces use `surfaces/<domain>/<surface>/DESIGN.md`.
    - Shared patterns use `shared/<topic>.md`.
    
    Every `DESIGN.md` follows [TEMPLATE.md](TEMPLATE.md) and keeps its sections in that order. A specification records its route or surface scope, design source, implementation locations, purpose, primary task with a declared action budget, layout, per-action interaction contract, per-state behavior, copy inventory, accessibility, and coverage status. New or changed interfaces must update the affected `DESIGN.md` and this index. Do not maintain a parallel page-specification document system.
    
    A page's Coverage Status is a verification result, not a placeholder. It states the date the document was checked against its implementation and lists the differences found.
    
    The router supplies the shell-level pending and error boundaries through `apps/web/src/components/route-boundaries.tsx`, so a page that has not yet resolved shows a content-shaped skeleton and a page that throws shows a recoverable failure instead of an empty region. A page's own `DESIGN.md` states only what it adds beyond those defaults.
    
    ## Shared Specifications
    
    - [Workspace shell](shared/workspace-shell.md)
    - [Page patterns](shared/page-patterns.md)
    - [Shared states](shared/shared-states.md)
    - [Interaction contract](shared/interaction-contract.md)
    - [Copy standards](shared/copy-standards.md)
    - [Responsive behavior](shared/responsive-behavior.md)
    
    ## Page and Surface Specifications
    
    - [Home](pages/home/DESIGN.md), including the server-derived first-use sequence
    - [Workspace Chat Bot](surfaces/workspace/chat-bot/DESIGN.md)
    - Providers: [Model providers and Portkey Gateway](pages/model-providers/DESIGN.md), including the dedicated Codex Account Pool
    - Logs: [Gateway statistics and request logs](pages/logs/DESIGN.md), including the shared time range
    - Workflows: [List](pages/workflows/list/DESIGN.md), [Editor](pages/workflows/editor/DESIGN.md), [Versions](pages/workflows/versions/DESIGN.md)
    - Runs: [Detail](pages/runs/detail/DESIGN.md), [Node logs](surfaces/workflow-run/node-logs/DESIGN.md)
    - Skills: [List](pages/skills/list/DESIGN.md), [Editor](pages/skills/editor/DESIGN.md)
    - MCP servers: [List](pages/mcp-servers/list/DESIGN.md), [Configuration](pages/mcp-servers/configuration/DESIGN.md)
    - Plugins: [List](pages/plugins/list/DESIGN.md), [Configuration](pages/plugins/configuration/DESIGN.md)
    - Artifacts: [Run artifacts](surfaces/workflow-run/artifacts/DESIGN.md), [Details](pages/artifacts/details/DESIGN.md)
    - Settings: [Usage](pages/settings/usage/DESIGN.md), [Audit log](pages/settings/audit-log/DESIGN.md), [Appearance](pages/settings/appearance/DESIGN.md)
    
    ## Route Map
    
    ```text
    /home
    /model-providers
    /logs
    /workflows/{new,:workflowId,:workflowId/versions}
    /skills/{new,:skillId}
    /mcp-servers/{new,:serverId}
    /plugins
    /plugins/:pluginId
    /artifacts/:artifactId
    /runs/:runId
    /settings/{usage,audit-log,appearance}
    ```
    
    The root route opens Home. `/settings/` opens Appearance. Route layouts and redirects are governed by the shared Workspace shell rather than separate page specifications.
    
    There is no `/onboarding` route family. First use is a server-derived sequence inside Home, so a separate browser-state onboarding flow would duplicate it with a less reliable completion signal.
    
    The `/model-providers` page is the top-level Providers destination. It uses page-level tabs for Model Providers and the dedicated Codex Account Pool; the Gateway summary remains on the Model Providers view.
    
    `/logs` is the top-level Logs destination for Gateway transport observability. It uses page-level tabs for Statistics and Requests over one shared time range. Providers configures what the Gateway dispatches to; Logs reads what it did.
    
    `/runs/:runId` is a Run log-reading destination reached from a Workflow's Run records dialog, not a top-level collection. There is no Run list route: Runs are reached through their Workflow. Provider request observability is not a Settings page: `/settings` keeps the WorkLite-owned Usage and Audit Log read models, which are business records over Runs and resource mutations rather than Gateway transport records.
    
    ## Shared Component Inventory
    
    Theme provider and appearance selector; application shell; router pending and error boundaries; sidebar; context bar; personal preferences menu; command menu; shell-level Chat Bot with plugin picker; shared streaming Markdown response renderer; page heading; form controls and messages; status badge; search, filters, object rows and tables; dialogs and sheets; save indicator; inspector; resizable log panel; React Flow workflow graph canvas; workflow run history dialog; run timeline; node log entry with payload and activity disclosure; plugin configuration; viewers for captured request bodies, run output and artifacts; skeletons, errors, offline banner.
    
    Domain-neutral reusable components belong in the shared UI package. Feature composition remains near its feature. Abstract only demonstrated repeated patterns.
    
    ## Implementation Sequence
    
    1. Foundations: semantic dual-theme tokens, initial theme resolution, typography, focus, motion, controls and feedback.
    2. Personal workspace shell: navigation, context bar, menus and responsive behavior.
    3. Home and collections: Home states and shared collection grammar.
    4. Editors and execution: Agent editor, Workflow graph editor, Workflow run history, logs and artifacts.
    5. Integrations and preferences: Skills, MCP servers and Settings.
    
    Every phase includes both themes, keyboard behavior, loading and failure states.

    # Workspace Shell
    
    ## Structure
    
    Use a persistent `232px` sidebar, a `52px` context bar, fluid main content, an optional `360px` inspector, and an optional resizable bottom run panel. The sidebar collapses to `56px` only between `768px` and `1023px`.
    
    Primary navigation is grouped and single-level. It contains six direct destinations: **Workspace** contains `Home` and `Workflows`; **Capabilities** contains `Plugins`, with `Skills` and `MCP Servers` available as capability sub-navigation; **Configuration** contains `Providers`, `Logs`, and `Settings`.
    
    Providers owns the Model Providers, Portkey Gateway summary, and Codex account views in one page context. Logs owns Gateway transport observability: request statistics and captured request details over one shared time range. The two are separate destinations because one configures upstream dispatch and the other reads what was dispatched. Skills and MCP Servers are the capability destinations; standalone Agents have no page-level destination; Plugins remains its peer. Workflow List owns execution-history access through its per-Workflow Run records dialog, whose expanded Run rows expose Artifacts inline; direct Artifact details provide deeper inspection. At `1024px` and above, the expanded sidebar shows group labels and all destinations. From `768px` to `1023px`, the compact icon rail uses group separators, direct icons, and tooltips. The mobile navigation drawer uses the same grouped destinations. Usage, audit log, and appearance are reached from Settings. Chat Bot is available throughout the workspace shell, presented prominently on Home and as a floating control elsewhere. Counts indicate actionable state only. The WorkLite mark is at the top and the personal preferences menu is at the bottom. The expanded preferences control keeps its neutral status label and shows the application version as a right-aligned monospace label; the compact rail exposes the same version inside the preferences menu.
    
    The selected navigation item uses `brand-subtle`, primary text, and a narrow brand indicator. The selected resource link represents its route family: Skills and MCP Server routes select Capabilities, while Artifact routes select Workflows. Personal preferences stay in the bottom menu.
    
    ## Context Bar
    
    Place navigation and breadcrumb context on the left. Place command search, state, secondary actions, and one primary page action on the right. Move low-frequency actions to overflow and never duplicate the primary action in the page heading.
    
    ## Panels
    
    The inspector opens only for selected contextual content, keeps its header and essential actions available, scrolls internally, and does not discard unsaved work when closed. It may expand to `440px` for structured configuration.
    
    The workspace shell owns the active Chat Bot execution identifier, the transient composer draft, and the pending message queue. Published Workflows are selected per message with `@` mentions and create normal Workflow Runs that remain independent from the Chat Bot session. Messages, plugin process state, script requests, automatic execution state, and results remain server-owned. Page navigation closes the visible conversation without cancelling work; a browser reload fetches the active execution identifier and selected target saved by the browser, and drops the queue, which is session state rather than persisted intent.
    
    Place the Chat Bot interaction surface at the bottom of the content region on every workspace page. Home keeps the single-line input visible by default. Other pages show only a draggable floating Chat Bot icon in the lower-right corner by default; clicking it opens the same raised conversation panel above the current page and focuses the input. Clicking outside an expanded Chat surface closes it while Chat-owned popup menus remain usable. Keep the icon inside the viewport safe area and preserve a keyboard-accessible open action without a visible Tooltip. Center the complete expanded surface and cap it at `1200px`. With a bound provider the expanded composer contains the single-line input and one stable icon-button target without a repeated visible Chat Bot title; the target shows Send while idle and Stop while the active turn is running. The input remains editable in both states. Without a bound provider the expanded surface contains its inline Chat Bot configuration panel instead of an input or send control. Home and other pages use the same personal session, expanded dimensions, and compact execution summary.
    
    The bottom panel defaults to about `240px`, resizes, and collapses to a status strip. Closing hides but never cancels a run. Logs distinguish timestamp, severity, source and content, and auto-follow only while the user is at the stream end.
    
    ## Route Boundaries
    
    The root route owns the pending and error boundaries for every page. An unresolved route renders a content-shaped skeleton inside the stable shell rather than an empty content region; a route that throws renders a recoverable failure whose retry invalidates the router. The sidebar, context bar, and Chat surface remain mounted through both states, so a slow or failed page never collapses the workspace.
    
    There is no separate first-use route family. Home derives first-use completion from persisted server resources, so the shell has no onboarding layout branch and no browser-state onboarding step.
    
    ## Command and User Menus
    
    `Command+K` or `Control+K` opens grouped search, recent destinations, navigation and safe creation commands. Destructive actions are excluded. Opening Chat Bot through the command menu changes the shell-owned conversation state through typed route search and must not rely on an ignored URL flag. The user menu contains the personal workspace identity, Appearance, Keyboard shortcuts, and the application version. Appearance includes the personal theme and language preferences.

    # Page Patterns
    
    ## Families
    
    - Collections: title, optional description, search, filters, active chips, and right-aligned primary actions in the toolbar directly above the compact table or object list.
    - Details: durable summary, metadata, relationships, activity and output.
    - Editors: task-focused workspace, persistent save state, contextual configuration and immutable-version context.
    - Settings: local navigation and a focused form column, not a card dashboard.
    
    ## Widths
    
    Home is centered up to `1200px`; collections are fluid up to `1440px`; settings and forms use `720px` to `840px`; details use up to `1200px`; editors and logs use available width.
    
    ## Collections
    
    Keep status near the name, use predictable sortable columns, preserve useful filters in URL state, expose row actions to pointer and keyboard users, and make truncated identifiers copyable. Use bulk actions only for proven repeated work.
    
    ## Persistent Tab State
    
    All page-level tabs must persist the selected tab in the route URL through a named Search parameter. The default tab is used when the parameter is missing or invalid. Changing tabs updates the URL without changing the page's visual shell, and a refresh or direct link restores the selected tab. Tab parameters must be validated at the route boundary so unsupported values never select an undefined view.
    
    ## Editors and Versions
    
    Show `Saving`, `Saved`, and `Unsaved changes`. Distinguish mutable drafts from immutable published versions. Validation navigates directly to affected content. Publish actions explain immutability and locked dependencies.
    
    ## Filter and View State
    
    A filter, tab, or expansion that a user would expect to survive a refresh or a shared link belongs in validated route search state, not in `window.location` read directly or in browser history side effects. Validate the parameter at the route boundary so an unsupported value resolves to the default rather than selecting an undefined view. When several filters describe one investigation, persist them together; restoring part of a view produces a different view.
    
    ## Acceptance Checklist
    
    A page defines route and workspace context, one primary action with a declared action budget, both themes, applicable states, keyboard behavior, accessible names, responsive behavior, persistent state ownership, security-sensitive behavior, and semantic-token usage. Its `DESIGN.md` follows `../TEMPLATE.md` and records a dated coverage verification.
    
    ## Changelog

    - Required refresh-surviving filter, tab, and expansion state to live in validated route search state, and required related filters to persist together.
    - Added the declared action budget and dated coverage verification to the page acceptance checklist.
    - Removed the Onboarding page family and its column width after the `/onboarding` route family was removed; first use is a server-derived sequence inside Home.
    - Made the collection description optional, matching the copy standards.
    
    ### 2026-09-11
    
    - Standardized page-level tab persistence through validated URL Search parameters so refreshes and direct links retain the selected view.
    
    ### 2026-08-14
    
    - Documented the focused onboarding column width and the absence of a decorative side panel.

    - Extracted page families, sizing, collection grammar and acceptance requirements.

    # Shared States
    
    ## Loading and Mutation
    
    Keep the shell stable. Use content-shaped skeletons instead of ordinary full-page spinners. Show progress locally for local mutations and prevent duplicate submissions without hiding context.
    
    A skeleton stands in for the content it replaces. Do not render the frame of absent content beside it: a table header above no rows, or a detail heading above no fields, reports structure the surface cannot yet fill.
    
    The router owns the shell-level pending and error boundaries. A route that has not resolved shows a content-shaped skeleton inside the stable shell, and a route that throws shows a recoverable failure with a retry that invalidates the router. A page defines only the states it adds beyond those defaults.
    
    Every state on this page is reachable in every route context. A detail route resolves loading, not-found, and load failure as three distinct states; presenting a pending fetch as a missing object misreports it.
    
    Local mutations apply optimistically where the change is reversible. A failure restores the previous value and explains itself beside the control that failed. `interaction-contract.md` governs which actions must behave this way.
    
    Use one destructive confirmation pattern for permanent removal: name the object, state the consequence, keep Cancel as the lower-emphasis action, use destructive styling only for the confirmed action, prevent duplicate submission, and retain the failure in the dialog until recovery or dismissal. Cancellation of work is not destructive: present it as a neutral secondary execution control with a text or icon cue and a distinct busy state.
    
    ## Empty and No Results
    
    An empty collection explains the object and provides one authorized next action. No-results state names the active filtering and offers `Clear filters`. Do not use large generic AI illustrations.
    
    These are two states, not one. A collection with nothing in it must not be described as having no matches, and must not offer to clear filters that are not set. Branch on whether the unfiltered collection is empty, not on whether the filtered result is.
    
    A placeholder value such as an em-dash is acceptable for a genuinely absent field. It is not acceptable as the permanent content of a column that has no data source; remove the column instead.
    
    ## Error and Permission
    
    Explain failures in user terms, preserve unaffected content, and provide recovery. Durable errors remain in the page rather than only in a toast. Resource errors identify the unavailable item or action without leaking protected details. Agent turns render credential-safe failure reasons and explicit cancellation cues inline; raw provider or SDK errors and malformed tool input are never presentation content.
    
    ## Offline and Streaming
    
    Use a restrained persistent reconnecting bar. Explain whether edits are local, blocked or persisted. Resume run events without duplication. Streaming content preserves scroll position unless the user is following the end, and offers an explicit return-to-end control while they are not. Create the destination response region as soon as a turn starts, retain partial content on failure, and expose a non-color streaming, cancellation, or failure cue without announcing every token to assistive technology. Send becomes Stop until the current turn completes or is cancelled.
    
    Agent composer drafts remain editable during an active turn. A draft submitted during that turn enters a visible removable FIFO queue and sends against the same execution when the turn completes, rather than being discarded: a composer that accepts a keystroke and then drops it reports work it did not do. The queue pauses without losing entries when the turn fails, when the reader stops it, and while a clarification question is pending, because in each case the queued message either depends on a result that did not arrive or would be misread as the answer to the question on screen. A paused queue states that it is paused. The queue is browser-session state and is not persisted.
    
    Human-gated execution is durable. A `Waiting for input` Run keeps its pending action visible across navigation and reload, exposes expiry and recovery controls, and resumes automatically when the server observes completion. QR expiry is a recoverable pending state rather than a failed Run.
    
    A paused Run is active but reversible execution state. It remains visible while suspended, offers resume through one neutral execution control, and keeps cancellation available as a separate terminal intent. Pause and resume report progress on the activated control; a failed command explains itself there without replacing the Run summary.
    
    A failed Run is recoverable at the node the server marks as retryable. Retry is a neutral execution control local to that node entry, not a destructive action and not a Run-level rerun. It reports progress on the control itself, preserves the existing failure reason until execution continues, and surfaces a rejected retry beside that reason rather than replacing it.
    
    ## Truthful Feedback
    
    Success feedback reports an outcome that occurred. A control must not confirm work it did not perform, and a toast must not substitute for the action itself. When a capability is unavailable for the current object, the control is absent rather than present and inert.
    
    ## Long Content and Security
    
    Truncate only summaries and provide expand, copy, download or details access. Inline Agent Skill calls stay collapsed by default, retain status and exit context in their summary, and reveal height-bounded scrollable raw output only on request. Never reveal secrets in fields, logs, errors or audit metadata. Untrusted content is rendered without inline execution.

    # Interaction Contract
    
    This document is the source of truth for how many deliberate actions a WorkLite task may cost and for which failures the product must recover from on its own. `shared-states.md` defines what each state looks like; this document defines who is responsible for leaving that state.
    
    ## Single Action
    
    One user goal has exactly one activation point in one region. A goal that is already expressed by a visible control must not also require a second control to take effect.
    
    - Do not split a single intent into a preparation action and a commit action. If a preparation step is always required before the commit, run it inside the commit.
    - Do not add a confirmation step to a reversible action. Confirmation is reserved for permanent removal and for publishing an immutable version.
    - Do not require a selection the product can already resolve. When exactly one valid value exists, or the last used value is still valid, apply it and act.
    - Do not duplicate a primary action in both the context bar and the page body.
    
    A surface that needs more than one action for its primary task must say so in its `DESIGN.md` under Primary Task, with the reason.
    
    ## Self-Healing State
    
    When the server can observe that a value is stale, the client recovers without being asked. A manual refresh control is permitted only when staleness is not observable.
    
    Self-healing applies to expired authentication codes, expired tokens, dropped streams, stale quota and usage figures, and any value already backed by a poll or an event stream.
    
    The recovery must be visible as state, not as an instruction. Show that the value is being replaced; do not ask the user to replace it. Cancelling the surrounding work stays available, because cancellation is a separate intent rather than a recovery from staleness.
    
    A surface that keeps a manual refresh control must record in its `DESIGN.md` why staleness cannot be observed.
    
    ## Action Budget
    
    Every `DESIGN.md` declares the number of deliberate actions its primary task costs, counted from the moment the surface is visible to the moment the goal is reached. Typing into a field is one action regardless of length. Navigation into the surface is not counted.
    
    A budget above one requires a stated reason: an irreversible outcome, a genuinely independent second intent, or a value the product cannot resolve.
    
    ## Immediate Feedback
    
    Every action reports progress on the control that was activated, within the same frame it was activated. Progress never replaces the surrounding content and never blocks unrelated controls.
    
    Local, reversible changes apply optimistically. A failure restores the previous value and explains itself next to the control that failed, not only in a toast.
    
    Duplicate submission is prevented by the control's own busy state rather than by disabling the region around it.
    
    ## Remembered Input
    
    A choice the user has already made is the default the next time the same action runs, as long as it is still valid. This applies to selected models, active filters, expanded rows, and chosen categories.
    
    Remembered input is applied silently. Do not present it as a step to confirm.
    
    ## Changelog
    
    ### 2026-09-19
    
    - Established the interaction contract: single activation point per goal, server-observable staleness recovered without a manual control, declared per-page action budgets, control-local immediate feedback, and silently reapplied remembered input.
    # Copy Standards
    
    This document is the source of truth for which user-facing text WorkLite is allowed to show. `docs/ui-design-system/README.md` governs typography and tone; The fixed Chinese resource set governs product copy ownership. This document governs whether a string may exist at all.
    
    ## Admitted Categories
    
    Product-owned text belongs to exactly one of four categories. Text that fits none of them is removed.
    
    - **Action.** Names what activating a control does: `Publish`, `Retry node`, `Clear filters`.
    - **State.** Reports what is happening or what is true right now: `Running`, `Unsaved changes`, `Waiting for QR scan`.
    - **Constraint.** Tells the user something they must know to act correctly and cannot infer from the interface: `Credentials are write-only and never shown in logs`, `This permanently deletes the Workflow, its draft, published versions, schedule, and run history.`
    - **Recovery.** Names the next step after a failure or an empty result: `Add a provider to make models available to agents.`
    
    ## Excluded Text
    
    Remove text that restates its own heading. A page titled Artifacts does not need to be described as outputs produced by workflow runs.
    
    Remove text that describes what a visible component already communicates. A save indicator makes `Changes are saved automatically.` redundant.
    
    Remove text that explains internal mechanics the user cannot act on, including poll intervals, refresh cadence, and expiry timestamps for values the product replaces on its own.
    
    Remove product definitions that do not change what the user does on the surface. Explaining what a workflow is does not help someone who is looking at their workflow list.
    
    Remove promotional and reassuring phrasing. State the fact instead.
    
    ## Automation Debt
    
    When an interaction becomes automatic, the text that existed to support the manual path is removed in the same change. An automatically replaced authentication code shows neither its expiry time nor an instruction to replace it: both describe work the user no longer does.
    
    Automation that removes a control removes its label, its help text, and its locale keys together, in the fixed Chinese resource set.
    
    ## Optional Descriptions
    
    A page or section description is optional. Write one only to state a constraint or to bound a scope that is not evident from the content. When no such text is needed, the heading stands alone.
    
    ## Inventory
    
    Every `DESIGN.md` lists its surface's Chinese resource keys under Copy Inventory with the category each key belongs to. A key that cannot be assigned a category is removed rather than reclassified. Removing a key removes its Copy Inventory row in the same change.
    
    ## Changelog
    
    ### 2026-09-19
    
    - Established copy standards: four admitted categories, explicit exclusions for restated headings and component-duplicating text, same-change removal of text made obsolete by automation, optional descriptions, and per-surface copy inventories.
