    # Responsive Behavior
    
    ## Wide Desktop
    
    At `1024px` and above, expand the sidebar, allow side-by-side inspectors, and retain useful table columns. Home keeps the Agent Chat composer visible; other pages use a lower-right draggable Chat icon until opened. The expanded Agent Chat panel uses the same centered panel up to `1200px` wide and approximately `680px` high, constrained by `24px` outer space. Its message region keeps `16px` horizontal padding, and automatic Skill execution regions remain inline as compact collapsed disclosure rows.
    
    ## Compact Desktop and Tablet
    
    From `768px` to `1023px`, use the `56px` grouped icon rail, hide low-priority columns, and let inspectors overlay or reduce content according to task importance. The workflow contextual Sheet yields to its fixed right-side panel as soon as that panel's desktop breakpoint becomes active. Agent resource tabs remain horizontally scrollable within their collection pages, and the Workflow Run records dialog keeps expanded artifact rows readable and its per-node retry control reachable within its scrolling surface. Keep the Home composer visible and use the draggable lower-right Chat icon on other pages; constrain the expanded Agent Chat panel within `16px` to `24px` outer space, and keep expanded Skill arguments, execution states, and bounded results inside the transcript column.
    
    ## Mobile
    
    Below `768px`, use a navigation drawer, retain page identity, state and primary action in the context bar, convert the workflow editor's combined palette and inspector to one full-screen or bottom sheet, keep the workflow canvas full-bleed within its editor region, replace wide tables with object rows, and show detailed logs full-screen or in a resizable sheet. Canvas zoom, fit-to-view, selection, and deletion controls remain reachable with `40px` to `44px` touch targets. The drawer preserves every grouped desktop destination named in `workspace-shell.md`, including Plugins and Logs; page-level collection and observability tabs remain reachable through horizontal scrolling, and the Workflow Run records dialog exposes Artifacts through in-place expansion. Home keeps its composer visible; other pages use a draggable lower-right Chat icon with `12px` safe-area margins until opened. Agent Chat uses at most about `70vh`; it does not become full-screen. Its single-line composer remains reachable above browser controls, and Chat and Proposed changes use internal views.
    
    A shared time-range control keeps its preset selection and its custom start and end fields reachable at every breakpoint. Below `768px` the presets and the two fields stack in one column rather than dropping the custom range, because a range the reader cannot narrow on a small screen makes the surface unusable there.
    
    Responsive layouts must not remove status, recovery, or cancellation controls, including the per-node retry control on a retryable failed node entry. The Agent composer retains a stable Send-or-Stop target, editable input, and keyboard-accessible published Workflow mention menu at every breakpoint; working feedback remains in the scrollable transcript rather than consuming composer space.
    
    Queued Chat Bot messages keep their rows, count, and per-row remove control inside the scrollable transcript at every breakpoint, and the return-to-end control stays reachable without covering the composer.

    # Workspace Shell
    
    ## Structure
    
    Use a persistent `232px` sidebar, a `52px` context bar, fluid main content, an optional `360px` inspector, and an optional resizable bottom run panel. The sidebar collapses to `56px` only between `768px` and `1023px`.
    
    Primary navigation is grouped and single-level. It contains six direct destinations: **Workspace** contains `Home` and `Workflows`; **Capabilities** contains `Plugins`, with `Skills` and `MCP Servers` available as capability sub-navigation; **Configuration** contains `Providers`, `Logs`, and `Settings`.
    
    Providers owns the Model Providers, Portkey Gateway summary, and Codex account views in one page context. Logs owns Gateway transport observability: request statistics and captured request details over one shared time range. The two are separate destinations because one configures upstream dispatch and the other reads what was dispatched. Skills and MCP Servers are the capability destinations; standalone Agents have no page-level destination; Plugins remains its peer. Workflow List owns execution-history access through its per-Workflow Run records dialog, whose expanded Run rows expose Artifacts inline; direct Artifact details provide deeper inspection. At `1024px` and above, the expanded sidebar shows group labels and all destinations. From `768px` to `1023px`, the compact icon rail uses group separators, direct icons, and tooltips. The mobile navigation drawer uses the same grouped destinations. Usage, audit log, and appearance are reached from Settings. Chat Bot is available throughout the workspace shell, presented prominently on Home and as a floating control elsewhere. Counts indicate actionable state only. The WorkLite mark is at the top and the personal preferences menu is at the bottom. The expanded preferences control keeps its neutral status label and shows the application version as a right-aligned monospace label; the compact rail exposes the same version inside the preferences menu.
    
    The selected navigation item uses `brand-subtle`, primary text, and a narrow brand indicator. The selected resource link represents its route family: Skills and MCP Server routes select Capabilities, while Artifact routes select Workflows. Personal preferences stay in the bottom menu.
    
    ## Context Bar
    
    Place navigation and breadcrumb context on the left. Place command search, state, secondary actions, and one primary page action on the right. Move low-frequency actions to overflow and never duplicate the primary action in the page heading.
    
    ## Panels
    
    The inspector opens only for selected contextual content, keeps its header and essential actions available, scrolls internally, and does not discard unsaved work when closed. It may expand to `440px` for structured configuration.
    
    The workspace shell owns the active Chat Bot execution identifier, the transient composer draft, and the pending message queue. Published Workflows are selected per message with `@` mentions and create normal Workflow Runs that remain independent from the Chat Bot session. Messages, plugin process state, script requests, automatic execution state, and results remain server-owned. Page navigation closes the visible conversation without cancelling work; a browser reload fetches the active execution identifier and selected target saved by the browser, and drops the queue, which is session state rather than persisted intent.
    
    Place the Chat Bot interaction surface at the bottom of the content region on every workspace page. Home keeps the single-line input visible by default. Other pages show only a draggable floating Chat Bot icon in the lower-right corner by default; clicking it opens the same raised conversation panel above the current page and focuses the input. Clicking outside an expanded Chat surface closes it while Chat-owned popup menus remain usable. Keep the icon inside the viewport safe area and preserve a keyboard-accessible open action without a visible Tooltip. Center the complete expanded surface and cap it at `1200px`. With a bound provider the expanded composer contains the single-line input and one stable icon-button target without a repeated visible Chat Bot title; the target shows Send while idle and Stop while the active turn is running. The input remains editable in both states. Without a bound provider the expanded surface contains its inline Chat Bot configuration panel instead of an input or send control. Home and other pages use the same personal session, expanded dimensions, and compact execution summary.
    
    The bottom panel defaults to about `240px`, resizes, and collapses to a status strip. Closing hides but never cancels a run. Logs distinguish timestamp, severity, source and content, and auto-follow only while the user is at the stream end.
    
    ## Route Boundaries
    
    The root route owns the pending and error boundaries for every page. An unresolved route renders a content-shaped skeleton inside the stable shell rather than an empty content region; a route that throws renders a recoverable failure whose retry invalidates the router. The sidebar, context bar, and Chat surface remain mounted through both states, so a slow or failed page never collapses the workspace.
    
    There is no separate first-use route family. Home derives first-use completion from persisted server resources, so the shell has no onboarding layout branch and no browser-state onboarding step.
    
    ## Command and User Menus
    
    `Command+K` or `Control+K` opens grouped search, recent destinations, navigation and safe creation commands. Destructive actions are excluded. Opening Chat Bot through the command menu changes the shell-owned conversation state through typed route search and must not rely on an ignored URL flag. The user menu contains the personal workspace identity, Appearance, Keyboard shortcuts, and the application version. Appearance includes the personal theme and language preferences.

    # Page Patterns
    
    ## Families
    
    - Collections: title, optional description, search, filters, active chips, and right-aligned primary actions in the toolbar directly above the compact table or object list.
    - Details: durable summary, metadata, relationships, activity and output.
    - Editors: task-focused workspace, persistent save state, contextual configuration and immutable-version context.
    - Settings: local navigation and a focused form column, not a card dashboard.
    
    ## Widths
    
    Home is centered up to `1200px`; collections are fluid up to `1440px`; settings and forms use `720px` to `840px`; details use up to `1200px`; editors and logs use available width.
    
    ## Collections
    
    Keep status near the name, use predictable sortable columns, preserve useful filters in URL state, expose row actions to pointer and keyboard users, and make truncated identifiers copyable. Use bulk actions only for proven repeated work.
    
    ## Persistent Tab State
    
    All page-level tabs must persist the selected tab in the route URL through a named Search parameter. The default tab is used when the parameter is missing or invalid. Changing tabs updates the URL without changing the page's visual shell, and a refresh or direct link restores the selected tab. Tab parameters must be validated at the route boundary so unsupported values never select an undefined view.
    
    ## Editors and Versions
    
    Show `Saving`, `Saved`, and `Unsaved changes`. Distinguish mutable drafts from immutable published versions. Validation navigates directly to affected content. Publish actions explain immutability and locked dependencies.
    
    ## Filter and View State
    
    A filter, tab, or expansion that a user would expect to survive a refresh or a shared link belongs in validated route search state, not in `window.location` read directly or in browser history side effects. Validate the parameter at the route boundary so an unsupported value resolves to the default rather than selecting an undefined view. When several filters describe one investigation, persist them together; restoring part of a view produces a different view.
    
    ## Acceptance Checklist
    
    A page defines route and workspace context, one primary action with a declared action budget, both themes, applicable states, keyboard behavior, accessible names, responsive behavior, persistent state ownership, security-sensitive behavior, and semantic-token usage. Its `DESIGN.md` follows `../TEMPLATE.md` and records a dated coverage verification.
    
    ## Changelog
    
    ### 2026-09-19
    
    - Required refresh-surviving filter, tab, and expansion state to live in validated route search state, and required related filters to persist together.
    - Added the declared action budget and dated coverage verification to the page acceptance checklist.

    # Shared States
    
    ## Loading and Mutation
    
    Keep the shell stable. Use content-shaped skeletons instead of ordinary full-page spinners. Show progress locally for local mutations and prevent duplicate submissions without hiding context.
    
    A skeleton stands in for the content it replaces. Do not render the frame of absent content beside it: a table header above no rows, or a detail heading above no fields, reports structure the surface cannot yet fill.
    
    The router owns the shell-level pending and error boundaries. A route that has not resolved shows a content-shaped skeleton inside the stable shell, and a route that throws shows a recoverable failure with a retry that invalidates the router. A page defines only the states it adds beyond those defaults.
    
    Every state on this page is reachable in every route context. A detail route resolves loading, not-found, and load failure as three distinct states; presenting a pending fetch as a missing object misreports it.
    
    Local mutations apply optimistically where the change is reversible. A failure restores the previous value and explains itself beside the control that failed. `interaction-contract.md` governs which actions must behave this way.
    
    Use one destructive confirmation pattern for permanent removal: name the object, state the consequence, keep Cancel as the lower-emphasis action, use destructive styling only for the confirmed action, prevent duplicate submission, and retain the failure in the dialog until recovery or dismissal. Cancellation of work is not destructive: present it as a neutral secondary execution control with a text or icon cue and a distinct busy state.
    
    ## Empty and No Results
    
    An empty collection explains the object and provides one authorized next action. No-results state names the active filtering and offers `Clear filters`. Do not use large generic AI illustrations.
    
    These are two states, not one. A collection with nothing in it must not be described as having no matches, and must not offer to clear filters that are not set. Branch on whether the unfiltered collection is empty, not on whether the filtered result is.
    
    A placeholder value such as an em-dash is acceptable for a genuinely absent field. It is not acceptable as the permanent content of a column that has no data source; remove the column instead.
    
    ## Error and Permission
    
    Explain failures in user terms, preserve unaffected content, and provide recovery. Durable errors remain in the page rather than only in a toast. Resource errors identify the unavailable item or action without leaking protected details. Agent turns render credential-safe failure reasons and explicit cancellation cues inline; raw provider or SDK errors and malformed tool input are never presentation content.
    
    ## Offline and Streaming
    
    Use a restrained persistent reconnecting bar. Explain whether edits are local, blocked or persisted. Resume run events without duplication. Streaming content preserves scroll position unless the user is following the end, and offers an explicit return-to-end control while they are not. Create the destination response region as soon as a turn starts, retain partial content on failure, and expose a non-color streaming, cancellation, or failure cue without announcing every token to assistive technology. Send becomes Stop until the current turn completes or is cancelled.
    
    Agent composer drafts remain editable during an active turn. A draft submitted during that turn enters a visible removable FIFO queue and sends against the same execution when the turn completes, rather than being discarded: a composer that accepts a keystroke and then drops it reports work it did not do. The queue pauses without losing entries when the turn fails, when the reader stops it, and while a clarification question is pending, because in each case the queued message either depends on a result that did not arrive or would be misread as the answer to the question on screen. A paused queue states that it is paused. The queue is browser-session state and is not persisted.
    
    Human-gated execution is durable. A `Waiting for input` Run keeps its pending action visible across navigation and reload, exposes expiry and recovery controls, and resumes automatically when the server observes completion. QR expiry is a recoverable pending state rather than a failed Run.
    
    A paused Run is active but reversible execution state. It remains visible while suspended, offers resume through one neutral execution control, and keeps cancellation available as a separate terminal intent. Pause and resume report progress on the activated control; a failed command explains itself there without replacing the Run summary.
    
    A failed Run is recoverable at the node the server marks as retryable. Retry is a neutral execution control local to that node entry, not a destructive action and not a Run-level rerun. It reports progress on the control itself, preserves the existing failure reason until execution continues, and surfaces a rejected retry beside that reason rather than replacing it.
    
    ## Truthful Feedback
    
    Success feedback reports an outcome that occurred. A control must not confirm work it did not perform, and a toast must not substitute for the action itself. When a capability is unavailable for the current object, the control is absent rather than present and inert.
    
    ## Long Content and Security
    
    Truncate only summaries and provide expand, copy, download or details access. Inline Agent Skill calls stay collapsed by default, retain status and exit context in their summary, and reveal height-bounded scrollable raw output only on request. Never reveal secrets in fields, logs, errors or audit metadata. Untrusted content is rendered without inline execution.
    
    ## Changelog
    
    ### 2026-09-22
    
    - Added paused Runs as reversible active execution state with neutral resume feedback, preserved Run visibility, and an independent cancellation intent.
    
    ### 2026-09-21
    
    - Replaced the unqueued-draft rule with a visible removable FIFO queue for drafts submitted during an active Agent turn, including its pause conditions on failure, stop, and pending clarification. This supersedes the 2026-08-27 removal of message queuing.
    - Required streaming surfaces to offer an explicit return-to-end control while the reader is away from the end.
    
    ### 2026-09-19
    
    - Assigned the shell-level pending and error boundaries to the router so every route inherits a content-shaped skeleton and a recoverable failure.
    - Required detail routes to distinguish loading, not-found, and load failure instead of presenting a pending fetch as a missing object.
    - Prohibited rendering the frame of absent content beside a skeleton, and required optimistic application with rollback for reversible local mutations.
    - Required empty and no-results to branch on the unfiltered collection, and prohibited permanent placeholder columns with no data source.
    - Added Truthful Feedback: success confirms work that occurred, and an unavailable capability omits its control rather than presenting it inert.
    
    ### 2026-09-18
    
    - Added node-scoped failed-Run recovery: a neutral retry control on the server-marked retryable node entry, with control-local progress and preserved failure reasons.
    
    ### 2026-09-16
    
    - Added durable human-gated Workflow waiting, QR expiry, refresh, and automatic continuation states.
    
    ### 2026-09-14
    
    - Standardized destructive confirmation structure and reclassified execution cancellation as neutral, non-destructive feedback.
    
    ### 2026-08-27
    
    - Required inline credential-safe Agent failure reasons and explicit cancellation cues without exposing malformed tool input or raw provider and SDK errors.
    - Defined collapsed-by-default Agent Skill-call summaries and bounded on-demand output for long transcript content.
    - Replaced obsolete local Agent message queue guidance with editable, unqueued drafts, transcript-owned working feedback, and active-turn Stop behavior.
    
    ### 2026-08-26
    
    - Added queued-message visibility, removal, and failure-pause behavior to shared streaming states.
    
    ### 2026-08-26
    
    - Defined incremental response placement, partial-content retention, conditional auto-follow, and restrained live announcements for model streams.
    
    ### 2026-08-13
    
    - Extracted shared loading, empty, error, permission, offline, streaming and long-content rules.

## Activity

    $ cat ui-ux-design/shared/interaction-contract.md
    # Interaction Contract
    
    This document is the source of truth for how many deliberate actions a WorkLite task may cost and for which failures the product must recover from on its own. `shared-states.md` defines what each state looks like; this document defines who is responsible for leaving that state.
    
    ## Single Action
    
    One user goal has exactly one activation point in one region. A goal that is already expressed by a visible control must not also require a second control to take effect.
    
    - Do not split a single intent into a preparation action and a commit action. If a preparation step is always required before the commit, run it inside the commit.
    - Do not add a confirmation step to a reversible action. Confirmation is reserved for permanent removal and for publishing an immutable version.
    - Do not require a selection the product can already resolve. When exactly one valid value exists, or the last used value is still valid, apply it and act.
    - Do not duplicate a primary action in both the context bar and the page body.
    
    A surface that needs more than one action for its primary task must say so in its `DESIGN.md` under Primary Task, with the reason.
    
    ## Self-Healing State
    
    When the server can observe that a value is stale, the client recovers without being asked. A manual refresh control is permitted only when staleness is not observable.
    
    Self-healing applies to expired authentication codes, expired tokens, dropped streams, stale quota and usage figures, and any value already backed by a poll or an event stream.
    
    The recovery must be visible as state, not as an instruction. Show that the value is being replaced; do not ask the user to replace it. Cancelling the surrounding work stays available, because cancellation is a separate intent rather than a recovery from staleness.
    
    A surface that keeps a manual refresh control must record in its `DESIGN.md` why staleness cannot be observed.
    
    ## Action Budget
    
    Every `DESIGN.md` declares the number of deliberate actions its primary task costs, counted from the moment the surface is visible to the moment the goal is reached. Typing into a field is one action regardless of length. Navigation into the surface is not counted.
    
    A budget above one requires a stated reason: an irreversible outcome, a genuinely independent second intent, or a value the product cannot resolve.
    
    ## Immediate Feedback
    
    Every action reports progress on the control that was activated, within the same frame it was activated. Progress never replaces the surrounding content and never blocks unrelated controls.
    
    Local, reversible changes apply optimistically. A failure restores the previous value and explains itself next to the control that failed, not only in a toast.
    
    Duplicate submission is prevented by the control's own busy state rather than by disabling the region around it.
    
    ## Remembered Input
    
    A choice the user has already made is the default the next time the same action runs, as long as it is still valid. This applies to selected models, active filters, expanded rows, and chosen categories.
    
    Remembered input is applied silently. Do not present it as a step to confirm.
    
    ## Changelog
    
    ### 2026-09-19
    
    - Established the interaction contract: single activation point per goal, server-observable staleness recovered without a manual control, declared per-page action budgets, control-local immediate feedback, and silently reapplied remembered input.

## Activity

    $ cat ui-ux-design/shared/copy-standards.md
    # Copy Standards
    
    This document is the source of truth for which user-facing text WorkLite is allowed to show. `docs/ui-design-system/README.md` governs typography and tone; The fixed Chinese resource set governs product copy ownership. This document governs whether a string may exist at all.
    
    ## Admitted Categories
    
    Product-owned text belongs to exactly one of four categories. Text that fits none of them is removed.
    
    - **Action.** Names what activating a control does: `Publish`, `Retry node`, `Clear filters`.
    - **State.** Reports what is happening or what is true right now: `Running`, `Unsaved changes`, `Waiting for QR scan`.
    - **Constraint.** Tells the user something they must know to act correctly and cannot infer from the interface: `Credentials are write-only and never shown in logs`, `This permanently deletes the Workflow, its draft, published versions, schedule, and run history.`
    - **Recovery.** Names the next step after a failure or an empty result: `Add a provider to make models available to agents.`
    
    ## Excluded Text
    
    Remove text that restates its own heading. A page titled Artifacts does not need to be described as outputs produced by workflow runs.
    
    Remove text that describes what a visible component already communicates. A save indicator makes `Changes are saved automatically.` redundant.
    
    Remove text that explains internal mechanics the user cannot act on, including poll intervals, refresh cadence, and expiry timestamps for values the product replaces on its own.
    
    Remove product definitions that do not change what the user does on the surface. Explaining what a workflow is does not help someone who is looking at their workflow list.
    
    Remove promotional and reassuring phrasing. State the fact instead.
    
    ## Automation Debt
    
    When an interaction becomes automatic, the text that existed to support the manual path is removed in the same change. An automatically replaced authentication code shows neither its expiry time nor an instruction to replace it: both describe work the user no longer does.
    
    Automation that removes a control removes its label, its help text, and its locale keys together, in the fixed Chinese resource set.
    
    ## Optional Descriptions
    
    A page or section description is optional. Write one only to state a constraint or to bound a scope that is not evident from the content. When no such text is needed, the heading stands alone.
    
    ## Inventory
    
    Every `DESIGN.md` lists its surface's Chinese resource keys under Copy Inventory with the category each key belongs to. A key that cannot be assigned a category is removed rather than reclassified. Removing a key removes its Copy Inventory row in the same change.
    
    ## Changelog
    
    ### 2026-09-19
    
    - Established copy standards: four admitted categories, explicit exclusions for restated headings and component-duplicating text, same-change removal of text made obsolete by automation, optional descriptions, and per-surface copy inventories.

    # Responsive Behavior
    
    ## Wide Desktop
    
    At `1024px` and above, expand the sidebar, allow side-by-side inspectors, and retain useful table columns. Home keeps the Agent Chat composer visible; other pages use a lower-right draggable Chat icon until opened. The expanded Agent Chat panel uses the same centered panel up to `1200px` wide and approximately `680px` high, constrained by `24px` outer space. Its message region keeps `16px` horizontal padding, and automatic Skill execution regions remain inline as compact collapsed disclosure rows.
    
    ## Compact Desktop and Tablet
    
    From `768px` to `1023px`, use the `56px` grouped icon rail, hide low-priority columns, and let inspectors overlay or reduce content according to task importance. The workflow contextual Sheet yields to its fixed right-side panel as soon as that panel's desktop breakpoint becomes active. Agent resource tabs remain horizontally scrollable within their collection pages, and the Workflow Run records dialog keeps expanded artifact rows readable and its per-node retry control reachable within its scrolling surface. Keep the Home composer visible and use the draggable lower-right Chat icon on other pages; constrain the expanded Agent Chat panel within `16px` to `24px` outer space, and keep expanded Skill arguments, execution states, and bounded results inside the transcript column.
    
    ## Mobile
    
    Below `768px`, use a navigation drawer, retain page identity, state and primary action in the context bar, convert the workflow editor's combined palette and inspector to one full-screen or bottom sheet, keep the workflow canvas full-bleed within its editor region, replace wide tables with object rows, and show detailed logs full-screen or in a resizable sheet. Canvas zoom, fit-to-view, selection, and deletion controls remain reachable with `40px` to `44px` touch targets. The drawer preserves every grouped desktop destination named in `workspace-shell.md`, including Plugins and Logs; page-level collection and observability tabs remain reachable through horizontal scrolling, and the Workflow Run records dialog exposes Artifacts through in-place expansion. Home keeps its composer visible; other pages use a draggable lower-right Chat icon with `12px` safe-area margins until opened. Agent Chat uses at most about `70vh`; it does not become full-screen. Its single-line composer remains reachable above browser controls, and Chat and Proposed changes use internal views.
    
    A shared time-range control keeps its preset selection and its custom start and end fields reachable at every breakpoint. Below `768px` the presets and the two fields stack in one column rather than dropping the custom range, because a range the reader cannot narrow on a small screen makes the surface unusable there.
    
    Responsive layouts must not remove status, recovery, or cancellation controls, including the per-node retry control on a retryable failed node entry. The Agent composer retains a stable Send-or-Stop target, editable input, and keyboard-accessible published Workflow mention menu at every breakpoint; working feedback remains in the scrollable transcript rather than consuming composer space.
    
    Queued Chat Bot messages keep their rows, count, and per-row remove control inside the scrollable transcript at every breakpoint, and the return-to-end control stays reachable without covering the composer.

    # Workflow Editor
    
    ## Route
    
    `/workflows/{new,:workflowId}`
    
    ## Design Source
    
    - `docs/ui-design-system/README.md`
    - Applicable shared specifications in `ui-ux-design/shared/`
    
    ## Implementation
    
    - `apps/web/src/routes/workflows/$workflowId.tsx`
    - `apps/web/src/components/workflow-canvas-nodes.tsx`
    
    ## Purpose
    
    Build and configure a Workflow graph, then publish it as an immutable version that can run.
    
    ## Primary Task
    
    Change the graph and persist the change. Action budget: two — edit the graph, then `Save`.
    
    The budget is above one because the graph is a composite draft rather than a single field: a node addition, a connection, and an inspector change accumulate into one revision, and the user decides when that revision is coherent enough to persist. Autosaving a half-connected graph would produce invalid intermediate revisions in the undo history. The editor compensates by showing `Saving`, `Saved`, and `Unsaved changes` continuously, so the unsaved state is never ambiguous.
    
    `Publish` is a separate, irreversible goal and keeps its own confirmation step.
    
    ## Model
    
    The workflow editor presents a directed control-flow dataflow graph with structured conditional edges and bounded loop edges.
    
    The palette includes Timer, Workflow Input, Agent, Choice Branch, TypeSafe System One, TypeSafe System One Map, Dashboard, Artifact, Artifact Query, Image, and the trusted WeChat Official Account Publish node when its built-in Plugin is available.
    
    - **Timer** is a source trigger with no inputs, one JSON output, an enabled control, and a fixed interval of at least five minutes; each Workflow may contain at most one Timer.
    - **Dashboard** has one required JSON `data` input, one JSON `output` port, and at most one instance per Workflow.
    - **Workflow Input** exposes the run input and may connect explicitly to Agent `context` as the initial token.
    - **Agent** owns its immutable embedded configuration and has one optional `context` input plus one output. When `context` has no explicit Workflow Input edge and no unbounded incoming edge, the initial Agent invocation uses the Workflow Run input, while later bounded-loop traversals supply the next context value. Its inspector selects `Text` or `JSON` output format.
    - **Choice Branch** has one required JSON `value` input and one JSON `output` port. It passes the input through unchanged and evaluates its outgoing unconditional or predicate edges in connection order, traversing only the first match; when no non-fallback edge matches, it traverses the first fallback edge. It can consume JSON from any upstream node.
    - **TypeSafe System One** has one required JSON `state` input and one JSON `output` port. Its inspector selects a configured TypeSafe public model and edits the immutable typed `questions` object. The node forwards the upstream System One response, including `answers`, without chat or Agent adaptation, while retaining object state fields for downstream context; outgoing predicates may address paths such as `$.answers.articleType.choice`.
    - **TypeSafe System One Map** has the same required JSON `state` input and JSON `output` port as TypeSafe System One, and evaluates its typed questions once per element of an array inside that state. Its inspector adds the items path, an optional context path, an optional concurrency bound, and an optional ranking answer path whose order, result limit, and minimum score appear only once a ranking path exists. Ranking is deterministic ordering applied after evaluation, so the inspector presents it as selection rather than as a second question.
    - **Artifact** has one required JSON `data` input, one output, and permits multiple instances; it configures a non-empty display name and a `Text`, `Markdown`, or `JSON` artifact type.
    - **Artifact Query** has one required JSON `request` input and one JSON output; its inspector selects a JSON Artifact name, a top-level title field, and one or more top-level description fields. It reads matching workspace history, including detached Artifacts, and emits the request with compact title-and-description candidates without creating Artifacts.
    - **Image** has one required string `prompt` input and one JSON output. Its inspector fixes `codex/gpt-image-2` and exposes only the supported image count, background, quality, and size choices. The node displays an image summary after execution and never renders or inspects base64 data.
    - **WeChat Official Account Publish** accepts required Markdown `article` and generated cover-image inputs plus optional JSON `metadata`, and outputs a publication reference.
    
    One output may fan out to multiple downstream nodes. Choice Branch output is the deliberate exception to that fan-out behavior: its outgoing routes are exclusive and only the first matching route is traversed. Each named input accepts at most one edge, except Agent `context`, which may combine one unbounded initial upstream edge with one bounded feedback edge. An initial Workflow Input edge must remain unconditional. Edges may be unconditional, predicate-based, or fallback routes. A loop-closing edge must define a positive maximum traversal count, and every possible cycle must cross at least one bounded edge. Dynamic joins and parallel execution remain unavailable.
    
    ## Layout
    
    The context bar contains breadcrumb, saved state, revision history, Workflow settings, Versions, `Export JSON`, the destructive delete action, `Save`, `Run` where valid, and `Publish`.
    
    The editor workspace has a central `@xyflow/react` canvas and one right-side contextual panel. React Flow selection is authoritative and synchronizes the selected node or edge with the panel. With no selection the panel shows the searchable node palette; selecting a node or edge replaces the palette with its inspector; clicking the canvas background or using the inspector's back action clears all graph selection and restores the palette. Palette and inspector content always use the panel's full available width.
    
    The canvas supports node dragging, handle-to-handle connection, edge selection and deletion, pointer-drag panning, free horizontal and vertical trackpad or wheel panning, pinch zoom, zoom controls, and fit-to-view. Ordinary wheel input pans instead of zooming. It intentionally renders no minimap and no canvas-wide selection outline: selected nodes use a persimmon node border, selected edges use a persimmon stroke, and keyboard focus remains visible on the focused node, edge, or control. React Flow primitives follow the resolved light or dark application theme.
    
    On smaller breakpoints the combined contextual panel becomes one drawer or sheet, opens automatically for a canvas selection, and closes when the fixed desktop panel becomes available. A bottom panel shows test output, logs, and artifacts.
    
    Workflow-level settings are grouped into General, Inputs, Execution, and Versioning. General contains the workflow name and publication metadata; Inputs contains the input editor and examples; Execution contains default error policy and runtime defaults; Versioning contains draft, revision, and publication context. Advanced settings stay collapsed until requested. Scheduling is configured only through the Timer node, never through Workflow settings.
    
    ## Interaction Contract
    
    **Add a node.** The searchable palette inserts the node at the center of the visible canvas viewport, selects it, and marks the draft unsaved. Insertion never requires pointer dragging.
    
    **Connect nodes.** Handle-to-handle connection validates against the port rules above. While connecting, compatible and incompatible targets have distinct visual states. An invalid or type-incompatible attempt leaves graph state unchanged and reports concisely. A connection that would close a cycle receives a bounded traversal limit rather than being rejected.
    
    **Configure a selection.** Selecting a node or edge opens its inspector. Node inspectors expose node-owned parameters directly. Edge selection reveals endpoints, routing mode, structured predicate controls, maximum traversals, and a remove command. Predicate controls take a dot-delimited source-output path, a supported comparison operator, and a JSON comparison value when the operator requires one. Fallback routes explain that they run only when no unconditional or predicate edge from the same source invocation matches. Conditional edges show a concise condition label on the canvas; bounded edges use a dashed line and a traversal-limit label. Pointer dragging is never required to review, configure, or remove graph objects.
    
    **Save.** Persists the accumulated revision. The save state reports `Saving` and settles on `Saved`. A failure returns the state to `Unsaved changes` and keeps the reason visible in the canvas region rather than only in a toast. An invalid edge comparison value blocks the save and names that specific problem.
    
    **Undo and redo.** Server-backed revision movement, reported through the same save state. Both controls disable while a save is in flight.
    
    **Run.** Targets the latest published version, is unavailable while the draft has unsaved changes, and labels that version boundary explicitly. The control reports busy on itself. After the server returns the new Run id, navigation enters `/runs/:runId` so the live Run detail becomes the immediate execution surface; Run history remains available in the Workflow List dialog.
    
    **Publish.** Opens a confirmation explaining that publishing locks the embedded Agent configuration and that later draft edits do not change this Workflow or its historical runs. Publication validates bounded-cycle constraints, port rules, public model ids, TypeSafe questions, image generation settings, required WeChat cover connectivity, and selected Skill and MCP availability. Validation failures navigate directly to the affected content.
    
    **Export JSON.** Downloads the current draft in the portable WorkLite format. Unsaved new Workflows must be saved first. The action stays neutral in both themes and does not compete with save, run, or publish.
    
    **Delete.** Opens a confirmation naming the Workflow and explaining permanent removal of its drafts, published versions, schedules, and run history. Success closes the dialog, reports the outcome, and returns to the Workflow list; failure keeps the dialog open with visible feedback.
    
    The Timer inspector's read-only runtime status is the one self-healing value here: it follows the workflow schedule query rather than a manual refresh. Everything else on this surface is draft state the user owns directly.
    
    ## Node Inspectors
    
    **Dashboard** nodes expose only a `header`, `main`, and `footer` layout editor. Each region holds an ordered list of elements added from the generic kinds `text`, `count`, `metric`, and `list`. `text` edits static text; `count` and `metric` edit a visible label, and `metric` also binds a field key and a text, number, boolean, or datetime type; `list` edits a title-key binding plus its own display fields, each with a unique non-empty key, visible label, and supported type (`text`, `number`, `boolean`, `datetime`, or `url`, where `url` fields become row links instead of rendered text). The inspector explains that the node becomes the Home board only after Publish, that Home reads its output from a successful Run, and that the board title is the Workflow name.
    
    **Agent** nodes are created without selecting a standalone Agent. Their inspector directly exposes a public model selector, system prompt, Skill multi-selection, MCP server multi-selection, output format, and error policy. Skill and MCP choices come only from real workspace resources.
    
    **Choice Branch** nodes expose no provider-specific configuration. Their inspector explains that the JSON value is passed through and that outgoing conditions are evaluated in connection order, with only the first match or first fallback traversed. Use the edge inspector to configure JSON paths such as `$.articleType` and their comparison values.
    
    **TypeSafe System One** nodes expose a TypeSafe public model selector and a structured JSON `questions` editor. The required `state` input is supplied by a connected JSON upstream node. The inspector explains that the request is forwarded as typed state and questions, that object state remains available in the output, and that typed answers support downstream routing.
    
    **TypeSafe System One Map** nodes reuse that model selector, questions editor, and error policy, because those controls mean the same thing for both nodes. They add an items path naming the array inside the connected state, an optional context path for the shared value sent beside every element, an optional concurrent-request bound, and an optional ranking answer path. Order, result limit, and minimum score are disclosed only after a ranking path exists, so no control is shown that would order nothing. The questions hint states that the question set is sent once per element rather than once per Run, and the node body shows the selected model, the items path, and the question count.
    
    **Artifact** nodes expose name and artifact-type controls and explain that a successful Run creates the Artifact while the node output carries its reference.
    
    **Artifact Query** nodes expose the JSON Artifact name, title field, and description fields as labeled controls. The inspector explains that the query reads all matching workspace history, including detached Artifacts and unfinished Research Notes, without editing them, and that the output carries the original request and candidate metadata. An empty result is an empty candidate list, not an error.
    
    **Image** inspectors present the fixed model and compact count, background, quality, and size controls.
    
    **WeChat Official Account Publish** inspectors select the configured official account and `Save draft` or `Publish` mode. The required cover input is reserved for a Workflow Image output; the inspector explains that the generated PNG is uploaded through the real MP cover picker and never offers a placeholder fallback. Metadata may provide a title override, author, and digest; otherwise the node reads the first Markdown heading as the title. The inspector explains that Publish may pause the Run for login or final confirmation. Workflows containing both an enabled Timer and a Publish-mode WeChat node are invalid in the initial increment.
    
    **Timer** inspectors expose `enabled` and the interval in minutes with a five-minute minimum, and explain that draft Timer changes become active only after Publish. For a published Workflow the inspector also shows read-only runtime status when available: the bound published version, next-run time, and last-run status.
    
    Node surfaces, default icons, and ordinary hover states remain neutral; selected, focused, or actively executing states may use the brand token. Every control requires an accessible label and a non-color status cue in both themes.
    
    ## States
    
    | State | Behavior |
    | --- | --- |
    | Loading | An existing Workflow's draft loads into a content-shaped canvas and panel rather than an empty graph. A new Workflow starts empty by definition, not by absence of data. |
    | Empty | An empty canvas states that nodes are added from the palette. |
    | No results | A palette search with no match names the query. |
    | Error | Save, publish, run, export, and delete failures stay visible next to their action or affected content. The Timer schedule region reports its own unavailability without affecting the rest of the inspector. |
    | Busy | Save reports through the save state; run, publish, export, and delete report on their own controls. Undo and redo disable only while a save is in flight. |
    | Offline | Inherits `shared-states.md`. Draft edits are local until saved, and the offline bar states that. |
    | Long content | The canvas pans and zooms rather than growing the page. The contextual panel scrolls internally. The output panel shows only persisted output from a selected run and never seeded logs. |
    
    The output panel contains only persisted output from a selected run. AI editing controls appear only when a server-backed proposal operation exists and never simulate an applied edit.

    ## Accessibility
    
    The graph is fully operable without pointer dragging: the palette adds nodes, and the inspector reviews, configures, and removes both nodes and edges. Selection stays synchronized between the canvas and the panel so keyboard focus and inspector content never disagree.
    
    Port labels and accessible names identify context and output semantics without relying on color. Persimmon marks selection and current execution only; completion and failure use semantic markers alongside text. Every icon-only control in the context bar and canvas carries an accessible name, and the zoom, fit-view, and deletion controls keep `40px` to `44px` touch targets at mobile widths. Save failures use `role="alert"`.
    
    ## Coverage Status
    
    Verified 2026-09-22. Differences found against `apps/web/src/routes/workflows/$workflowId.tsx`:
    
    - ~~The editor had no reusable JSON Choice Branch node.~~ Resolved: the palette, canvas, inspector, and graph serializer now expose `worklite/branch@1`; its outgoing conditions select one route in definition order.
    
    - ~~The editor had no TypeSafe System One Workflow node.~~ Resolved: the palette, canvas, inspector, and graph serializer now expose `typesafe/systemone@1`; its `state` input and typed `answers` output use the existing JSON port and edge-condition contract.
    
    - ~~`Run` created a Run but left the editor as the active surface.~~ Resolved: successful creation now navigates to the returned `/runs/:runId` detail route.
    
    - No loading state for an existing Workflow. `useWorkflowQuery` destructures only `data`, so a pending load renders an empty canvas that is indistinguishable from an empty graph; the name field shows `editor.untitled` until the draft arrives.
    - No load-failure state. A failed Workflow query leaves the editor on an empty canvas with no explanation, and unsaved work could be attempted against a draft that never loaded.
    - `Publish` has no validation feedback path in the UI beyond a toast: `publishWorkflow` reports failure through `toast.error` only, so a validation failure does not navigate to the affected content as this specification requires.
    - Run, publish, export, and import failures are toast-only. `shared-states.md` requires durable errors to remain in the page; only `save` writes to the persistent `saveError` region.
    - `editor.saveBeforeRun` is reused as the publish precondition message when `isNew`, so publishing a brand-new Workflow tells the user to save before *running* it.
    - 34 locale keys under `workflows:editor.*` are orphaned, enumerated in the Copy Inventory above.
    - `editor.emptyCanvas` is defined and referenced once but the canvas renders no empty-state text region, so an empty graph shows a bare grid.
    - Delete sets `setDeleteBusy(true)` and only resets it inside the `catch`, relying on navigation to unmount the component on success; the busy flag is never cleared on the success path.

    function markdownToHtml(markdown: string): string {
      const { articleMarkdown, referenceHeading, referencesMarkdown } = splitReferences(markdown);
      const context = createCitationContext(parseReferenceEntries(referencesMarkdown));
      const articleHtml = renderTokens(Lexer.lex(articleMarkdown), context);
      const referencesHeading = containsChinese(markdown) ? '相关链接' : referenceHeading ?? generatedReferenceHeading(markdown);
      const referencesHtml = context.entries.length > 0 ? renderReferences(referencesHeading, context.entries) : '';
      return `<section style="${ARTICLE_ROOT_STYLE}">${articleHtml}${referencesHtml}</section>`;
    }
    
    function generatedReferenceHeading(markdown: string): string {
      return containsChinese(markdown) ? '相关链接' : 'Related Links';
    }
    
    function containsChinese(value: string): boolean {
      return /[一-鿿]/.test(value);
    }
    
    function splitReferences(markdown: string): { articleMarkdown: string; referenceHeading: string | null; referencesMarkdown: string } {
      const pattern = /\n?#{1,6}\s*(References|Reference List|Sources|Related Links|参考资料|引用资料|参考链接|相关链接)\s*(?=\n|$)/gi;
      let match: RegExpExecArray | null;
      let last: RegExpExecArray | null = null;
      while ((match = pattern.exec(markdown)) !== null) last = match;
      if (!last) return { articleMarkdown: markdown, referenceHeading: null, referencesMarkdown: '' };
      const headingStart = last.index + (last[0].startsWith('\n') ? 1 : 0);
      return {
        articleMarkdown: markdown.slice(0, headingStart),
        referenceHeading: last[1].trim(),
        referencesMarkdown: markdown.slice(last.index + last[0].length),
      };
    }
    
    function parseReferenceEntries(markdown: string): ReferenceEntry[] {
      const entries: ReferenceEntry[] = [];
      for (const originalLine of markdown.split(/\r?\n/)) {
        const line = originalLine.trim();
        if (!line) continue;
        const explicitNumber = Number(line.match(/^\[?(\d+)[.)\]]\s*/)?.[1] ?? null);
        const linkedSources = [...line.matchAll(/\[([^\]]*)\]\((https?:\/\/[^\s)]+)\)/g)];
        if (linkedSources.length > 0) {
          linkedSources.forEach((source, index) => {
            entries.push({ number: index === 0 ? explicitNumber : null, label: cleanReferenceLabel(source[1]), url: source[2] });
          });
          continue;
        }
        const urls = extractUrls(line);
        if (urls.length > 0) {
          urls.forEach((url, index) => {
            entries.push({ number: index === 0 ? explicitNumber : null, label: cleanReferenceLabel(line, url), url });
          });
          continue;
        }
        entries.push({ number: explicitNumber, label: cleanReferenceLabel(line), url: null });
      }
      return deduplicateReferences(entries);
    }
    
    function extractUrls(value: string): string[] {
      return [...value.matchAll(/https?:\/\/[^\s<>() [\]{}'"“”‘’]+/gi)].map((match) => {
        let url = match[0];
        while (/[.,;:!?）)\]}>]$/.test(url)) url = url.slice(0, -1);
        return url;
      });
    }
    
    function deduplicateReferences(entries: ReferenceEntry[]): ReferenceEntry[] {
      const seen = new Set<string>();
      const result: ReferenceEntry[] = [];
      for (const entry of entries) {
        const key = entry.url ?? entry.label.toLowerCase();
        if (seen.has(key)) continue;
        seen.add(key);
        result.push(entry);
      }
      return result;
    }
    
    function cleanReferenceLabel(value: string, url?: string): string {
      let label = value
        .replace(/\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]+\)/g, '$1')
        .replace(/https?:\/\/[^\s<>() [\]{}'"“”‘’]+/gi, '')
        .replace(/[*_`]+/g, '')
        .replace(/^[-*+]\s*/, '')
        .replace(/^\[?\d+[.)\]]\s*/, '');
      if (url) label = label.split(url).join('');
      // Trailing Chinese commas are stripped too: a source line commonly separates its title from the URL
      // with one, and the rendered entry appends its own separator after the label.
      label = label.replace(/^[\s:：\-–—|]+/, '').replace(/[\s:：，,、;；\-–—|]+$/, '');
      return label || '';
    }

        if (entry.number === null) entry.number = nextNumber++;
    # Workflow Editor
    
    ## Route
    
    `/workflows/{new,:workflowId}`
    
    ## Design Source
    
    - `docs/ui-design-system/README.md`
    - Applicable shared specifications in `ui-ux-design/shared/`
    
    ## Implementation
    
    - `apps/web/src/routes/workflows/$workflowId.tsx`
    - `apps/web/src/components/workflow-canvas-nodes.tsx`
    
    ## Purpose
    
    Build and configure a Workflow graph, then publish it as an immutable version that can run.
    
    ## Primary Task
    
    Change the graph and persist the change. Action budget: two — edit the graph, then `Save`.
    
    The budget is above one because the graph is a composite draft rather than a single field: a node addition, a connection, and an inspector change accumulate into one revision, and the user decides when that revision is coherent enough to persist. Autosaving a half-connected graph would produce invalid intermediate revisions in the undo history. The editor compensates by showing `Saving`, `Saved`, and `Unsaved changes` continuously, so the unsaved state is never ambiguous.
    
    `Publish` is a separate, irreversible goal and keeps its own confirmation step.
    
    ## Model
    
    The workflow editor presents a directed control-flow dataflow graph with structured conditional edges and bounded loop edges.
    
    The palette includes Timer, Workflow Input, Agent, Choice Branch, TypeSafe System One, TypeSafe System One Map, Dashboard, Artifact, Artifact Query, Image, and the trusted WeChat Official Account Publish node when its built-in Plugin is available.
    
    - **Timer** is a source trigger with no inputs, one JSON output, an enabled control, and a fixed interval of at least five minutes; each Workflow may contain at most one Timer.
    - **Dashboard** has one required JSON `data` input, one JSON `output` port, and at most one instance per Workflow.
    - **Workflow Input** exposes the run input and may connect explicitly to Agent `context` as the initial token.
    - **Agent** owns its immutable embedded configuration and has one optional `context` input plus one output. When `context` has no explicit Workflow Input edge and no unbounded incoming edge, the initial Agent invocation uses the Workflow Run input, while later bounded-loop traversals supply the next context value. Its inspector selects `Text` or `JSON` output format.
    - **Choice Branch** has one required JSON `value` input and one JSON `output` port. It passes the input through unchanged and evaluates its outgoing unconditional or predicate edges in connection order, traversing only the first match; when no non-fallback edge matches, it traverses the first fallback edge. It can consume JSON from any upstream node.
    - **TypeSafe System One** has one required JSON `state` input and one JSON `output` port. Its inspector selects a configured TypeSafe public model and edits the immutable typed `questions` object. The node forwards the upstream System One response, including `answers`, without chat or Agent adaptation, while retaining object state fields for downstream context; outgoing predicates may address paths such as `$.answers.articleType.choice`.
    - **TypeSafe System One Map** has the same required JSON `state` input and JSON `output` port as TypeSafe System One, and evaluates its typed questions once per element of an array inside that state. Its inspector adds the items path, an optional context path, an optional concurrency bound, and an optional ranking answer path whose order, result limit, and minimum score appear only once a ranking path exists. Ranking is deterministic ordering applied after evaluation, so the inspector presents it as selection rather than as a second question.
    - **Artifact** has one required JSON `data` input, one output, and permits multiple instances; it configures a non-empty display name and a `Text`, `Markdown`, or `JSON` artifact type.
    - **Artifact Query** has one required JSON `request` input and one JSON output; its inspector selects a JSON Artifact name, a top-level title field, and one or more top-level description fields. It reads matching workspace history, including detached Artifacts, and emits the request with compact title-and-description candidates without creating Artifacts.
    - **Image** has one required string `prompt` input and one JSON output. Its inspector fixes `codex/gpt-image-2` and exposes only the supported image count, background, quality, and size choices. The node displays an image summary after execution and never renders or inspects base64 data.
    - **WeChat Official Account Publish** accepts required Markdown `article` and generated cover-image inputs plus optional JSON `metadata`, and outputs a publication reference.
    
    One output may fan out to multiple downstream nodes. Choice Branch output is the deliberate exception to that fan-out behavior: its outgoing routes are exclusive and only the first matching route is traversed. Each named input accepts at most one edge, except Agent `context`, which may combine one unbounded initial upstream edge with one bounded feedback edge. An initial Workflow Input edge must remain unconditional. Edges may be unconditional, predicate-based, or fallback routes. A loop-closing edge must define a positive maximum traversal count, and every possible cycle must cross at least one bounded edge. Dynamic joins and parallel execution remain unavailable.
    
    ## Layout
    
    The context bar contains breadcrumb, saved state, revision history, Workflow settings, Versions, `Export JSON`, the destructive delete action, `Save`, `Run` where valid, and `Publish`.
    
    The editor workspace has a central `@xyflow/react` canvas and one right-side contextual panel. React Flow selection is authoritative and synchronizes the selected node or edge with the panel. With no selection the panel shows the searchable node palette; selecting a node or edge replaces the palette with its inspector; clicking the canvas background or using the inspector's back action clears all graph selection and restores the palette. Palette and inspector content always use the panel's full available width.
    
    The canvas supports node dragging, handle-to-handle connection, edge selection and deletion, pointer-drag panning, free horizontal and vertical trackpad or wheel panning, pinch zoom, zoom controls, and fit-to-view. Ordinary wheel input pans instead of zooming. It intentionally renders no minimap and no canvas-wide selection outline: selected nodes use a persimmon node border, selected edges use a persimmon stroke, and keyboard focus remains visible on the focused node, edge, or control. React Flow primitives follow the resolved light or dark application theme.
    
    On smaller breakpoints the combined contextual panel becomes one drawer or sheet, opens automatically for a canvas selection, and closes when the fixed desktop panel becomes available. A bottom panel shows test output, logs, and artifacts.
    
    Workflow-level settings are grouped into General, Inputs, Execution, and Versioning. General contains the workflow name and publication metadata; Inputs contains the input editor and examples; Execution contains default error policy and runtime defaults; Versioning contains draft, revision, and publication context. Advanced settings stay collapsed until requested. Scheduling is configured only through the Timer node, never through Workflow settings.
    
    ## Interaction Contract
    
    **Add a node.** The searchable palette inserts the node at the center of the visible canvas viewport, selects it, and marks the draft unsaved. Insertion never requires pointer dragging.
    
    **Connect nodes.** Handle-to-handle connection validates against the port rules above. While connecting, compatible and incompatible targets have distinct visual states. An invalid or type-incompatible attempt leaves graph state unchanged and reports concisely. A connection that would close a cycle receives a bounded traversal limit rather than being rejected.
    
    **Configure a selection.** Selecting a node or edge opens its inspector. Node inspectors expose node-owned parameters directly. Edge selection reveals endpoints, routing mode, structured predicate controls, maximum traversals, and a remove command. Predicate controls take a dot-delimited source-output path, a supported comparison operator, and a JSON comparison value when the operator requires one. Fallback routes explain that they run only when no unconditional or predicate edge from the same source invocation matches. Conditional edges show a concise condition label on the canvas; bounded edges use a dashed line and a traversal-limit label. Pointer dragging is never required to review, configure, or remove graph objects.
    
    **Save.** Persists the accumulated revision. The save state reports `Saving` and settles on `Saved`. A failure returns the state to `Unsaved changes` and keeps the reason visible in the canvas region rather than only in a toast. An invalid edge comparison value blocks the save and names that specific problem.
    
    **Undo and redo.** Server-backed revision movement, reported through the same save state. Both controls disable while a save is in flight.
    
    **Run.** Targets the latest published version, is unavailable while the draft has unsaved changes, and labels that version boundary explicitly. The control reports busy on itself. After the server returns the new Run id, navigation enters `/runs/:runId` so the live Run detail becomes the immediate execution surface; Run history remains available in the Workflow List dialog.
    
    **Publish.** Opens a confirmation explaining that publishing locks the embedded Agent configuration and that later draft edits do not change this Workflow or its historical runs. Publication validates bounded-cycle constraints, port rules, public model ids, TypeSafe questions, image generation settings, required WeChat cover connectivity, and selected Skill and MCP availability. Validation failures navigate directly to the affected content.
    
    **Export JSON.** Downloads the current draft in the portable WorkLite format. Unsaved new Workflows must be saved first. The action stays neutral in both themes and does not compete with save, run, or publish.
    
    **Delete.** Opens a confirmation naming the Workflow and explaining permanent removal of its drafts, published versions, schedules, and run history. Success closes the dialog, reports the outcome, and returns to the Workflow list; failure keeps the dialog open with visible feedback.
    
    The Timer inspector's read-only runtime status is the one self-healing value here: it follows the workflow schedule query rather than a manual refresh. Everything else on this surface is draft state the user owns directly.
    
    ## Node Inspectors
    
    **Dashboard** nodes expose only a `header`, `main`, and `footer` layout editor. Each region holds an ordered list of elements added from the generic kinds `text`, `count`, `metric`, and `list`. `text` edits static text; `count` and `metric` edit a visible label, and `metric` also binds a field key and a text, number, boolean, or datetime type; `list` edits a title-key binding plus its own display fields, each with a unique non-empty key, visible label, and supported type (`text`, `number`, `boolean`, `datetime`, or `url`, where `url` fields become row links instead of rendered text). The inspector explains that the node becomes the Home board only after Publish, that Home reads its output from a successful Run, and that the board title is the Workflow name.
    
    **Agent** nodes are created without selecting a standalone Agent. Their inspector directly exposes a public model selector, system prompt, Skill multi-selection, MCP server multi-selection, output format, and error policy. Skill and MCP choices come only from real workspace resources.
    
    **Choice Branch** nodes expose no provider-specific configuration. Their inspector explains that the JSON value is passed through and that outgoing conditions are evaluated in connection order, with only the first match or first fallback traversed. Use the edge inspector to configure JSON paths such as `$.articleType` and their comparison values.
    
    **TypeSafe System One** nodes expose a TypeSafe public model selector and a structured JSON `questions` editor. The required `state` input is supplied by a connected JSON upstream node. The inspector explains that the request is forwarded as typed state and questions, that object state remains available in the output, and that typed answers support downstream routing.
    
    **TypeSafe System One Map** nodes reuse that model selector, questions editor, and error policy, because those controls mean the same thing for both nodes. They add an items path naming the array inside the connected state, an optional context path for the shared value sent beside every element, an optional concurrent-request bound, and an optional ranking answer path. Order, result limit, and minimum score are disclosed only after a ranking path exists, so no control is shown that would order nothing. The questions hint states that the question set is sent once per element rather than once per Run, and the node body shows the selected model, the items path, and the question count.
    
    **Artifact** nodes expose name and artifact-type controls and explain that a successful Run creates the Artifact while the node output carries its reference.
    
    **Artifact Query** nodes expose the JSON Artifact name, title field, and description fields as labeled controls. The inspector explains that the query reads all matching workspace history, including detached Artifacts and unfinished Research Notes, without editing them, and that the output carries the original request and candidate metadata. An empty result is an empty candidate list, not an error.
    
    **Image** inspectors present the fixed model and compact count, background, quality, and size controls.
    
    **WeChat Official Account Publish** inspectors select the configured official account and `Save draft` or `Publish` mode. The required cover input is reserved for a Workflow Image output; the inspector explains that the generated PNG is uploaded through the real MP cover picker and never offers a placeholder fallback. Metadata may provide a title override, author, and digest; otherwise the node reads the first Markdown heading as the title. The inspector explains that Publish may pause the Run for login or final confirmation. Workflows containing both an enabled Timer and a Publish-mode WeChat node are invalid in the initial increment.
    
    **Timer** inspectors expose `enabled` and the interval in minutes with a five-minute minimum, and explain that draft Timer changes become active only after Publish. For a published Workflow the inspector also shows read-only runtime status when available: the bound published version, next-run time, and last-run status.
    
    Node surfaces, default icons, and ordinary hover states remain neutral; selected, focused, or actively executing states may use the brand token. Every control requires an accessible label and a non-color status cue in both themes.
    
    ## States
    
    | State | Behavior |
    | --- | --- |
    | Loading | An existing Workflow's draft loads into a content-shaped canvas and panel rather than an empty graph. A new Workflow starts empty by definition, not by absence of data. |
    | Empty | An empty canvas states that nodes are added from the palette. |
    | No results | A palette search with no match names the query. |
    | Error | Save, publish, run, export, and delete failures stay visible next to their action or affected content. The Timer schedule region reports its own unavailability without affecting the rest of the inspector. |
    | Busy | Save reports through the save state; run, publish, export, and delete report on their own controls. Undo and redo disable only while a save is in flight. |
    | Offline | Inherits `shared-states.md`. Draft edits are local until saved, and the offline bar states that. |
    | Long content | The canvas pans and zooms rather than growing the page. The contextual panel scrolls internally. The output panel shows only persisted output from a selected run and never seeded logs. |
    
    The output panel contains only persisted output from a selected run. AI editing controls appear only when a server-backed proposal operation exists and never simulate an applied edit.

    Human-gated execution is durable. A `Waiting for input` Run keeps its pending action visible across navigation and reload, exposes expiry and recovery controls, and resumes automatically when the server observes completion. QR expiry is a recoverable pending state rather than a failed Run.
    
    A paused Run is active but reversible execution state. It remains visible while suspended, offers resume through one neutral execution control, and keeps cancellation available as a separate terminal intent. Pause and resume report progress on the activated control; a failed command explains itself there without replacing the Run summary.
    
    A failed Run is recoverable at the node the server marks as retryable. Retry is a neutral execution control local to that node entry, not a destructive action and not a Run-level rerun. It reports progress on the control itself, preserves the existing failure reason until execution continues, and surfaces a rejected retry beside that reason rather than replacing it.
    
    ## Truthful Feedback
    
    Success feedback reports an outcome that occurred. A control must not confirm work it did not perform, and a toast must not substitute for the action itself. When a capability is unavailable for the current object, the control is absent rather than present and inert.
    
    ## Long Content and Security
    
    Truncate only summaries and provide expand, copy, download or details access. Inline Agent Skill calls stay collapsed by default, retain status and exit context in their summary, and reveal height-bounded scrollable raw output only on request. Never reveal secrets in fields, logs, errors or audit metadata. Untrusted content is rendered without inline execution.
    
    ## Changelog
    
    ### 2026-09-22
    
    - Added paused Runs as reversible active execution state with neutral resume feedback, preserved Run visibility, and an independent cancellation intent.
    
    ### 2026-09-21
    
    - Replaced the unqueued-draft rule with a visible removable FIFO queue for drafts submitted during an active Agent turn, including its pause conditions on failure, stop, and pending clarification. This supersedes the 2026-08-27 removal of message queuing.
    - Required streaming surfaces to offer an explicit return-to-end control while the reader is away from the end.
    
    ### 2026-09-19
    
    - Assigned the shell-level pending and error boundaries to the router so every route inherits a content-shaped skeleton and a recoverable failure.
    - Required detail routes to distinguish loading, not-found, and load failure instead of presenting a pending fetch as a missing object.
    - Prohibited rendering the frame of absent content beside a skeleton, and required optimistic application with rollback for reversible local mutations.
    - Required empty and no-results to branch on the unfiltered collection, and prohibited permanent placeholder columns with no data source.
    - Added Truthful Feedback: success confirms work that occurred, and an unavailable capability omits its control rather than presenting it inert.
    
    ### 2026-09-18
    
    - Added node-scoped failed-Run recovery: a neutral retry control on the server-marked retryable node entry, with control-local progress and preserved failure reasons.
