    # Workspace Shell
    
    ## Structure
    
    Use a persistent `232px` sidebar, a `52px` context bar, fluid main content, an optional `360px` inspector, and an optional resizable bottom run panel. The sidebar collapses to `56px` only between `768px` and `1023px`.
    
    Primary navigation is grouped and single-level. It contains six direct destinations: **Workspace** contains `Home` and `Workflows`; **Capabilities** contains `Plugins`, with `Skills` and `MCP Servers` available as capability sub-navigation; **Configuration** contains `Providers`, `Logs`, and `Settings`.
    
    Providers owns the Model Providers, Portkey Gateway summary, and Codex account views in one page context. Logs owns Gateway transport observability: request statistics and captured request details over one shared time range. The two are separate destinations because one configures upstream dispatch and the other reads what was dispatched. Skills and MCP Servers are the capability destinations; standalone Agents have no page-level destination; Plugins remains its peer. Workflow List owns execution-history access through its per-Workflow Run records dialog, whose expanded Run rows expose Artifacts inline; direct Artifact details provide deeper inspection. At `1024px` and above, the expanded sidebar shows group labels and all destinations. From `768px` to `1023px`, the compact icon rail uses group separators, direct icons, and tooltips. The mobile navigation drawer uses the same grouped destinations. Usage, audit log, and appearance are reached from Settings. Chat Bot is available throughout the workspace shell, presented prominently on Home and as a floating control elsewhere. Counts indicate actionable state only. The WorkLite mark is at the top and the personal preferences menu is at the bottom. The expanded preferences control keeps its neutral status label and shows the application version as a right-aligned monospace label; the compact rail exposes the same version inside the preferences menu.
    
    The selected navigation item uses `brand-subtle`, primary text, and a narrow brand indicator. The selected resource link represents its route family: Skills and MCP Server routes select Capabilities, while Artifact routes select Workflows. Personal preferences stay in the bottom menu.
    
    ## Context Bar
    
    Place navigation and breadcrumb context on the left. Place command search, state, secondary actions, and one primary page action on the right. Move low-frequency actions to overflow and never duplicate the primary action in the page heading.
    
    ## Panels
    
    The inspector opens only for selected contextual content, keeps its header and essential actions available, scrolls internally, and does not discard unsaved work when closed. It may expand to `440px` for structured configuration.
    
    The workspace shell owns the active Chat Bot execution identifier, the transient composer draft, and the pending message queue. Published Workflows are selected per message with `@` mentions and create normal Workflow Runs that remain independent from the Chat Bot session. Messages, plugin process state, script requests, automatic execution state, and results remain server-owned. Page navigation closes the visible conversation without cancelling work; a browser reload fetches the active execution identifier and selected target saved by the browser, and drops the queue, which is session state rather than persisted intent.
    
    Place the Chat Bot interaction surface at the bottom of the content region on every workspace page. Home keeps the single-line input visible by default. Other pages show only a draggable floating Chat Bot icon in the lower-right corner by default; clicking it opens the same raised conversation panel above the current page and focuses the input. Clicking outside an expanded Chat surface closes it while Chat-owned popup menus remain usable. Keep the icon inside the viewport safe area and preserve a keyboard-accessible open action without a visible Tooltip. Center the complete expanded surface and cap it at `1200px`. With a bound provider the expanded composer contains the single-line input and one stable icon-button target without a repeated visible Chat Bot title; the target shows Send while idle and Stop while the active turn is running. The input remains editable in both states. Without a bound provider the expanded surface contains its inline Chat Bot configuration panel instead of an input or send control. Home and other pages use the same personal session, expanded dimensions, and compact execution summary.
    
    The bottom panel defaults to about `240px`, resizes, and collapses to a status strip. Closing hides but never cancels a run. Logs distinguish timestamp, severity, source and content, and auto-follow only while the user is at the stream end.
    
    ## Route Boundaries
    
    The root route owns the pending and error boundaries for every page. An unresolved route renders a content-shaped skeleton inside the stable shell rather than an empty content region; a route that throws renders a recoverable failure whose retry invalidates the router. The sidebar, context bar, and Chat surface remain mounted through both states, so a slow or failed page never collapses the workspace.
    
    There is no separate first-use route family. Home derives first-use completion from persisted server resources, so the shell has no onboarding layout branch and no browser-state onboarding step.
    
    ## Command and User Menus
    
    `Command+K` or `Control+K` opens grouped search, recent destinations, navigation and safe creation commands. Destructive actions are excluded. Opening Chat Bot through the command menu changes the shell-owned conversation state through typed route search and must not rely on an ignored URL flag.     # WorkLite UI/UX Design Index
    
    ## Governance
    
    This directory is the source of truth for page structure, shared UI architecture, implementation sequencing, and page-level acceptance criteria. `docs/ui-design-system/README.md` remains the source of truth for visual language.
    
    Interface specifications follow the page structure rather than a flat filename list:
    
    - Route pages use `pages/<area>/<page>/DESIGN.md`.
    - Multi-page flows use `flows/<flow>/DESIGN.md`.
    - Non-route surfaces use `surfaces/<domain>/<surface>/DESIGN.md`.
    - Shared patterns use `shared/<topic>.md`.
    
    Every `DESIGN.md` follows [TEMPLATE.md](TEMPLATE.md) and keeps its sections in that order. A specification records its route or surface scope, design source, implementation locations, purpose, primary task with a declared action budget, layout, per-action interaction contract, per-state behavior, copy inventory, accessibility, and coverage status. New or changed interfaces must update the affected `DESIGN.md` and this index. Do not maintain a parallel page-specification document system.
    
    A page's Coverage Status is a verification result, not a placeholder. It states the date the document was checked against its implementation and lists the differences found.
    
    The router supplies the shell-level pending and error boundaries through `apps/web/src/components/route-boundaries.tsx`, so a page that has not yet resolved shows a content-shaped skeleton and a page that throws shows a recoverable failure instead of an empty region. A page's own `DESIGN.md` states only what it adds beyond those defaults.
    
    ## Shared Specifications
    
    - [Workspace shell](shared/workspace-shell.md)
    - [Page patterns](shared/page-patterns.md)
    - [Shared states](shared/shared-states.md)
    - [Interaction contract](shared/interaction-contract.md)
    - [Copy standards](shared/copy-standards.md)
    - [Responsive behavior](shared/responsive-behavior.md)
    
    ## Page and Surface Specifications
    
    - [Home](pages/home/DESIGN.md), including the server-derived first-use sequence
    - [Workspace Chat Bot](surfaces/workspace/chat-bot/DESIGN.md)
    - Providers: [Model providers and Portkey Gateway](pages/model-providers/DESIGN.md), including the dedicated Codex Account Pool
    - Logs: [Gateway statistics and request logs](pages/logs/DESIGN.md), including the shared time range
    - Workflows: [List](pages/workflows/list/DESIGN.md), [Editor](pages/workflows/editor/DESIGN.md), [Versions](pages/workflows/versions/DESIGN.md)
    - Runs: [Detail](pages/runs/detail/DESIGN.md), [Node logs](surfaces/workflow-run/node-logs/DESIGN.md)
    - Skills: [List](pages/skills/list/DESIGN.md), [Editor](pages/skills/editor/DESIGN.md)
    - MCP servers: [List](pages/mcp-servers/list/DESIGN.md), [Configuration](pages/mcp-servers/configuration/DESIGN.md)
    - Plugins: [List](pages/plugins/list/DESIGN.md), [Configuration](pages/plugins/configuration/DESIGN.md)
    - Artifacts: [Run artifacts](surfaces/workflow-run/artifacts/DESIGN.md), [Details](pages/artifacts/details/DESIGN.md)
    - Settings: [Usage](pages/settings/usage/DESIGN.md), [Audit log](pages/settings/audit-log/DESIGN.md), [Appearance](pages/settings/appearance/DESIGN.md)
    
    ## Route Map
    
    ```text
    /home
    /model-providers
    /logs
    /workflows/{new,:workflowId,:workflowId/versions}
    /skills/{new,:skillId}
    /mcp-servers/{new,:serverId}
    /plugins
    /plugins/:pluginId
    /artifacts/:artifactId
    /runs/:runId
    /settings/{usage,audit-log,appearance}
    ```
    
    The root route opens Home. `/settings/` opens Appearance. Route layouts and redirects are governed by the shared Workspace shell rather than separate page specifications.
    
    There is no `/onboarding` route family. First use is a server-derived sequence inside Home, so a separate browser-state onboarding flow would duplicate it with a less reliable completion signal.
    
    The `/model-providers` page is the top-level Providers destination. It uses page-level tabs for Model Providers and the dedicated Codex Account Pool; the Gateway summary remains on the Model Providers view.
    
    `/logs` is the top-level Logs destination for Gateway transport observability. It uses page-level tabs for Statistics and Requests over one shared time range. Providers configures what the Gateway dispatches to; Logs reads what it did.
    
    `/runs/:runId` is a Run log-reading destination reached from a Workflow's Run records dialog, not a top-level collection. There is no Run list route: Runs are reached through their Workflow. Provider request observability is not a Settings page: `/settings` keeps the WorkLite-owned Usage and Audit Log read models, which are business records over Runs and resource mutations rather than Gateway transport records.
    
    ## Shared Component Inventory
    
    Theme provider and appearance selector; application shell; router pending and error boundaries; sidebar; context bar; personal preferences menu; command menu; shell-level Chat Bot with plugin picker; shared streaming Markdown response renderer; page heading; form controls and messages; status badge; search, filters, object rows and tables; dialogs and sheets; save indicator; inspector; resizable log panel; React Flow workflow graph canvas; workflow run history dialog; run timeline; node log entry with payload and activity disclosure; plugin configuration; viewers for captured request bodies, run output and artifacts; skeletons, errors, offline banner.
    
    Domain-neutral reusable components belong in the shared UI package. Feature composition remains near its feature. Abstract only demonstrated repeated patterns.
    
    ## Implementation Sequence
    
    1. Foundations: semantic dual-theme tokens, initial theme resolution, typography, focus, motion, controls and feedback.
    2. Personal workspace shell: navigation, context bar, menus and responsive behavior.
    3. Home and collections: Home states and shared collection grammar.
    4. Editors and execution: Agent editor, Workflow graph editor, Workflow run history, logs and artifacts.
    5. Integrations and preferences: Skills, MCP servers and Settings.
    
    Every phase includes both themes, keyboard behavior, loading and failure states.

    function citationNumberFor(url: string, label: string, context: CitationContext): number {
      const existing = context.numbersByUrl.get(url);
      if (existing !== undefined) {
        const entry = context.entries.find((item) => item.url === url);
        if (entry && !entry.label) entry.label = label;
        return existing;
      }
      const number = context.nextNumber++;
      context.entries.push({ number, label: label || referenceSourceLabel(url), url });
      context.numbersByUrl.set(url, number);
      return number;
    }
    
    function renderTokens(tokens: Token[], context: CitationContext): string {
      return tokens.map((token) => renderBlockToken(token, context)).join('');
    }
    
    function renderBlockToken(token: Token, context: CitationContext): string {
      switch (token.type) {
        case 'space':
        case 'def':
        case 'html':
          return '';
        case 'paragraph':
          return `<p style="${PARAGRAPH_STYLE}">${renderInlineTokens((token as Tokens.Paragraph).tokens, context)}</p>`;
        case 'heading':
          return renderHeading(token.depth, renderInlineTokens((token as Tokens.Heading).tokens, context));
        case 'code':
          return `<section style="${CODE_BLOCK_STYLE}"><code style="${CODE_TEXT_STYLE}">${escapeHtml(token.text)}</code></section>`;
        case 'blockquote':
          return `<section style="${BLOCKQUOTE_STYLE}">${renderTokens((token as Tokens.Blockquote).tokens, context)}</section>`;
        case 'hr':
          return '<section style="height:1px;margin:30px 0;background:#e4e4e7;font-size:0;line-height:0;">&nbsp;</section>';
        case 'list':
          return renderList(token as Tokens.List, context);
        case 'table':
          return renderTable(token as Tokens.Table, context);
        case 'text':
          return token.tokens ? renderInlineTokens(token.tokens, context) : escapeHtml(token.text);
        default:
          return escapeHtml(token.raw);
      }
    }
    
    function renderHeading(depth: number, html: string): string {
      const level = Math.min(Math.max(depth, 1), 6);
      return `<h${level} style="${HEADING_LEVEL_STYLES[level]}">${html}</h${level}>`;
    }
    
    function renderList(token: Tokens.List, context: CitationContext): string {
      const tag = token.ordered ? 'ol' : 'ul';
      const listStyle = token.ordered ? 'decimal' : 'disc';
      const items = token.items.map((item) => `<li style="margin:0 0 8px;">${renderTokens(item.tokens, context)}</li>`).join('');
      return `<${tag} style="margin:0 0 18px;padding-left:1.35em;list-style-type:${listStyle};">${items}</${tag}>`;
    }
    
    function renderTable(token: Tokens.Table, context: CitationContext): string {
      const header = token.header.map((cell) => `<th style="${tableCellStyle(true, cell.align)}">${renderInlineTokens(cell.tokens, context)}</th>`).join('');
      const rows = token.rows.map((row) => `<tr>${row.map((cell) => `<td style="${tableCellStyle(false, cell.align)}">${renderInlineTokens(cell.tokens, context)}</td>`).join('')}</tr>`).join('');
      return `<section style="margin:0 0 18px;overflow-x:auto;"><table style="width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;font-size:14px;line-height:1.6;"><thead><tr>${header}</tr></thead><tbody>${rows}</tbody></table></section>`;
    }
    
    function tableCellStyle(header: boolean, align: 'left' | 'center' | 'right' | null): string {
      return `padding:9px 10px;border:1px solid #e4e4e7;text-align:${align ?? 'left'};${header ? 'background:#fafafa;color:#27272a;font-weight:600;' : 'color:#3f3f46;'}`;
    }
    
    function renderInlineTokens(tokens: Token[], context: CitationContext): string {
      return tokens.map((token) => renderInlineToken(token, context)).join('');
    }
    
    function nestedTokens(token: Token): Token[] {
      return 'tokens' in token && Array.isArray(token.tokens) ? token.tokens : [];
    }
    
    function asLinkToken(token: Token): Tokens.Link | null {
      if (token.type !== 'link' || !('href' in token) || typeof token.href !== 'string' || !('tokens' in token) || !Array.isArray(token.tokens)) return null;
      return token as Tokens.Link;
    }
    
    function renderInlineToken(token: Token, context: CitationContext): string {
      switch (token.type) {
        case 'text':
        case 'escape':
          return 'tokens' in token && token.tokens ? renderInlineTokens(token.tokens, context) : renderTextWithCitations(token.text, context);
        case 'strong':
          return `<strong style="color:#18181b;font-weight:600;">${renderInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token), context)}</strong>`;
        case 'em':
          return `<em style="color:#18181b;">${renderInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token), context)}</em>`;
        case 'del':
          return `<del style="color:#71717a;">${renderInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token), context)}</del>`;
        case 'codespan':
          return `<code style="${INLINE_CODE_STYLE}">${escapeHtml(token.text)}</code>`;
        case 'br':
          return '<br>';
        case 'link': {
          const link = asLinkToken(token);
          return link ? renderLink(link, context) : escapeHtml(token.raw);
        }
        case 'image':
          return `<img src="${escapeHtml(token.href)}" alt="${escapeHtml(token.text)}" style="display:block;max-width:100%;margin:0 auto 18px;border-radius:4px;">`;
        case 'html':
          return '';
        default:
          return escapeHtml(token.raw);
      }
    }
    
    function renderLink(token: Tokens.Link, context: CitationContext): string {
      const url = normalizeHttpUrl(token.href);
      if (!url) return renderInlineTokens(token.tokens, context);
      if (isWechatArticleUrl(url)) {
        return `<a href="${escapeHtml(url)}" style="color:#2563eb;text-decoration:none;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(37,99,235,0.35);">${renderInlineTokens(token.tokens, context)}</a>`;
      }
      const plainText = plainInlineTokens(token.tokens).trim();
      const label = !plainText || token.autolink === true || plainText === url ? referenceSourceLabel(url) : plainText;
      citationNumberFor(url, label, context);
      return `<span style="color:#18181b;font-weight:600;">${escapeHtml(label)}</span>`;
    }
    
    function renderTextWithCitations(value: string, context: CitationContext): string {
      let result = '';
      let lastIndex = 0;
      for (const match of value.matchAll(/\[(\d+)\]/g)) {
        const index = match.index ?? 0;
        const marker = match[0];
        const number = Number(match[1]);
        result += escapeHtml(value.slice(lastIndex, index));
        if (!context.entries.some((entry) => entry.number === number)) result += escapeHtml(marker);
        lastIndex = index + marker.length;
      }
      return result + escapeHtml(value.slice(lastIndex));
    }
    
    function plainInlineTokens(tokens: Token[]): string {
      return tokens.map((token) => {
        switch (token.type) {
          case 'text':
          case 'escape':
            return nestedTokens(token).length > 0 ? plainInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token)) : token.text;
          case 'strong':
          case 'em':
          case 'del':
            return plainInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token));
          case 'codespan':
            return token.text;
          case 'br':
            return ' ';
          case 'link': {
            const link = asLinkToken(token);
            return link ? plainInlineTokens(link.tokens) : '';

    ## Error and Permission
    
    Explain failures in user terms, preserve unaffected content, and provide recovery. Durable errors remain in the page rather than only in a toast. Resource errors identify the unavailable item or action without leaking protected details. Agent turns render credential-safe failure reasons and explicit cancellation cues inline; raw provider or SDK errors and malformed tool input are never presentation content.
    
    ## Offline and Streaming
    
    Use a restrained persistent reconnecting bar. Explain whether edits are local, blocked or persisted. Resume run events without duplication. Streaming content preserves scroll position unless the user is following the end, and offers an explicit return-to-end control while they are not. Create the destination response region as soon as a turn starts, retain partial content on failure, and expose a non-color streaming, cancellation, or failure cue without announcing every token to assistive technology. Send becomes Stop until the current turn completes or is cancelled.
    
    Agent composer drafts remain editable during an active turn. A draft submitted during that turn enters a visible removable FIFO queue and sends against the same execution when the turn completes, rather than being discarded: a composer that accepts a keystroke and then drops it reports work it did not do. The queue pauses without losing entries when the turn fails, when the reader stops it, and while a clarification question is pending, because in each case the queued message either depends on a result that did not arrive or would be misread as the answer to the question on screen. A paused queue states that it is paused. The queue is browser-session state and is not persisted.
    
    Human-gated execution is durable. A `Waiting for input` Run keeps its pending action visible across navigation and reload, exposes expiry and recovery controls, and resumes automatically when the server observes completion. QR expiry is a recoverable pending state rather than a failed Run.
    
    A paused Run is active but reversible execution state. It remains visible while suspended, offers resume through one neutral execution control, and keeps cancellation available as a separate terminal intent. Pause and resume report progress on the activated control; a failed command explains itself there without replacing the Run summary.
    
    A failed Run is recoverable at the node the server marks as retryable. Retry is a neutral execution control local to that node entry, not a destructive action and not a Run-level rerun. It reports progress on the control itself, preserves the existing failure reason until execution continues, and surfaces a rejected retry beside that reason rather than replacing it.
    
    ## Truthful Feedback
    
    Success feedback reports an outcome that occurred. A control must not confirm work it did not perform, and a toast must not substitute for the action itself. When a capability is unavailable for the current object, the control is absent rather than present and inert.
    
    ## Long Content and Security
    
    Truncate only summaries and provide expand, copy, download or details access. Inline Agent Skill calls stay collapsed by default, retain status and exit context in their summary, and reveal height-bounded scrollable raw output only on request. Never reveal secrets in fields, logs, errors or audit metadata. Untrusted content is rendered without inline execution.

    function markdownToHtml(markdown: string): string {
      const { articleMarkdown, referenceHeading, referencesMarkdown } = splitReferences(markdown);
      const context = createCitationContext(parseReferenceEntries(referencesMarkdown));
      const articleHtml = renderTokens(Lexer.lex(articleMarkdown), context);
      const referencesHeading = containsChinese(markdown) ? '相关链接' : referenceHeading ?? generatedReferenceHeading(markdown);
      const referencesHtml = context.entries.length > 0 ? renderReferences(referencesHeading, context.entries) : '';
      return `<section style="${ARTICLE_ROOT_STYLE}">${articleHtml}${referencesHtml}</section>`;
    }
    
    function generatedReferenceHeading(markdown: string): string {
      return containsChinese(markdown) ? '相关链接' : 'Related Links';
    }
    
    function containsChinese(value: string): boolean {
      return /[一-鿿]/.test(value);
    }
    
    function splitReferences(markdown: string): { articleMarkdown: string; referenceHeading: string | null; referencesMarkdown: string } {
      const pattern = /\n?#{1,6}\s*(References|Reference List|Sources|Related Links|参考资料|引用资料|参考链接|相关链接)\s*(?=\n|$)/gi;
      let match: RegExpExecArray | null;
      let last: RegExpExecArray | null = null;
      while ((match = pattern.exec(markdown)) !== null) last = match;
      if (!last) return { articleMarkdown: markdown, referenceHeading: null, referencesMarkdown: '' };
      const headingStart = last.index + (last[0].startsWith('\n') ? 1 : 0);
      return {
        articleMarkdown: markdown.slice(0, headingStart),
        referenceHeading: last[1].trim(),
        referencesMarkdown: markdown.slice(last.index + last[0].length),
      };
    }
    
    function parseReferenceEntries(markdown: string): ReferenceEntry[] {
      const entries: ReferenceEntry[] = [];
      for (const originalLine of markdown.split(/\r?\n/)) {
        const line = originalLine.trim();
        if (!line) continue;
        const explicitNumber = Number(line.match(/^\[?(\d+)[.)\]]\s*/)?.[1] ?? null);
        const linkedSources = [...line.matchAll(/\[([^\]]*)\]\((https?:\/\/[^\s)]+)\)/g)];
        if (linkedSources.length > 0) {
          linkedSources.forEach((source, index) => {
            entries.push({ number: index === 0 ? explicitNumber : null, label: cleanReferenceLabel(source[1]), url: source[2] });
          });
          continue;
        }
        const urls = extractUrls(line);
        if (urls.length > 0) {
          urls.forEach((url, index) => {
            entries.push({ number: index === 0 ? explicitNumber : null, label: cleanReferenceLabel(line, url), url });
          });
          continue;
        }
        entries.push({ number: explicitNumber, label: cleanReferenceLabel(line), url: null });
      }
      return deduplicateReferences(entries);
    }
    
    function extractUrls(value: string): string[] {
      return [...value.matchAll(/https?:\/\/[^\s<>() [\]{}'"“”‘’]+/gi)].map((match) => {
        let url = match[0];
        while (/[.,;:!?）)\]}>]$/.test(url)) url = url.slice(0, -1);
        return url;
      });
    }
    
    function deduplicateReferences(entries: ReferenceEntry[]): ReferenceEntry[] {
      const seen = new Set<string>();
      const result: ReferenceEntry[] = [];
      for (const entry of entries) {
        const key = entry.url ?? entry.label.toLowerCase();
        if (seen.has(key)) continue;
        seen.add(key);
        result.push(entry);
      }
      return result;
    }
    
    function cleanReferenceLabel(value: string, url?: string): string {
      let label = value
        .replace(/\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]+\)/g, '$1')
        .replace(/https?:\/\/[^\s<>() [\]{}'"“”‘’]+/gi, '')
        .replace(/[*_`]+/g, '')
        .replace(/^[-*+]\s*/, '')
        .replace(/^\[?\d+[.)\]]\s*/, '');
      if (url) label = label.split(url).join('');
      // Trailing Chinese commas are stripped too: a source line commonly separates its title from the URL
      // with one, and the rendered entry appends its own separator after the label.
      label = label.replace(/^[\s:：\-–—|]+/, '').replace(/[\s:：，,、;；\-–—|]+$/, '');
      return label || '';
    }
    
    function createCitationContext(entries: ReferenceEntry[]): CitationContext {
      const explicitNumbers = entries.map((entry) => entry.number).filter((number): number is number => number !== null);
      let nextNumber = explicitNumbers.length > 0 ? Math.max(...explicitNumbers) + 1 : 1;
      for (const entry of entries) {
        if (entry.number === null) entry.number = nextNumber++;
        if (entry.url && !entry.label) entry.label = referenceSourceLabel(entry.url);
      }
      const numbersByUrl = new Map<string, number>();
      for (const entry of entries) {
        if (entry.url && entry.number !== null) numbersByUrl.set(entry.url, entry.number);
      }
      return { entries, numbersByUrl, nextNumber };
    }
    
    function citationNumberFor(url: string, label: string, context: CitationContext): number {
      const existing = context.numbersByUrl.get(url);
      if (existing !== undefined) {
        const entry = context.entries.find((item) => item.url === url);
        if (entry && !entry.label) entry.label = label;
        return existing;
      }
      const number = context.nextNumber++;
      context.entries.push({ number, label: label || referenceSourceLabel(url), url });
      context.numbersByUrl.set(url, number);
      return number;

    29-## Model
    30-
    31-The workflow editor presents a directed control-flow dataflow graph with structured conditional edges and bounded loop edges.
    32-
    33:The palette includes Timer, Workflow Input, Agent, Choice Branch, TypeSafe System One, TypeSafe System One Map, Dashboard, Artifact, Artifact Query, Image, and the trusted WeChat Official Account Publish node when its built-in Plugin is available.
    34-
    35-- **Timer** is a source trigger with no inputs, one JSON output, an enabled control, and a fixed interval of at least five minutes; each Workflow may contain at most one Timer.
    36-- **Dashboard** has one required JSON `data` input, one JSON `output` port, and at most one instance per Workflow.
    37-- **Workflow Input** exposes the run input and may connect explicitly to Agent `context` as the initial token.
    38-- **Agent** owns its immutable embedded configuration and has one optional `context` input plus one output. When `context` has no explicit Workflow Input edge and no unbounded incoming edge, the initial Agent invocation uses the Workflow Run input, while later bounded-loop traversals supply the next context value. Its inspector selects `Text` or `JSON` output format.
    39-- **Choice Branch** has one required JSON `value` input and one JSON `output` port. It passes the input through unchanged and evaluates its outgoing unconditional or predicate edges in connection order, traversing only the first match; when no non-fallback edge matches, it traverses the first fallback edge. It can consume JSON from any upstream node.
    40-- **TypeSafe System One** has one required JSON `state` input and one JSON `output` port. Its inspector selects a configured TypeSafe public model and edits the immutable typed `questions` object. The node forwards the upstream System One response, including `answers`, without chat or Agent adaptation, while retaining object state fields for downstream context; outgoing predicates may address paths such as `$.answers.articleType.choice`.
    41-- **TypeSafe System One Map** has the same required JSON `state` input and JSON `output` port as TypeSafe System One, and evaluates its typed questions once per element of an array inside that state. Its inspector adds the items path, an optional context path, an optional concurrency bound, and an optional ranking answer path whose order, result limit, and minimum score appear only once a ranking path exists. Ranking is deterministic ordering applied after evaluation, so the inspector presents it as selection rather than as a second question.
    42-- **Artifact** has one required JSON `data` input, one output, and permits multiple instances; it configures a non-empty display name and a `Text`, `Markdown`, or `JSON` artifact type.
    43-- **Artifact Query** has one required JSON `request` input and one JSON output; its inspector selects a JSON Artifact name, a top-level title field, and one or more top-level description fields. It reads matching workspace history, including detached Artifacts, and emits the request with compact title-and-description candidates without creating Artifacts.
    44-- **Image** has one required string `prompt` input and one JSON output. Its inspector fixes `codex/gpt-image-2` and exposes only the supported image count, background, quality, and size choices. The node displays an image summary after execution and never renders or inspects base64 data.
    45:- **WeChat Official Account Publish** accepts required Markdown `article` and generated cover-image inputs plus optional JSON `metadata`, and outputs a publication reference.
    46-
    47-One output may fan out to multiple downstream nodes. Choice Branch output is the deliberate exception to that fan-out behavior: its outgoing routes are exclusive and only the first matching route is traversed. Each named input accepts at most one edge, except Agent `context`, which may combine one unbounded initial upstream edge with one bounded feedback edge. An initial Workflow Input edge must remain unconditional. Edges may be unconditional, predicate-based, or fallback routes. A loop-closing edge must define a positive maximum traversal count, and every possible cycle must cross at least one bounded edge. Dynamic joins and parallel execution remain unavailable.

    49-## Layout
    50-
    51-The context bar contains breadcrumb, saved state, revision history, Workflow settings, Versions, `Export JSON`, the destructive delete action, `Save`, `Run` where valid, and `Publish`.
    52-
    53-The editor workspace has a central `@xyflow/react` canvas and one right-side contextual panel. React Flow selection is authoritative and synchronizes the selected node or edge with the panel. With no selection the panel shows the searchable node palette; selecting a node or edge replaces the palette with its inspector; clicking the canvas background or using the inspector's back action clears all graph selection and restores the palette. Palette and inspector content always use the panel's full available width.
    54-
    55-The canvas supports node dragging, handle-to-handle connection, edge selection and deletion, pointer-drag panning, free horizontal and vertical trackpad or wheel panning, pinch zoom, zoom controls, and fit-to-view. Ordinary wheel input pans instead of zooming. It intentionally renders no minimap and no canvas-wide selection outline: selected nodes use a persimmon node border, selected edges use a persimmon stroke, and keyboard focus remains visible on the focused node, edge, or control. React Flow primitives follow the resolved light or dark application theme.
    56-
    57-On smaller breakpoints the combined contextual panel becomes one drawer or sheet, opens automatically for a canvas selection, and closes when the fixed desktop panel becomes available. A bottom panel shows test output, logs, and artifacts.
    58-
    59-Workflow-level settings are grouped into General, Inputs, Execution, and Versioning. General contains the workflow name and publication metadata; Inputs contains the input editor and examples; Execution contains default error policy and runtime defaults; Versioning contains draft, revision, and publication context. Advanced settings stay collapsed until requested. Scheduling is configured only through the Timer node, never through Workflow settings.
    60-
    61-## Interaction Contract
    62-
    63-**Add a node.** The searchable palette inserts the node at the center of the visible canvas viewport, selects it, and marks the draft unsaved. Insertion never requires pointer dragging.
    64-
    65-**Connect nodes.** Handle-to-handle connection validates against the port rules above. While connecting, compatible and incompatible targets have distinct visual states. An invalid or type-incompatible attempt leaves graph state unchanged and reports concisely. A connection that would close a cycle receives a bounded traversal limit rather than being rejected.
    66-
    67-**Configure a selection.** Selecting a node or edge opens its inspector. Node inspectors expose node-owned parameters directly. Edge selection reveals endpoints, routing mode, structured predicate controls, maximum traversals, and a remove command. Predicate controls take a dot-delimited source-output path, a supported comparison operator, and a JSON comparison value when the operator requires one. Fallback routes explain that they run only when no unconditional or predicate edge from the same source invocation matches. Conditional edges show a concise condition label on the canvas; bounded edges use a dashed line and a traversal-limit label. Pointer dragging is never required to review, configure, or remove graph objects.

    92-

Order, result limit, and minimum score are disclosed only after a ranking path exists, so no control is shown that would order nothing. The questions hint states that the question set is sent once per element rather than once per Run, and the node body shows the selected model, the items path, and the question count.

    161-Use Lucide icons consistently, normally at `16px` and at `18px` in primary navigation. Icon-only controls require an accessible name, tooltip, and an adequate interaction target. Emoji are not product icons.

    163:## Product-Specific Patterns
    164-
    165-### Chat Workflow Mentions
    166-
    167-The embedded Chat Bot mention menu supports published Workflows only. Keep the selected Workflow chip compact and removable so users understand that the mention creates a Workflow Run. Workflow progress uses the existing queued, running, completed, failed, and cancelled status semantics, with text and icon cues in addition to color. Successful Workflow Artifacts appear as restrained transcript cards with a direct details action. Draft Workflows are not listed as runnable mentions.
    168-
    169-### Agents
    170-
    171-Present agents as configurable work units, not cartoon characters. Identity comes from a restrained geometric symbol or letter mark, name, responsibility, model, available skills or tools, ownership, version, and recent run state.
    172-
    173:### AI Response Content
    174-
    175-Use one shared streaming Markdown renderer for model-generated text across Chat Bot and future Agent response surfaces. It must handle incomplete Markdown during streaming, GitHub Flavored Markdown, long words, tables, links, lists, quotations, and fenced code without executing embedded HTML or scripts. Product styling wraps the renderer and uses semantic tokens in both themes; transport parsing and conversation state do not belong inside the renderer.
    176-
    177-In conversational layouts, user messages align to the right in compact neutral bubbles and remain plain text. Agent responses align to the left with a wider, unframed reading column so structured output remains scannable. Alignment, accessible labels, and optional identity marks distinguish speakers without relying on color. Streaming updates follow the end only when the reader was already at the end, and a return-to-end control appears while they are not.
    178-
    179-One Agent turn is one block with one identity mark, however many message segments and Skill calls it contains. Its segments and Skill-call rows share that block's content column, so a turn that answers, runs a script, and answers again reads as one reply instead of as several speakers. Working, cancelled, and failure cues render as inline notes without identity marks, because a status is not a speaker; they remain independent status regions for assistive technology.
    180-
    181-Create a Chat Bot response placeholder in the transcript as soon as a turn starts. Show restrained inline progress there instead of replacing or disabling the composer. While a turn is running, keep the draft input editable and replace the send control with a familiar square Stop icon; stopping is a neutral execution control rather than a destructive action. Preserve the draft after completion or cancellation, and use text plus icon cues for working and cancelled states.
    182-
    183-A message submitted during a running turn joins a visible removable queue and sends when that turn completes. A composer that accepts a keystroke and silently discards it reports work the product did not do, so queuing is the honest behavior for input the reader has already committed. Queue rows are restrained neutral transcript entries with a count and a per-row remove control, not a second execution surface. The queue pauses in place — keeping every entry and its order — when the turn fails, when the reader stops it, and while a clarification question is pending, and it says that it is paused.
    184-
    185-Present inline Skill calls as compact disclosure rows by default. The collapsed row keeps the Skill identity, script name, execution status, and exit code visible without allowing arguments, host details, or raw output to dominate the transcript. A keyboard-accessible disclosure control reveals the complete metadata, warning, and a height-bounded internally scrollable output region. Failed calls remain collapsed unless the user opens them.
    186-
    187-Treat `@` selection in the Chat Bot composer as structured dispatch, not decorated message text. Opening `@` presents a searchable keyboard-accessible published Workflow menu with pointer selection, arrow navigation, `Enter`, and `Escape`. A selection becomes one removable mention token before the task text inside the same bordered input surface; it must not appear as a separate adjacent field or region. Only one Workflow may be selected for a task, and its identity remains visible until dispatch or removal. The token and task text may wrap together within that shared surface on narrow screens. Chat Bot does not expose Agent mentions or child sessions.

    **Agent** nodes are created without selecting a standalone Agent. Their inspector directly exposes a public model selector, system prompt, Skill multi-selection, MCP server multi-selection, output format, and error policy. Skill and MCP choices come only from real workspace resources.
    
    **Choice Branch** nodes expose no provider-specific configuration. Their inspector explains that the JSON value is passed through and that outgoing conditions are evaluated in connection order, with only the first match or first fallback traversed. Use the edge inspector to configure JSON paths such as `$.articleType` and their comparison values.
    
    **TypeSafe System One** nodes expose a TypeSafe public model selector and a structured JSON `questions` editor. The required `state` input is supplied by a connected JSON upstream node. The inspector explains that the request is forwarded as typed state and questions, that object state remains available in the output, and that typed answers support downstream routing.
    
    **TypeSafe System One Map** nodes reuse that model selector, questions editor, and error policy, because those controls mean the same thing for both nodes. They add an items path naming the array inside the connected state, an optional context path for the shared value sent beside every element, an optional concurrent-request bound, and an optional ranking answer path. Order, result limit, and minimum score are disclosed only after a ranking path exists, so no control is shown that would order nothing. The questions hint states that the question set is sent once per element rather than once per Run. The compact node body shows its kind and named ports; the inspector holds the selected model, items path, and question count.
    
    **Artifact** nodes expose name and artifact-type controls and explain that a successful Run creates the Artifact while the node output carries its reference.
    
    **Artifact Query** nodes expose the JSON Artifact name, title field, and description fields as labeled controls. The inspector explains that the query reads all matching workspace history, including detached Artifacts and unfinished Research Notes, without editing them, and that the output carries the original request and candidate metadata. An empty result is an empty candidate list, not an error.
    
    **Image** inspectors present the fixed model and compact count, background, quality, and size controls.
    
    **WeChat Official Account Publish** inspectors select the configured official account and `Save draft` or `Publish` mode. The required cover input is reserved for a Workflow Image output; the inspector explains that the generated PNG is uploaded through the real MP cover picker and never offers a placeholder fallback. Metadata may provide a title override, author, and digest; otherwise the node reads the first Markdown heading as the title. The inspector explains that Publish may pause the Run for login or final confirmation. Workflows containing both an enabled Timer and a Publish-mode WeChat node are invalid in the initial increment.
    
    **Timer** inspectors expose `enabled` and the interval in minutes with a five-minute minimum, and explain that draft Timer changes become active only after Publish. For a published Workflow the inspector also shows read-only runtime status when available: the bound published version, next-run time, and last-run status.
    
    Node surfaces, default icons, and ordinary hover states remain neutral; selected, focused, or actively executing states may use the brand token. Every control requires an accessible label and a non-color status cue in both themes.
    
    ## States
    
    | State | Behavior |
    | --- | --- |
    | Loading | An existing Workflow's draft loads into a content-shaped canvas and panel rather than an empty graph. A new Workflow starts empty by definition, not by absence of data. |
    | Empty | An empty canvas states that nodes are added from the palette. |
    | No results | A palette search with no match names the query. |
    | Error | Save, publish, run, export, and delete failures stay visible next to their action or affected content. The Timer schedule region reports its own unavailability without affecting the rest of the inspector. |
    | Busy | Save reports through the save state; run, publish, export, and delete report on their own controls. Undo and redo disable only while a save is in flight. |
    | Offline | Inherits `shared-states.md`. Draft edits are local until saved, and the offline bar states that. |
    # WorkLite UI/UX Design Index
    
    ## Governance
    
    This directory is the source of truth for page structure, shared UI architecture, implementation sequencing, and page-level acceptance criteria. `docs/ui-design-system/README.md` remains the source of truth for visual language.
    
    Interface specifications follow the page structure rather than a flat filename list:
    
    - Route pages use `pages/<area>/<page>/DESIGN.md`.
    - Multi-page flows use `flows/<flow>/DESIGN.md`.
    - Non-route surfaces use `surfaces/<domain>/<surface>/DESIGN.md`.
    - Shared patterns use `shared/<topic>.md`.
    
    Every `DESIGN.md` follows [TEMPLATE.md](TEMPLATE.md) and keeps its sections in that order. A specification records its route or surface scope, design source, implementation locations, purpose, primary task with a declared action budget, layout, per-action interaction contract, per-state behavior, copy inventory, accessibility, and coverage status. New or changed interfaces must update the affected `DESIGN.md` and this index. Do not maintain a parallel page-specification document system.
    
    A page's Coverage Status is a verification result, not a placeholder. It states the date the document was checked against its implementation and lists the differences found.
    
    The router supplies the shell-level pending and error boundaries through `apps/web/src/components/route-boundaries.tsx`, so a page that has not yet resolved shows a content-shaped skeleton and a page that throws shows a recoverable failure instead of an empty region. A page's own `DESIGN.md` states only what it adds beyond those defaults.

    import { Body, Controller, Get, Header, Headers, Param, Post, Req, Res } from '@nestjs/common';
    import type { Request, Response } from 'express';
    import type { CreateRunRequest, RunProgressEvent } from '@worklite/contracts';
    import { RunsService } from './runs.service';
    
    @Controller()
    export class RunsController {
      constructor(private readonly runs: RunsService) {}
    
      @Get('runs')
      list(@Req() request: Request) {
        return this.runs.list(request, 'personal');
      }
    
      @Get('runs/:runId')
      get(@Req() request: Request, @Param('runId') runId: string) {
        return this.runs.get(request, 'personal', runId);
      }
    
      @Get('runs/:runId/events')
      @Header('Cache-Control', 'no-cache, no-transform')
      async events(@Req() request: Request, @Param('runId') runId: string, @Headers('last-event-id') lastEventId: string | undefined, @Res() response: Response): Promise<void> {
        const afterSequence = parseLastEventId(lastEventId);
        await this.runs.get(request, 'personal', runId);
        response.status(200);
        response.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/event-stream');
        response.setHeader('Connection', 'keep-alive');
        response.setHeader('X-Accel-Buffering', 'no');
        response.flushHeaders();
        let lastSequence = afterSequence;
        let replaying = true;
        let closed = false;
        const pending: RunProgressEvent[] = [];
        const send = (event: RunProgressEvent) => {
          if (closed || event.runId !== runId || event.sequence <= lastSequence) return;
          lastSequence = event.sequence;
          response.write(`id: ${event.sequence}\ndata: ${JSON.stringify(event)}\n\n`);
        };
        const unsubscribe = this.runs.subscribe((event) => {
          if (event.runId !== runId) return;
          if (replaying) pending.push(event);
          else send(event);
        });
        const heartbeat = setInterval(() => response.write(': keep-alive\n\n'), 15_000);
        const cleanup = () => {
          if (closed) return;
          closed = true;
          clearInterval(heartbeat);
          unsubscribe();
        };
        request.once('close', cleanup);
        const replay = await this.runs.events(request, 'personal', runId, afterSequence);
        replay.forEach(send);
        replaying = false;
        pending.sort((left, right) => left.sequence - right.sequence).forEach(send);
        const latest = await this.runs.get(request, 'personal', runId);
        if (latest.status === 'succeeded' || latest.status === 'failed' || latest.status === 'cancelled' || latest.status === 'timed_out') {
          cleanup();
          response.end();
        }
      }
    
      @Post('workflow-versions/:workflowVersionId/runs')
      createForVersion(@Req() request: Request, @Param('workflowVersionId') workflowVersionId: string, @Body() body: CreateRunRequest) {

      }

      }

      async createForVersion(request: Request, workflowVersionId: string, input: CreateRunRequest): Promise<{ runId: string }> {

          .from(workflowVersions)
          .innerJoin(workflows, eq(workflowVersions.workflowId, workflows.id))

        await this.db.update(workflowPendingActions).set({ status: 'cancelled', qrCode: null, updatedAt: finishedAt }).where(and(eq(workflowPendingActions.runId, runId), eq(workflowPendingActions.status, 'pending')));
        await this.db.update(workflowNodeRuns).set({ status: 'cancelled', error: 'Workflow run cancelled.', finishedAt }).where(and(eq(workflowNodeRuns.runId, runId), inArray(workflowNodeRuns.status, ['queued', 'running', 'waiting_for_input'])));

        const [version] = await this.db.select().from(workflowVersions).where(eq(workflowVersions.id, run.workflowVersionId)).limit(1);

      async pause(request: Request, workspaceSlug: string, runId: string): Promise<RunView> {
        const team = await this.workspaces.getWorkspace(request, workspaceSlug);
        const now = new Date();
        const pausedRun = await this.db.transaction((transaction) => {
          const [updatedRun] = transaction.update(workflowRuns)
            .set({ status: 'paused', updatedAt: now })
            .where(and(eq(workflowRuns.id, runId), eq(workflowRuns.workspaceId, team.id), inArray(workflowRuns.status, ['queued', 'running'])))
            .returning().all();
          if (!updatedRun) return null;
          transaction.update(workflowNodeRuns)
            .set({ status: 'queued' })
            .where(and(eq(workflowNodeRuns.runId, runId), eq(workflowNodeRuns.status, 'running')))
            .run();
          return updatedRun;
        });
        if (!pausedRun) return this.get(request, workspaceSlug, runId);
        this.activeRuns.get(runId)?.abort();
        await this.publish(runId, 'run.status', { status: 'paused' });
        const [workflow] = await this.db.select().from(workflows).where(eq(workflows.id, pausedRun.workflowId)).limit(1);
        const [version] = await this.db.select().from(workflowVersions).where(eq(workflowVersions.id, pausedRun.workflowVersionId)).limit(1);
        if (!workflow || !version) throw new NotFoundException('Run dependencies not found');
        return this.toView(pausedRun, workflow, version, workspaceSlug, 'You', true);
      }

    # AI Workflows
    
    ## Project Architecture Change Workflow
    
    Use this workflow for changes to system architecture, technology choices, service or domain boundaries, persistence, runtime behavior, security boundaries, repository structure, deployment topology, or any decision documented in `docs/project-architecture/README.md`.
    
    `docs/project-architecture/README.md` is the source of truth for project architecture.
    
    1. Read `docs/project-architecture/README.md` in full before proposing or implementing an architecture change.
    2. Discuss the motivation, alternatives, tradeoffs, migration impact, and implementation boundaries with the user.
    3. Do not modify files or implement the change until the user explicitly confirms the agreed approach.
    4. After confirmation, update `docs/project-architecture/README.md` before changing implementation files.
    5. Update all affected sections so the document remains internally consistent; do not leave obsolete guidance in place.
    6. Add a dated entry to the document's `Changelog` describing the decision and its impact.
    7. Implement only the architecture described by the updated document and only within the approved scope.
    8. If implementation reveals a required deviation or new architectural choice, stop and return to user discussion and explicit confirmation.
    9. Keep code, configuration, tests, and operational documentation consistent with the architecture source of truth.
    10. Report both documentation and implementation changes when handing the task back to the user.
    
    If a request contains architecture and ordinary implementation work, this workflow takes precedence for the architecture portion. After the architecture is approved and documented, apply any relevant implementation workflow to the remaining work.
    
    ## UI Change Workflow
    
    Use this workflow for any user-interface change, including pages, components, layouts, visual styling, design tokens, colors, typography, icons, motion, responsive behavior, themes, user-facing copy, interaction feedback, and workflow-editor presentation.
    
    `docs/ui-design-system/README.md` is the source of truth for UI design principles and visual language. `ui-ux-design/README.md` is the source of truth for page structure, shared UI architecture, implementation sequencing, and page-level acceptance criteria.
    
    1. Read `docs/ui-design-system/README.md` and `ui-ux-design/README.md` in full before proposing or implementing a UI change. Then follow the design index and read every shared document and applicable `DESIGN.md` for the requested surface.
    2. Compare the requested change with the documented principles, tokens, shared patterns, page rules, interaction patterns, and product-specific guidance.
    3. Explain the proposed visual result, affected surfaces, relevant tradeoffs, and any required design-system changes to the user.
    4. Do not modify UI files or implement the change until the user explicitly confirms the proposed approach.
    5. If the proposal introduces or changes a design decision, update the affected `DESIGN.md`, applicable shared specification, and `ui-ux-design/README.md` index before changing implementation files. New pages require a page `DESIGN.md` before implementation.
    6. Implement only the confirmed approach. Use shared semantic design tokens and reusable components; do not introduce page-level hard-coded styles that duplicate or bypass the design system.
    7. Design and implement light and dark modes together. Neither mode may be treated as a fallback or simple color inversion.
    8. Preserve accessibility, including sufficient contrast, visible keyboard focus, non-color status cues, reduced-motion support, and accessible names for icon-only controls.
    9. If implementation reveals a conflict with the design system or requires a new design choice, stop and return to user discussion and explicit confirmation.
    10. Do not create or modify tests. After implementation, only a simple type check is permitted; do not package, build, or run test suites.
    11. Report the design-system basis, shared and page documents read or changed, affected UI surfaces, light and dark mode behavior, and type-check result when handing the task back to the user.
    
    If a request contains both architecture and UI changes, apply the Project Architecture Change Workflow first, then this workflow. This workflow takes precedence over the General Fallback Workflow for UI work.
    
    ## General Fallback Workflow
    
    Use this workflow only when no more specific workflow applies to the user's request.
    
    1. Do not execute the request immediately.
    2. Explain the proposed development approach, intended changes, and relevant implementation considerations to the user.
    3. Wait for the user's explicit confirmation before modifying files or performing any implementation action.
    4. After confirmation, implement only the approved approach and scope.
    5. Do not create or modify test cases for the implementation.
    6. After implementation, only a simple type check is permitted.
    7. Do not package or build the project.
    8. Do not run test cases or attempt other validation commands beyond the permitted simple type check.
    9. Report the implemented changes and the result of the type check, if one was available and performed.
    The Timer inspector's read-only runtime status is the one self-healing value here: it follows the workflow schedule query rather than a manual refresh. Everything else on this surface is draft state the user owns directly.
    
    ## Node Inspectors
    
    **Dashboard** nodes expose only a `header`, `main`, and `footer` layout editor. Each region holds an ordered list of elements added from the generic kinds `text`, `count`, `metric`, and `list`. `text` edits static text; `count` and `metric` edit a visible label, and `metric` also binds a field key and a text, number, boolean, or datetime type; `list` edits a title-key binding plus its own display fields, each with a unique non-empty key, visible label, and supported type (`text`, `number`, `boolean`, `datetime`, or `url`, where `url` fields become row links instead of rendered text). The inspector explains that the node becomes the Home board only after Publish, that Home reads its output from a successful Run, and that the board title is the Workflow name.
    
    **Agent** nodes are created without selecting a standalone Agent. Their inspector directly exposes a public model selector, system prompt, Skill multi-selection, MCP server multi-selection, output format, and error policy. Skill and MCP choices come only from real workspace resources.
    
    **Choice Branch** nodes expose no provider-specific configuration. Their inspector explains that the JSON value is passed through and that outgoing conditions are evaluated in connection order, with only the first match or first fallback traversed. Use the edge inspector to configure JSON paths such as `$.articleType` and their comparison values.
    
    **TypeSafe System One** nodes expose a TypeSafe public model selector and a structured JSON `questions` editor. The required `state` input is supplied by a connected JSON upstream node. The inspector explains that the request is forwarded as typed state and questions, that object state remains available in the output, and that typed answers support downstream routing.
    
    **TypeSafe System One Map** nodes reuse that model selector, questions editor, and error policy, because those controls mean the same thing for both nodes. They add an items path naming the array inside the connected state, an optional context path for the shared value sent beside every element, an optional concurrent-request bound, and an optional ranking answer path. Order, result limit, and minimum score are disclosed only after a ranking path exists, so no control is shown that would order nothing. The questions hint states that the question set is sent once per element rather than once per Run. The compact node body shows its kind and named ports; the inspector holds the selected model, items path, and question count.
    
    **Artifact** nodes expose name and artifact-type controls and explain that a successful Run creates the Artifact while the node output carries its reference.
    
    **Artifact Query** nodes expose the JSON Artifact name, title field, and description fields as labeled controls. The inspector explains that the query reads all matching workspace history, including detached Artifacts and unfinished Research Notes, without editing them, and that the output carries the original request and candidate metadata. An empty result is an empty candidate list, not an error.
    
    **Image** inspectors present the fixed model and compact count, background, quality, and size controls.
    
    **WeChat Official Account Publish** inspectors select the configured official account and `Save draft` or `Publish` mode. The required cover input is reserved for a Workflow Image output; the inspector explains that the generated PNG is uploaded through the real MP cover picker and never offers a placeholder fallback. Metadata may provide a title override, author, and digest; otherwise the node reads the first Markdown heading as the title. The inspector explains that Publish may pause the Run for login or final confirmation. Workflows containing both an enabled Timer and a Publish-mode WeChat node are invalid in the initial increment.
    
    **Timer** inspectors expose `enabled` and the interval in minutes with a five-minute minimum, and explain that draft Timer changes become active only after Publish. For a published Workflow the inspector also shows read-only runtime status when available: the bound published version, next-run time, and last-run status.
    
    Node surfaces, default icons, and ordinary hover states remain neutral; selected, focused, or actively executing states may use the brand token. Every control requires an accessible label and a non-color status cue in both themes.
    
    ## States
    
    | State | Behavior |
    | --- | --- |
    | Loading | An existing Workflow's draft loads into a content-shaped canvas and panel rather than an empty graph. A new Workflow starts empty by definition, not by absence of data. |
    # WorkLite UI/UX Design Index
    
    ## Governance
    
    This directory is the source of truth for page structure, shared UI architecture, implementation sequencing, and page-level acceptance criteria. `docs/ui-design-system/README.md` remains the source of truth for visual language.
    
    Interface specifications follow the page structure rather than a flat filename list:
    
    - Route pages use `pages/<area>/<page>/DESIGN.md`.
    - Multi-page flows use `flows/<flow>/DESIGN.md`.
    - Non-route surfaces use `surfaces/<domain>/<surface>/DESIGN.md`.
    - Shared patterns use `shared/<topic>.md`.
    
    Every `DESIGN.md` follows [TEMPLATE.md](TEMPLATE.md) and keeps its sections in that order. A specification records its route or surface scope, design source, implementation locations, purpose, primary task with a declared action budget, layout, per-action interaction contract, per-state behavior, copy inventory, accessibility, and coverage status. New or changed interfaces must update the affected `DESIGN.md` and this index. Do not maintain a parallel page-specification document system.
    
    A page's Coverage Status is a verification result, not a placeholder. It states the date the document was checked against its implementation and lists the differences found.
    
    The router supplies the shell-level pending and error boundaries through `apps/web/src/components/route-boundaries.tsx`, so a page that has not yet resolved shows a content-shaped skeleton and a page that throws shows a recoverable failure instead of an empty region. A page's own `DESIGN.md` states only what it adds beyond those defaults.
    
    ## Shared Specifications
    
    - [Workspace shell](shared/workspace-shell.md)
    - [Page patterns](shared/page-patterns.md)
    - [Shared states](shared/shared-states.md)
    - [Interaction contract](shared/interaction-contract.md)
    - [Copy standards](shared/copy-standards.md)
    - [Responsive behavior](shared/responsive-behavior.md)
    
    ## Page and Surface Specifications
    
    - [Home](pages/home/DESIGN.md), including the server-derived first-use sequence
    - [Workspace Chat Bot](surfaces/workspace/chat-bot/DESIGN.md)
    - Providers: [Model providers and Portkey Gateway](pages/model-providers/DESIGN.md), including the dedicated Codex Account Pool
    - Logs: [Gateway statistics and request logs](pages/logs/DESIGN.md), including the shared time range
    - Workflows: [List](pages/workflows/list/DESIGN.md), [Editor](pages/workflows/editor/DESIGN.md), [Versions](pages/workflows/versions/DESIGN.md)
    - Runs: [Detail](pages/runs/detail/DESIGN.md), [Node logs](surfaces/workflow-run/node-logs/DESIGN.md)
    - Skills: [List](pages/skills/list/DESIGN.md), [Editor](pages/skills/editor/DESIGN.md)
    - MCP servers: [List](pages/mcp-servers/list/DESIGN.md), [Configuration](pages/mcp-servers/configuration/DESIGN.md)
    - Plugins: [List](pages/plugins/list/DESIGN.md), [Configuration](pages/plugins/configuration/DESIGN.md)
    - Artifacts: [Run artifacts](surfaces/workflow-run/artifacts/DESIGN.md), [Details](pages/artifacts/details/DESIGN.md)
    - Settings: [Usage](pages/settings/usage/DESIGN.md), [Audit log](pages/settings/audit-log/DESIGN.md), [Appearance](pages/settings/appearance/DESIGN.md)
    
    ## Route Map
    
    ```text
    /home
    /model-providers
    /logs
    /workflows/{new,:workflowId,:workflowId/versions}
    /skills/{new,:skillId}
    /mcp-servers/{new,:serverId}
    /plugins
    /plugins/:pluginId
    /artifacts/:artifactId
    /runs/:runId
    /settings/{usage,audit-log,appearance}
    ```
    
    The root route opens Home. `/settings/` opens Appearance. Route layouts and redirects are governed by the shared Workspace shell rather than separate page specifications.
    
    There is no `/onboarding` route family. First use is a server-derived sequence inside Home, so a separate browser-state onboarding flow would duplicate it with a less reliable completion signal.
    
    The `/model-providers` page is the top-level Providers destination. It uses page-level tabs for Model Providers and the dedicated Codex Account Pool; the Gateway summary remains on the Model Providers view.
    
    `/logs` is the top-level Logs destination for Gateway transport observability. It uses page-level tabs for Statistics and Requests over one shared time range. Providers configures what the Gateway dispatches to; Logs reads what it did.
    
    `/runs/:runId` is a Run log-reading destination reached from a Workflow's Run records dialog, not a top-level collection. There is no Run list route: Runs are reached through their Workflow. Provider request observability is not a Settings page: `/settings` keeps the WorkLite-owned Usage and Audit Log read models, which are business records over Runs and resource mutations rather than Gateway transport records.
    
    ## Shared Component Inventory
    
    Theme provider and appearance selector; application shell; router pending and error boundaries; sidebar; context bar; personal preferences menu; command menu; shell-level Chat Bot with plugin picker; shared streaming Markdown response renderer; page heading; form controls and messages; status badge; search, filters, object rows and tables; dialogs and sheets; save indicator; inspector; resizable log panel; React Flow workflow graph canvas; workflow run history dialog; run timeline; node log entry with payload and activity disclosure; plugin configuration; viewers for captured request bodies, run output and artifacts; skeletons, errors, offline banner.
    
    Domain-neutral reusable components belong in the shared UI package. Feature composition remains near its feature. Abstract only demonstrated repeated patterns.
    
    ## Implementation Sequence
    
    1. Foundations: semantic dual-theme tokens, initial theme resolution, typography, focus, motion, controls and feedback.
    2. Personal workspace shell: navigation, context bar, menus and responsive behavior.
    3. Home and collections: Home states and shared collection grammar.
    4. Editors and execution: Agent editor, Workflow graph editor, Workflow run history, logs and artifacts.
    5. Integrations and preferences: Skills, MCP servers and Settings.
    
    Every phase includes both themes, keyboard behavior, loading and failure states.

This supersedes the 2026-09-21 decision that Provider request observability lives with Providers.

A preset persists as its own name and a custom range as absolute instants, so a shared preset link is not frozen into a dead interval.
