    # Workflow Editor
    
    ## Route
    
    `/workflows/{new,:workflowId}`
    
    ## Design Source
    
    - `docs/ui-design-system/README.md`
    - Applicable shared specifications in `ui-ux-design/shared/`
    
    ## Implementation
    
    - `apps/web/src/routes/workflows/$workflowId.tsx`
    - `apps/web/src/components/workflow-canvas-nodes.tsx`
    
    ## Purpose
    
    Build and configure a Workflow graph, then publish it as an immutable version that can run.
    
    ## Primary Task
    
    Change the graph and persist the change. Action budget: two — edit the graph, then `Save`.
    
    The budget is above one because the graph is a composite draft rather than a single field: a node addition, a connection, and an inspector change accumulate into one revision, and the user decides when that revision is coherent enough to persist. Autosaving a half-connected graph would produce invalid intermediate revisions in the undo history. The editor compensates by showing `Saving`, `Saved`, and `Unsaved changes` continuously, so the unsaved state is never ambiguous.
    
    `Publish` is a separate, irreversible goal and keeps its own confirmation step.
    
    ## Model
    
    The workflow editor presents a directed control-flow dataflow graph with structured conditional edges and bounded loop edges.
    
    The palette includes Timer, Workflow Input, Agent, Choice Branch, TypeSafe System One, TypeSafe System One Map, Dashboard, Artifact, Artifact Query, Image, and the trusted WeChat Official Account Publish node when its built-in Plugin is available.
    
    - **Timer** is a source trigger with no inputs, one JSON output, an enabled control, and a fixed interval of at least five minutes; each Workflow may contain at most one Timer.
    - **Dashboard** has one required JSON `data` input, one JSON `output` port, and at most one instance per Workflow.
    - **Workflow Input** exposes the run input and may connect explicitly to Agent `context` as the initial token.
    - **Agent** owns its immutable embedded configuration and has one optional `context` input plus one output. When `context` has no explicit Workflow Input edge and no unbounded incoming edge, the initial Agent invocation uses the Workflow Run input, while later bounded-loop traversals supply the next context value. Its inspector selects `Text` or `JSON` output format.
    - **Choice Branch** has one required JSON `value` input and one JSON `output` port. It passes the input through unchanged and evaluates its outgoing unconditional or predicate edges in connection order, traversing only the first match; when no non-fallback edge matches, it traverses the first fallback edge. It can consume JSON from any upstream node.
    - **TypeSafe System One** has one required JSON `state` input and one JSON `output` port. Its inspector selects a configured TypeSafe public model and edits the immutable typed `questions` object. The node forwards the upstream System One response, including `answers`, without chat or Agent adaptation, while retaining object state fields for downstream context; outgoing predicates may address paths such as `$.answers.articleType.choice`.
    - **TypeSafe System One Map** has the same required JSON `state` input and JSON `output` port as TypeSafe System One, and evaluates its typed questions once per element of an array inside that state. Its inspector adds the items path, an optional context path, an optional concurrency bound, and an optional ranking answer path whose order, result limit, and minimum score appear only once a ranking path exists. Ranking is deterministic ordering applied after evaluation, so the inspector presents it as selection rather than as a second question.
    - **Artifact** has one required JSON `data` input, one output, and permits multiple instances; it configures a non-empty display name and a `Text`, `Markdown`, or `JSON` artifact type.
    - **Artifact Query** has one required JSON `request` input and one JSON output; its inspector selects a JSON Artifact name, a top-level title field, and one or more top-level description fields. It reads matching workspace history, including detached Artifacts, and emits the request with compact title-and-description candidates without creating Artifacts.
    - **Image** has one required string `prompt` input and one JSON output. Its inspector fixes `codex/gpt-image-2` and exposes only the supported image count, background, quality, and size choices. The node displays an image summary after execution and never renders or inspects base64 data.
    - **WeChat Official Account Publish** accepts required Markdown `article` and generated cover-image inputs plus optional JSON `metadata`, and outputs a publication reference.
    
    One output may fan out to multiple downstream nodes. Choice Branch output is the deliberate exception to that fan-out behavior: its outgoing routes are exclusive and only the first matching route is traversed. Each named input accepts at most one edge, except Agent `context`, which may combine one unbounded initial upstream edge with one bounded feedback edge. An initial Workflow Input edge must remain unconditional. Edges may be unconditional, predicate-based, or fallback routes. A loop-closing edge must define a positive maximum traversal count, and every possible cycle must cross at least one bounded edge. Dynamic joins and parallel execution remain unavailable.
    
    ## Layout
    
    The context bar contains breadcrumb, saved state, revision history, Workflow settings, Versions, `Export JSON`, the destructive delete action, `Save`, `Run` where valid, and `Publish`.
    
    The editor workspace has a central `@xyflow/react` canvas and one right-side contextual panel. React Flow selection is authoritative and synchronizes the selected node or edge with the panel. With no selection the panel shows the searchable node palette; selecting a node or edge replaces the palette with its inspector; clicking the canvas background or using the inspector's back action clears all graph selection and restores the palette. Palette and inspector content always use the panel's full available width.
    
    The canvas supports node dragging, handle-to-handle connection, edge selection and deletion, pointer-drag panning, free horizontal and vertical trackpad or wheel panning, pinch zoom, zoom controls, fit-to-view, and an explicit Align flow action. Ordinary wheel input pans instead of zooming. It intentionally renders no minimap and no canvas-wide selection outline. Compact stage nodes show the name, node kind, and named ports; configuration details stay in the inspector. The main path reads left to right, with branches separated vertically. Selected nodes and edges use the blue brand token, and keyboard focus remains visible on the focused node, edge, or control. React Flow primitives follow the resolved light or dark application theme.
    
    On smaller breakpoints the combined contextual panel becomes one drawer or sheet, opens automatically for a canvas selection, and closes when the fixed desktop panel becomes available. A bottom panel shows test output, logs, and artifacts.
    
    Workflow-level settings are grouped into General, Inputs, Execution, and Versioning. General contains the workflow name and publication metadata; Inputs contains the input editor and examples; Execution contains default error policy and runtime defaults; Versioning contains draft, revision, and publication context. Advanced settings stay collapsed until requested. Scheduling is configured only through the Timer node, never through Workflow settings.
    
    ## Interaction Contract
    
    **Add a node.** The searchable palette inserts the node at the center of the visible canvas viewport, selects it, and marks the draft unsaved. Insertion never requires pointer dragging.
    
    **Connect nodes.** Handle-to-handle connection validates against the port rules above. While connecting, compatible and incompatible targets have distinct visual states. An invalid or type-incompatible attempt leaves graph state unchanged and reports concisely. A connection that would close a cycle receives a bounded traversal limit rather than being rejected.
    
    **Configure a selection.** Selecting a node or edge opens its inspector. Node inspectors expose node-owned parameters directly. Edge selection reveals endpoints, routing mode, structured predicate controls, maximum traversals, and a remove command. Predicate controls take a dot-delimited source-output path, a supported comparison operator, and a JSON comparison value when the operator requires one. Fallback routes explain that they run only when no unconditional or predicate edge from the same source invocation matches. Conditional edges show a concise condition label on the canvas; bounded edges use a dashed line and a traversal-limit label. Pointer dragging is never required to review, configure, or remove graph objects.
    
    Selecting a node emphasizes its direct connections and adjacent nodes while softening unrelated paths. Selecting an edge emphasizes that edge and its endpoints. A slow directional stroke on emphasized edges identifies the inspected route; it does not claim that a Run is executing. Selection changes use restrained motion, and reduced-motion settings retain the same static contrast and arrows.
    
    **Align flow.** A canvas action arranges the current graph in left-to-right dependency columns, excluding bounded feedback edges from rank calculation and retaining clear spacing between nodes in each column. It changes draft positions only, preserves node and edge definitions, marks the draft unsaved, and fits the rearranged graph in view. Existing saved positions are left alone until the user invokes this action.
    
    **Save.** Persists the accumulated revision. The save state reports `Saving` and settles on `Saved`. A failure returns the state to `Unsaved changes` and keeps the reason visible in the canvas region rather than only in a toast. An invalid edge comparison value blocks the save and names that specific problem.
    
    **Undo and redo.** Server-backed revision movement, reported through the same save state. Both controls disable while a save is in flight.
    
    **Run.** Targets the latest published version, is unavailable while the draft has unsaved changes, and labels that version boundary explicitly. The control reports busy on itself. After the server returns the new Run id, navigation enters `/runs/:runId` so the live Run detail becomes the immediate execution surface; Run history remains available in the Workflow List dialog.
    
    **Publish.** Opens a confirmation explaining that publishing locks the embedded Agent configuration and that later draft edits do not change this Workflow or its historical runs. Publication validates bounded-cycle constraints, port rules, public model ids, TypeSafe questions, image generation settings, required WeChat cover connectivity, and selected Skill and MCP availability. Validation failures navigate directly to the affected content.
    
    **Export JSON.** Downloads the current draft in the portable WorkLite format. Unsaved new Workflows must be saved first. The action stays neutral in both themes and does not compete with save, run, or publish.
    
    **Delete.** Opens a confirmation naming the Workflow and explaining permanent removal of its drafts, published versions, schedules, and run history. Success closes the dialog, reports the outcome, and returns to the Workflow list; failure keeps the dialog open with visible feedback.
    
    The Timer inspector's read-only runtime status is the one self-healing value here: it follows the workflow schedule query rather than a manual refresh. Everything else on this surface is draft state the user owns directly.
    
    ## Node Inspectors
    
    **Dashboard** nodes expose only a `header`, `main`, and `footer` layout editor. Each region holds an ordered list of elements added from the generic kinds `text`, `count`, `metric`, and `list`. `text` edits static text; `count` and `metric` edit a visible label, and `metric` also binds a field key and a text, number, boolean, or datetime type; `list` edits a title-key binding plus its own display fields, each with a unique non-empty key, visible label, and supported type (`text`, `number`, `boolean`, `datetime`, or `url`, where `url` fields become row links instead of rendered text). The inspector explains that the node becomes the Home board only after Publish, that Home reads its output from a successful Run, and that the board title is the Workflow name.
    
    **Agent** nodes are created without selecting a standalone Agent. Their inspector directly exposes a public model selector, system prompt, Skill multi-selection, MCP server multi-selection, output format, and error policy. Skill and MCP choices come only from real workspace resources.
    
    **Choice Branch** nodes expose no provider-specific configuration. Their inspector explains that the JSON value is passed through and that outgoing conditions are evaluated in connection order, with only the first match or first fallback traversed. Use the edge inspector to configure JSON paths such as `$.articleType` and their comparison values.
    
    **TypeSafe System One** nodes expose a TypeSafe public model selector and a structured JSON `questions` editor. The required `state` input is supplied by a connected JSON upstream node. The inspector explains that the request is forwarded as typed state and questions, that object state remains available in the output, and that typed answers support downstream routing.
    
    **TypeSafe System One Map** nodes reuse that model selector, questions editor, and error policy, because those controls mean the same thing for both nodes. They add an items path naming the array inside the connected state, an optional context path for the shared value sent beside every element, an optional concurrent-request bound, and an optional ranking answer path. Order, result limit, and minimum score are disclosed only after a ranking path exists, so no control is shown that would order nothing. The questions hint states that the question set is sent once per element rather than once per Run. The compact node body shows its kind and named ports; the inspector holds the selected model, items path, and question count.
    
    **Artifact** nodes expose name and artifact-type controls and explain that a successful Run creates the Artifact while the node output carries its reference.
    
    **Artifact Query** nodes expose the JSON Artifact name, title field, and description fields as labeled controls. The inspector explains that the query reads all matching workspace history, including detached Artifacts and unfinished Research Notes, without editing them, and that the output carries the original request and candidate metadata. An empty result is an empty candidate list, not an error.
    
    **Image** inspectors present the fixed model and compact count, background, quality, and size controls.
    
    **WeChat Official Account Publish** inspectors select the configured official account and `Save draft` or `Publish` mode. The required cover input is reserved for a Workflow Image output; the inspector explains that the generated PNG is uploaded through the real MP cover picker and never offers a placeholder fallback. Metadata may provide a title override, author, and digest; otherwise the node reads the first Markdown heading as the title. The inspector explains that Publish may pause the Run for login or final confirmation. Workflows containing both an enabled Timer and a Publish-mode WeChat node are invalid in the initial increment.
    
    **Timer** inspectors expose `enabled` and the interval in minutes with a five-minute minimum, and explain that draft Timer changes become active only after Publish. For a published Workflow the inspector also shows read-only runtime status when available: the bound published version, next-run time, and last-run status.
    
    Node surfaces, default icons, and ordinary hover states remain neutral; selected, focused, or actively executing states may use the brand token. Every control requires an accessible label and a non-color status cue in both themes.
    
    ## States
    
    | State | Behavior |
    | --- | --- |
    | Loading | An existing Workflow's draft loads into a content-shaped canvas and panel rather than an empty graph. A new Workflow starts empty by definition, not by absence of data. |
    | Empty | An empty canvas states that nodes are added from the palette. |
    | No results | A palette search with no match names the query. |
    | Error | Save, publish, run, export, and delete failures stay visible next to their action or affected content. The Timer schedule region reports its own unavailability without affecting the rest of the inspector. |
    | Busy | Save reports through the save state; run, publish, export, and delete report on their own controls. Undo and redo disable only while a save is in flight. |
    | Offline | Inherits `shared-states.md`. Draft edits are local until saved, and the offline bar states that. |
    | Long content | The canvas pans and zooms rather than growing the page. The contextual panel scrolls internally. The output panel shows only persisted output from a selected run and never seeded logs. |
    
    The output panel contains only persisted output from a selected run. AI editing controls appear only when a server-backed proposal operation exists and never simulate an applied edit.

    ## Accessibility
    ## Accessibility
    
    The graph is fully operable without pointer dragging: the palette adds nodes, and the inspector reviews, configures, and removes both nodes and edges. Selection stays synchronized between the canvas and the panel so keyboard focus and inspector content never disagree.
    
    Port labels and accessible names identify context and output semantics without relying on color. Blue marks selection and current execution only; completion and failure use semantic markers alongside text. Every icon-only control in the context bar and canvas carries an accessible name, and the zoom, fit-view, and deletion controls keep `40px` to `44px` touch targets at mobile widths. Save failures use `role="alert"`.
    
    ## Coverage Status
    
    Reviewed 2026-09-23 against `apps/web/src/routes/workflows/$workflowId.tsx` and `apps/web/src/components/workflow-canvas-nodes.tsx`. The compact node, concise route label, selection emphasis, reduced-motion, and explicit alignment behaviors are represented in code; they have not been visually checked in a running browser. Remaining differences found:
    
    - ~~The editor had no reusable JSON Choice Branch node.~~ Resolved: the palette, canvas, inspector, and graph serializer now expose `worklite/branch@1`; its outgoing conditions select one route in definition order.
    
    - ~~The editor had no TypeSafe System One Workflow node.~~ Resolved: the palette, canvas, inspector, and graph serializer now expose `typesafe/systemone@1`; its `state` input and typed `answers` output use the existing JSON port and edge-condition contract.
    
    - ~~`Run` created a Run but left the editor as the active surface.~~ Resolved: successful creation now navigates to the returned `/runs/:runId` detail route.
    
    - The Workflow layout has an explicit Align flow action, but a first-time user must activate it to apply the layered layout; saved coordinates are intentionally preserved on open.
    
    - No loading state for an existing Workflow. `useWorkflowQuery` destructures only `data`, so a pending load renders an empty canvas that is indistinguishable from an empty graph; the name field shows `editor.untitled` until the draft arrives.
    - No load-failure state. A failed Workflow query leaves the editor on an empty canvas with no explanation, and unsaved work could be attempted against a draft that never loaded.
    - `Publish` has no validation feedback path in the UI beyond a toast: `publishWorkflow` reports failure through `toast.error` only, so a validation failure does not navigate to the affected content as this specification requires.
    - Run, publish, export, and import failures are toast-only. `shared-states.md` requires durable errors to remain in the page; only `save` writes to the persistent `saveError` region.
    - `editor.saveBeforeRun` is reused as the publish precondition message when `isNew`, so publishing a brand-new Workflow tells the user to save before *running* it.
    - 34 locale keys under `workflows:editor.*` are orphaned, enumerated in the Copy Inventory above.
    - `editor.emptyCanvas` is defined and referenced once but the canvas renders no empty-state text region, so an empty graph shows a bare grid.
    - Delete sets `setDeleteBusy(true)` and only resets it inside the `catch`, relying on navigation to unmount the component on success; the busy flag is never cleared on the success path.

    function nestedTokens(token: Token): Token[] {
      return 'tokens' in token && Array.isArray(token.tokens) ? token.tokens : [];
    }
    
    function asLinkToken(token: Token): Tokens.Link | null {
      if (token.type !== 'link' || !('href' in token) || typeof token.href !== 'string' || !('tokens' in token) || !Array.isArray(token.tokens)) return null;
      return token as Tokens.Link;
    }
    
    function renderInlineToken(token: Token, context: CitationContext): string {
      switch (token.type) {
        case 'text':
        case 'escape':
          return 'tokens' in token && token.tokens ? renderInlineTokens(token.tokens, context) : renderTextWithCitations(token.text, context);
        case 'strong':
          return `<strong style="color:#18181b;font-weight:600;">${renderInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token), context)}</strong>`;
        case 'em':
          return `<em style="color:#18181b;">${renderInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token), context)}</em>`;
        case 'del':
          return `<del style="color:#71717a;">${renderInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token), context)}</del>`;
        case 'codespan':
          return `<code style="${INLINE_CODE_STYLE}">${escapeHtml(token.text)}</code>`;
        case 'br':
          return '<br>';
        case 'link': {
          const link = asLinkToken(token);
          return link ? renderLink(link, context) : escapeHtml(token.raw);
        }
        case 'image':
          return `<img src="${escapeHtml(token.href)}" alt="${escapeHtml(token.text)}" style="display:block;max-width:100%;margin:0 auto 18px;border-radius:4px;">`;
        case 'html':
          return '';
        default:
          return escapeHtml(token.raw);
      }
    }
    
    function renderLink(token: Tokens.Link, context: CitationContext): string {
      const url = normalizeHttpUrl(token.href);
      if (!url) return renderInlineTokens(token.tokens, context);
      if (isWechatArticleUrl(url)) {
        return `<a href="${escapeHtml(url)}" style="color:#2563eb;text-decoration:none;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(37,99,235,0.35);">${renderInlineTokens(token.tokens, context)}</a>`;
      }
      const plainText = plainInlineTokens(token.tokens).trim();
      const label = !plainText || token.autolink === true || plainText === url ? referenceSourceLabel(url) : plainText;
      citationNumberFor(url, label, context);
      return `<span style="color:#18181b;font-weight:600;">${escapeHtml(label)}</span>`;
    }
    
    function renderTextWithCitations(value: string, context: CitationContext): string {
      let result = '';
      let lastIndex = 0;
      for (const match of value.matchAll(/\[(\d+)\]/g)) {
        const index = match.index ?? 0;
        const marker = match[0];
        const number = Number(match[1]);
        result += escapeHtml(value.slice(lastIndex, index));
        if (!context.entries.some((entry) => entry.number === number)) result += escapeHtml(marker);
        lastIndex = index + marker.length;
      }
      return result + escapeHtml(value.slice(lastIndex));
    }
    
    function plainInlineTokens(tokens: Token[]): string {
      return tokens.map((token) => {
        switch (token.type) {
          case 'text':
          case 'escape':
            return nestedTokens(token).length > 0 ? plainInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token)) : token.text;
          case 'strong':
          case 'em':
          case 'del':
            return plainInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token));
          case 'codespan':
            return token.text;
          case 'br':
            return ' ';
          case 'link': {
            const link = asLinkToken(token);
            return link ? plainInlineTokens(link.tokens) : '';
          }
          case 'image':
            return token.text;
          default:
            return '';
        }
      }).join('');
    }
    
    // Entries read as `[n] label: url` so a reference matches the `[n]` marker the body already uses.
    // The url stays plain text because WeChat strips an off-site anchor from published article bodies.
    function renderReferences(heading: string, entries: ReferenceEntry[]): string {
      const items = entries.map((entry) => {
        const label = escapeHtml(entry.label || (entry.url ? referenceSourceLabel(entry.url) : 'Source'));
        const marker = `<span style="${REFERENCE_MARKER_STYLE}">[${entry.number}]</span>`;
        const url = entry.url ? `<span style="${REFERENCE_URL_STYLE}">${escapeHtml(entry.url)}</span>` : '';
        return `<section style="${REFERENCE_ENTRY_STYLE}">${marker}<span style="${REFERENCE_TITLE_STYLE}">${label}${entry.url ? '：' : ''}</span>${url}</section>`;
      }).join('');
      return `${renderHeading(2, escapeHtml(heading))}<section style="margin:0;padding:0;">${items}</section>`;
    }
    
    function normalizeHttpUrl(value: string): string | null {
      try {
        const url = new URL(value);
        return url.protocol === 'http:' || url.protocol === 'https:' ? url.toString() : null;
      } catch {
        return null;
      }
    }
    
    function isWechatArticleUrl(value: string): boolean {
      try {
        const hostname = new URL(value).hostname.toLowerCase();
        return hostname === 'mp.weixin.qq.com' || hostname.endsWith('.mp.weixin.qq.com');
      } catch {
        return false;
      }
    }
    
    function referenceSourceLabel(value: string): string {

        const team = await this.workspaces.getWorkspace(request, workspaceSlug);
        const [row] = await this.db.select({ run: workflowRuns, workflow: workflows, version: workflowVersions })
          .from(workflowRuns)

          .innerJoin(workflowVersions, eq(workflowRuns.workflowVersionId, workflowVersions.id))

    import type { Request, Response } from 'express';
    import type { CreateRunRequest, RunProgressEvent } from '@worklite/contracts';
    import { RunsService } from './runs.service';
    
    @Controller()
    export class RunsController {
      constructor(private readonly runs: RunsService) {}
    
      @Get('runs')
      list(@Req() request: Request) {
        return this.runs.list(request, 'personal');
      }
    
      @Get('runs/:runId')
      get(@Req() request: Request, @Param('runId') runId: string) {
        return this.runs.get(request, 'personal', runId);
      }
    
      @Get('runs/:runId/events')
      @Header('Cache-Control', 'no-cache, no-transform')
      async events(@Req() request: Request, @Param('runId') runId: string, @Headers('last-event-id') lastEventId: string | undefined, @Res() response: Response): Promise<void> {
        const afterSequence = parseLastEventId(lastEventId);
        await this.runs.get(request, 'personal', runId);
        response.status(200);
        response.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/event-stream');
        response.setHeader('Connection', 'keep-alive');
        response.setHeader('X-Accel-Buffering', 'no');
        response.flushHeaders();
        let lastSequence = afterSequence;
        let replaying = true;
        let closed = false;
        const pending: RunProgressEvent[] = [];
        const send = (event: RunProgressEvent) => {
          if (closed || event.runId !== runId || event.sequence <= lastSequence) return;
          lastSequence = event.sequence;
          response.write(`id: ${event.sequence}\ndata: ${JSON.stringify(event)}\n\n`);
        };
        const unsubscribe = this.runs.subscribe((event) => {
          if (event.runId !== runId) return;
          if (replaying) pending.push(event);
          else send(event);
        });
        const heartbeat = setInterval(() => response.write(': keep-alive\n\n'), 15_000);
        const cleanup = () => {
          if (closed) return;
          closed = true;
          clearInterval(heartbeat);
          unsubscribe();
        };
        request.once('close', cleanup);
        const replay = await this.runs.events(request, 'personal', runId, afterSequence);
        replay.forEach(send);
        replaying = false;
        pending.sort((left, right) => left.sequence - right.sequence).forEach(send);
        const latest = await this.runs.get(request, 'personal', runId);
        if (latest.status === 'succeeded' || latest.status === 'failed' || latest.status === 'cancelled' || latest.status === 'timed_out') {
          cleanup();
          response.end();
        }
      }
    
      @Post('workflow-versions/:workflowVersionId/runs')
      createForVersion(@Req() request: Request, @Param('workflowVersionId') workflowVersionId: string, @Body() body: CreateRunRequest) {
        return this.runs.createForVersion(request, workflowVersionId, body);
      }
    
      @Post('runs/:runId/cancel')
      cancel(@Req() request: Request, @Param('runId') runId: string) {
        return this.runs.cancel(request, 'personal', runId);
      }
    
      @Post('runs/:runId/pause')
      pause(@Req() request: Request, @Param('runId') runId: string) {
        return this.runs.pause(request, 'personal', runId);
      }
    
      @Post('runs/:runId/resume')
      resume(@Req() request: Request, @Param('runId') runId: string) {
        return this.runs.resume(request, 'personal', runId);
      }
    
      @Post('runs/:runId/pending-action/refresh')
      refreshPendingAction(@Req() request: Request, @Param('runId') runId: string) {
        return this.runs.refreshPendingAction(request, 'personal', runId);

        return this.runs.retryNode(request, 'personal', runId, nodeRunId);
      }
    }

    docs/ui-design-system/README.md:266:## Changelog
    - Added the first-party Timer source node with enabled and five-minute-minimum interval controls in the contextual inspector.
    - Made Publish activate Timer changes and removed the independent schedule form from Workflow Execution settings.
    - Defined enabled, interval, bound version, next-run, last-status, unpublished, loading, and failure states without coupling scheduling to Home.
    
    ### 2026-09-10
    
    - Refined successful deletion to close its dialog before showing feedback and returning to the Workflow list.
    - Added permanent deletion for saved Workflows with named confirmation and return to the Workflow list.
    
    ### 2026-09-10
    
    - Replaced standalone Agent and version selection with inline Workflow Agent configuration for model, system prompt, Skills, MCP servers, and error policy.
    - Reduced the Workflow Agent graph contract to one upstream context input and one output.
    
    ### 2026-09-09
    
    - Added the Export JSON action for downloading the current portable workflow draft.
    
    ### 2026-09-01
    
    - Enabled free horizontal and vertical trackpad or wheel panning while retaining pointer-drag panning, pinch zoom, and explicit zoom controls.
    - Merged the node palette and inspector into one right-side contextual panel with selection-driven content and one responsive Sheet.
    - Removed the canvas-wide focus outline and required palette and inspector content to fill the contextual panel width.
    - Unified selection under React Flow, added node-local selection and focus styling, theme-aware edges, visible port labels and connection feedback, textarea wheel isolation, viewport-centered insertion, and responsive panel cleanup.
    
    ### 2026-08-31
    
    - Added Workflow Input, Skill Set, and Agent node presentation with a named context port.
    - Made reusable prompts and Skill authorization visible as graph connections while retaining sequential execution and one edge per input port.
    - Replaced the fixed ordered sequence with an `@xyflow/react` DAG canvas supporting persisted layout, explicit edges, data fan-out, panning, zooming, fit-to-view, and a minimap.
    - Added inline Text editing and contextual node and edge configuration while deferring conditions, joins, loops, and parallel execution.
    - Restored the `@xyflow/react` implementation and removed the minimap while retaining the same graph contract.
    
    ### 2026-08-29
    
    - Removed simulated templates, AI edits and run logs from the editor contract; required real workspace embedded Agent configurations, explicit published-version Run behavior and persisted output only.
    
    ### 2026-08-29
    
    - Defined the first-phase ComfyUI-inspired workspace layout, creation flow, agent palette, grouped settings, and responsive inspector behavior while retaining linear execution.
    - Extended the editor model to generic Text and Agent nodes with immutable embedded Agent configuration and file Artifact context.
    
    ### 2026-08-13
    
    - Established the ordered-step Workflow Editor specification.
    ### 2026-08-28
    
    - Kept selected Agent mentions inline with task text inside one composer input surface.
    - Added structured `@` Agent selection, removable mention tokens, and a compact persistent child-session band for Chat Bot.
    - Adopted Vercel AI Elements' compositional Conversation, Message, and Prompt Input pattern for Chat Bot while retaining WorkLite's semantic tokens, persisted execution state, and shared safe Markdown renderer.
    
    ### 2026-08-27
    
    - Unified interactive component states around a single crisp boundary, a soft gapless focus halo, restrained hover contrast, and consistent invalid and disabled behavior.
    - Made inline Skill calls compact and collapsed by default, with status and exit context retained in the summary and bounded details available on demand.
    - Added transcript-owned Agent working placeholders, editable drafts during execution, and a neutral Stop control that replaces Send for active turns.
    
    ### 2026-08-26
    
    - Added the shared streaming Markdown response pattern for current and future Agent output.
    - Defined right-aligned plain-text user messages, left-aligned unframed Agent responses, secure Markdown handling, and conditional stream following.
    
    ### 2026-08-24
    
    - Adopted the provided orange robot outline as the WorkLite brand mark.
    - Added transparent responsive PNG assets and browser icon variants.
    
    ### 2026-08-25
    
    - Reframed the product UI as a single-user personal workspace.
    - Removed team switchers, member administration, account entry surfaces, and team-specific language from the shared visual model.
    - Kept the same dual-theme tokens, execution semantics, resource density, and accessible interaction requirements.
    
    ### 2026-08-14
    
    - Integrated the internationalization standard into UI copy, layout, and accessibility requirements.
    
    ### 2026-08-13
    
    - Established the WorkLite UI design system as the source of truth for interface changes.
    - Defined a Linear-inspired professional workspace with equal light and dark theme support.
    - Selected persimmon orange as the restrained brand, focus, selection, and execution color.
    - Defined foundational guidance for color, typography, spacing, shape, components, agents, workflows, runs, motion, and accessibility.
    - Aligned the workflow editor with the initial ordered-step architecture and removed free-form graph-canvas guidance.
    - Added the UI implementation specification as the companion source of truth for page-level work.

    function plainInlineTokens(tokens: Token[]): string {
      return tokens.map((token) => {
        switch (token.type) {
          case 'text':
          case 'escape':
            return nestedTokens(token).length > 0 ? plainInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token)) : token.text;
          case 'strong':
          case 'em':
          case 'del':
            return plainInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token));
          case 'codespan':
            return token.text;
          case 'br':
            return ' ';
          case 'link': {
            const link = asLinkToken(token);
            return link ? plainInlineTokens(link.tokens) : '';
          }
          case 'image':
            return token.text;
          default:
            return '';
        }
      }).join('');
    }
    
    // Entries read as `[n] label: url` so a reference matches the `[n]` marker the body already uses.
    // The url stays plain text because WeChat strips an off-site anchor from published article bodies.
    function renderReferences(heading: string, entries: ReferenceEntry[]): string {
      const items = entries.map((entry) => {
        const label = escapeHtml(entry.label || (entry.url ? referenceSourceLabel(entry.url) : 'Source'));
        const marker = `<span style="${REFERENCE_MARKER_STYLE}">[${entry.number}]</span>`;
        const url = entry.url ? `<span style="${REFERENCE_URL_STYLE}">${escapeHtml(entry.url)}</span>` : '';
        return `<section style="${REFERENCE_ENTRY_STYLE}">${marker}<span style="${REFERENCE_TITLE_STYLE}">${label}${entry.url ? '：' : ''}</span>${url}</section>`;
      }).join('');
      return `${renderHeading(2, escapeHtml(heading))}<section style="margin:0;padding:0;">${items}</section>`;
    }
    
    function normalizeHttpUrl(value: string): string | null {
      try {
        const url = new URL(value);
        return url.protocol === 'http:' || url.protocol === 'https:' ? url.toString() : null;
      } catch {
        return null;
      }
    }
    
    function isWechatArticleUrl(value: string): boolean {
      try {
        const hostname = new URL(value).hostname.toLowerCase();
        return hostname === 'mp.weixin.qq.com' || hostname.endsWith('.mp.weixin.qq.com');
      } catch {
        return false;
      }
    }
    
    function referenceSourceLabel(value: string): string {
      try {
        const url = new URL(value);
        const segments = url.pathname.split('/').filter(Boolean);
        if ((url.hostname.toLowerCase() === 'github.com' || url.hostname.toLowerCase() === 'www.github.com') && segments.length >= 2) return `${segments[0]}/${segments[1].replace(/\.git$/, '')}`;
        const host = url.hostname.toLowerCase().replace(/^www\./, '');
        return [host, ...segments.slice(0, 2)].join('/');
      } catch {
        return value;
      }
    }
    
    function escapeHtml(value: string): string {
      return value.replaceAll('&', '&amp;').replaceAll('<', '&lt;').replaceAll('>', '&gt;').replaceAll('"', '&quot;');

      async get(request: Request, workspaceSlug: string, runId: string): Promise<RunView> {

          .from(workflowRuns)
          .innerJoin(workflows, eq(workflowRuns.workflowId, workflows.id))
          .innerJoin(workflowVersions, eq(workflowRuns.workflowVersionId, workflowVersions.id))
          .where(and(eq(workflowRuns.id, runId), eq(workflowRuns.workspaceId, team.id))).limit(1);

    ## Accessibility
    
    The graph is fully operable without pointer dragging: the palette adds nodes, and the inspector reviews, configures, and removes both nodes and edges. Selection stays synchronized between the canvas and the panel so keyboard focus and inspector content never disagree.
    
    Port labels and accessible names identify context and output semantics without relying on color. Blue marks selection and current execution only; completion and failure use semantic markers alongside text. Every icon-only control in the context bar and canvas carries an accessible name, and the zoom, fit-view, and deletion controls keep `40px` to `44px` touch targets at mobile widths. Save failures use `role="alert"`.
    
    ## Coverage Status
    
    Reviewed 2026-09-23 against `apps/web/src/routes/workflows/$workflowId.tsx` and `apps/web/src/components/workflow-canvas-nodes.tsx`. The compact node, concise route label, selection emphasis, reduced-motion, and explicit alignment behaviors are represented in code; they have not been visually checked in a running browser. Remaining differences found:
    
    - ~~The editor had no reusable JSON Choice Branch node.~~ Resolved: the palette, canvas, inspector, and graph serializer now expose `worklite/branch@1`; its outgoing conditions select one route in definition order.
    
    - ~~The editor had no TypeSafe System One Workflow node.~~ Resolved: the palette, canvas, inspector, and graph serializer now expose `typesafe/systemone@1`; its `state` input and typed `answers` output use the existing JSON port and edge-condition contract.
    
    - ~~`Run` created a Run but left the editor as the active surface.~~ Resolved: successful creation now navigates to the returned `/runs/:runId` detail route.
    
    - The Workflow layout has an explicit Align flow action, but a first-time user must activate it to apply the layered layout; saved coordinates are intentionally preserved on open.
    
    - No loading state for an existing Workflow. `useWorkflowQuery` destructures only `data`, so a pending load renders an empty canvas that is indistinguishable from an empty graph; the name field shows `editor.untitled` until the draft arrives.
    - No load-failure state. A failed Workflow query leaves the editor on an empty canvas with no explanation, and unsaved work could be attempted against a draft that never loaded.
    - `Publish` has no validation feedback path in the UI beyond a toast: `publishWorkflow` reports failure through `toast.error` only, so a validation failure does not navigate to the affected content as this specification requires.
    - Run, publish, export, and import failures are toast-only. `shared-states.md` requires durable errors to remain in the page; only `save` writes to the persistent `saveError` region.
    - `editor.saveBeforeRun` is reused as the publish precondition message when `isNew`, so publishing a brand-new Workflow tells the user to save before *running* it.
    - 34 locale keys under `workflows:editor.*` are orphaned, enumerated in the Copy Inventory above.
    - `editor.emptyCanvas` is defined and referenced once but the canvas renders no empty-state text region, so an empty graph shows a bare grid.
    - Delete sets `setDeleteBusy(true)` and only resets it inside the `catch`, relying on navigation to unmount the component on success; the busy flag is never cleared on the success path.
    
    ## Changelog
    
    ### 2026-09-23 - TypeSafe System One Map node

    - Added items path, context path, concurrency, and ranking controls, disclosing ranking order, limit, and minimum only after a ranking path exists so the inspector never shows a control that orders nothing.
    - Introduced no new color, icon, or layout language: the node uses the neutral node surface, the shared single `state` port, and the existing selection, focus, and execution treatments in both themes.

It keeps model selection and typed questions in Workflow configuration, uses the required JSON state port, preserves object state for downstream context, and exposes typed answers for structured routing.

    export function parseCommandEvent(value: string): CommandExecutionEvent {
      const event = JSON.parse(value) as Partial<CommandExecutionEvent>;
      if (
        typeof event.sequence !== 'number'
        || typeof event.commandId !== 'string'
        || (event.type !== 'stdout' && event.type !== 'stderr' && event.type !== 'lifecycle')
        || typeof event.data !== 'string'
        || typeof event.createdAt !== 'string'
      ) {
        throw new Error('The command event stream returned an invalid event.');
      }
      return event as CommandExecutionEvent;
    }
    
    export function parseAgentExecutionEvent(value: string): AgentExecutionEvent {
      const event = JSON.parse(value) as Partial<AgentExecutionEvent>;
      if (typeof event.sequence !== 'number' || typeof event.executionId !== 'string' || !event.data || typeof event.data !== 'object' || typeof event.createdAt !== 'string') {
        throw new Error('The Agent event stream returned an invalid event.');
      }
      return event as AgentExecutionEvent;
    }
    
    export function parseRunProgressEvent(value: string): RunProgressEvent {
      const event = JSON.parse(value) as Partial<RunProgressEvent>;
      if (
        typeof event.runId !== 'string'
        || typeof event.sequence !== 'number'
        || typeof event.type !== 'string'
        || typeof event.occurredAt !== 'string'
      ) {
        throw new Error('The workflow run event stream returned an invalid event.');
      }
      return event as RunProgressEvent;

    # WeChat Article Output
    
    ## Scope
    
    This specification governs the article body produced by the trusted WeChat Official Account Publish node. The editor owns the article title and metadata; Markdown body content is converted to inline-styled HTML before it enters the real WeChat MP editor.
    
    ## Reading Structure
    
    - Keep body copy neutral, at 16px with a 1.9 line height and a two-character first-line indent for paragraphs.
    - Use Mint Cyan `#008D83` consistently for headings. Level-two headings use a soft mint surface and a lighter left bar; level-three headings use a fine neutral rule with a short pale-mint underline. Do not add section numbers.
    - Keep paragraph text, emphasis, quotations, lists, and code neutral. Emphasis may use a pale neutral background; body content must not repeat the heading color.
    - Render fenced code in a monospace face on a light neutral surface with a restrained neutral edge. Preserve whitespace and escape source text. Inline code uses the same neutral family.
    - Keep quotations on a soft neutral surface with a neutral edge and a subtle shadow.
    - Give tables a charcoal header, pale mint top rule, alternating neutral rows, a lightly differentiated first column, and a restrained shadow. Do not use a yellow accent.
    - Keep Markdown hierarchy semantic and retain paragraphs, headings, bold and italic text, quotations, ordered and unordered lists, tables, inline code, fenced code, and horizontal rules.
    
    ## Platform Constraint
    
    Styles are inline because the WeChat editor receives converted HTML. The published body does not depend on preview-only controls, scripts, or external stylesheets. Links outside WeChat article pages continue to render in the generated related-links section.
    
    ## Coverage Status
    
    Reviewed 2026-09-23 against `apps/api/src/modules/plugins/wechat-official-account.service.ts` before the formatting update. The renderer already handled the listed Markdown structures, but headings used inconsistent fixed colors, paragraphs lacked the approved indent and spacing, and tables used a plain gray header. The Mint Cyan treatment and neutral code presentation are being aligned in the implementation.

    $ sed -n '196,276p' docs/ui-design-system/README.md && sed -n '87,102p' ui-ux-design/README.md && git status --short ui-ux-design/README.md ui-ux-design/pages/workflows/editor/DESIGN.md ui-ux-design/shared/wechat-article-output.md docs/ui-design-system/README.md
    - Provide familiar icon controls for zoom in, zoom out, fit view, and deletion.
    - Keep edge direction and handle compatibility visible through shape, persistent port labels, and valid or invalid interaction state rather than color alone.
    - Preserve a keyboard-accessible inspector path for reviewing configuration and removing selected nodes or edges, with an explicit return to the node palette.
    - Keep the contextual panel available at every breakpoint; collapse the combined palette and inspector to one drawer or bottom sheet when the layout cannot support a side panel.
    - Use blue borders or indicators for the selected and currently executing node or edge. Selection belongs to the graph and must remain synchronized with contextual panel content and keyboard focus.
    - Represent successful and failed states through compact green or red markers rather than filling the whole node.
    - Render edges with restrained neutral strokes and reserve stronger treatment for selection and execution.
    - Shorten conditional edge labels to the decision value on the canvas; the inspector retains the full predicate. Selecting a graph item emphasizes its directly connected nodes and edges and softens unrelated paths. A subtle directional animation may run on those selected edges only, with a static equivalent for reduced-motion preferences.
    - Offer an explicit align action for dense graphs. It rearranges draft positions without changing graph behavior and leaves the draft unsaved until the user saves it.
    - Present AI-assisted edits in a side panel and make proposed structured operations understandable and reviewable.
    - Group workflow-level settings into General, Inputs, Execution, and Versioning sections, with advanced fields disclosed progressively.
    
    Restrained blue emphasis communicates graph selection and active execution while neutral surfaces and edges keep dense workflows readable. Directional selection animation indicates the path being inspected, not Run progress.
    
    ### Runs and Logs
    
    Workflow List exposes Run records through a per-Workflow dialog. Use the following canonical run labels: `Queued`, `Running`, `Waiting for input`, `Completed`, `Failed`, and `Cancelled`.
    
    A Run waiting on a human-gated browser action presents a compact amber pending-action panel before its node logs. The panel names the required action and shows the QR image. An expired code is replaced automatically, so the panel shows neither an expiry time nor an instruction to refresh: during replacement the current image dims and a status line reports that a new code is arriving. `Cancel run` remains, because abandoning the Run is a separate intent rather than a recovery from staleness. Authentication state is communicated with text and icon cues; the QR is not the only explanation. Completion updates through the existing Run event stream and does not require a separate “I scanned it” control.
    
    Show the current step and continuing progress for long operations. Expanded Workflow Run records present ordered node execution logs with node identity, status, timing, duration, and retry context. Failed Runs surface the credential-safe failure reason before the log list and repeat it on the failed node entry. Append logs without forcing disruptive scrolling. Use monospace text for identifiers and raw output, and allow users to distinguish timestamps, severity, source, and content. Successful completion should be clear but restrained; failure must include context and a next step where possible. Artifact disclosure is absent when the immutable Workflow version has no Artifact node; an empty Artifact state is reserved for eligible versions that produced none.
    
    Failure is the one node log state that carries a recovery action. When the server reports a failed node entry as retryable, that entry offers a single neutral secondary `Retry node` control beside its failure reason. Retry is an ordinary execution control, not a destructive or primary action, so it uses neutral styling with an icon and text label rather than brand fill or red. Only the retryable entry exposes it; other failed, cancelled, and successful entries show none, and the control never appears at the Run level where it could be mistaken for rerunning the whole Workflow. Activating it shows a local busy state on that control alone, leaves the surrounding log list in place, and keeps any failure text visible until the Run event stream replaces it with continued execution. A retry that the server rejects preserves the original failure reason and explains the rejection in the same entry.
    
    ## Motion
    
    - Hover feedback: approximately `120ms`.
    - Tooltips and menus: approximately `150ms`.
    - Panels and dialogs: `180ms` to `220ms`.
    - Prefer natural ease-out curves.
    - Avoid decorative page transitions, bounce effects, strong zoom, and large animated gradients.
    - Use motion to clarify execution, selection, expansion, and state changes.
    - Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` and retain static state cues when animation is disabled.
    
    ## Accessibility
    
    - Meet WCAG AA contrast for standard text and essential controls.
    - Keep a visible keyboard focus ring in both themes.
    - Do not communicate state using color alone.
    - Provide interaction targets of at least approximately `32px` for compact desktop controls.
    - Associate validation messages with their fields.
    - Make icon controls and complex editor controls accessible by name and keyboard.
    - Preserve a keyboard-accessible alternative for canvas operations.
    
    ## Anti-Patterns
    
    Do not introduce:
    
    - Large areas of blue or decorative AI gradients.
    - Glassmorphism, excessive glow, or pervasive shadows.
    - Oversized marketing typography inside the application workspace.
    - Excessive card nesting or large consumer-style rounded corners.
    - Chat interfaces as the default representation of every AI capability.
    - Decorative robot imagery as the identity of agents.
    - Theme-specific functionality or an unpolished secondary theme.
    - Page-local colors, spacing, or radii that duplicate shared tokens.
    
    ## UI Decision Checklist
    
    Before confirming a UI proposal, verify that it:
    
    - Supports the product character and user task.
    - Uses existing semantic tokens and patterns where possible.
    - Defines both light and dark behavior.
    - Preserves clear information hierarchy at the intended density.
    - Uses blue only for brand, focus, selection, or execution.
    - Includes loading, empty, error, disabled, and long-content states where relevant.
    - Meets keyboard, focus, contrast, reduced-motion, and non-color-cue requirements.
    - Introduces a documented design-system decision before implementation when no existing rule applies.
    
    ## Changelog
    
    ### 2026-09-23 - Workflow canvas readability
    
    - Replaced parameter-heavy canvas cards with compact stage nodes and moved detailed configuration into the inspector.
    - Added direct-connection emphasis, reduced-motion directional selection feedback, concise condition labels, and explicit graph alignment while keeping execution state distinct from selection.
    
    ### 2026-09-22 - Paused Workflow Run
    
    - Added `paused` as a warning status with a non-color pause cue, visually distinct from durable `waiting_for_input` and neutral cancelled execution.
    - Added reversible Run pause and resume controls with control-local progress and retained Run-detail cancellation for paused Runs.
    
    ### 2026-09-23 - WeChat article output
    
    - Added the shared Mint Cyan article-body contract for heading hierarchy, paragraph indentation, neutral content blocks, code, and creative same-family tables.
    
    ### 2026-09-23 - Compact Workflow flow view
    
    - Updated the [Workflow Editor specification](pages/workflows/editor/DESIGN.md) for compact stage nodes, concise route labels, selection path emphasis, reduced-motion directional feedback, and explicit draft alignment.
    
    ### 2026-09-23 - Chat Bot response loading
    
    - Deferred the shared Markdown renderer until the Chat Bot transcript is visible, keeping the collapsed Home transcript mounted and response text readable while the renderer loads.
    
    ### 2026-09-23 - Home Workflow output links
    
    - Updated the [Home](pages/home/DESIGN.md) contract so rows use a top-level `url` from the Dashboard output when the layout has no explicit URL field.

        case 'def':
        case 'html':
          return '';
        case 'paragraph':
          return `<p style="${PARAGRAPH_STYLE}">${renderInlineTokens((token as Tokens.Paragraph).tokens, context)}</p>`;
        case 'heading':
          return renderHeading(token.depth, renderInlineTokens((token as Tokens.Heading).tokens, context));
        case 'code':
          return `<section style="${CODE_BLOCK_STYLE}"><code style="${CODE_TEXT_STYLE}">${escapeHtml(token.text)}</code></section>`;
        case 'blockquote':
          return `<section style="${BLOCKQUOTE_STYLE}">${renderTokens((token as Tokens.Blockquote).tokens, context)}</section>`;
        case 'hr':
          return '<section style="height:1px;margin:30px 0;background:#e4e4e7;font-size:0;line-height:0;">&nbsp;</section>';
        case 'list':
          return renderList(token as Tokens.List, context);
        case 'table':
          return renderTable(token as Tokens.Table, context);
        case 'text':
          return token.tokens ? renderInlineTokens(token.tokens, context) : escapeHtml(token.text);
        default:
          return escapeHtml(token.raw);
      }
    }
    
    function renderHeading(depth: number, html: string): string {
      const level = Math.min(Math.max(depth, 1), 6);
      return `<h${level} style="${HEADING_LEVEL_STYLES[level]}">${html}</h${level}>`;
    }
    
    function renderList(token: Tokens.List, context: CitationContext): string {
      const tag = token.ordered ? 'ol' : 'ul';
      const listStyle = token.ordered ? 'decimal' : 'disc';
      const items = token.items.map((item) => `<li style="margin:0 0 8px;">${renderTokens(item.tokens, context)}</li>`).join('');
      return `<${tag} style="margin:0 0 18px;padding-left:1.35em;list-style-type:${listStyle};">${items}</${tag}>`;
    }
    
    function renderTable(token: Tokens.Table, context: CitationContext): string {
      const header = token.header.map((cell) => `<th style="${tableCellStyle(true, cell.align)}">${renderInlineTokens(cell.tokens, context)}</th>`).join('');
      const rows = token.rows.map((row) => `<tr>${row.map((cell) => `<td style="${tableCellStyle(false, cell.align)}">${renderInlineTokens(cell.tokens, context)}</td>`).join('')}</tr>`).join('');
      return `<section style="margin:0 0 18px;overflow-x:auto;"><table style="width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;font-size:14px;line-height:1.6;"><thead><tr>${header}</tr></thead><tbody>${rows}</tbody></table></section>`;
    }
    
    function tableCellStyle(header: boolean, align: 'left' | 'center' | 'right' | null): string {
      return `padding:9px 10px;border:1px solid #e4e4e7;text-align:${align ?? 'left'};${header ? 'background:#fafafa;color:#27272a;font-weight:600;' : 'color:#3f3f46;'}`;
    }
    
    function renderInlineTokens(tokens: Token[], context: CitationContext): string {
      return tokens.map((token) => renderInlineToken(token, context)).join('');
    }
    
    function nestedTokens(token: Token): Token[] {
      return 'tokens' in token && Array.isArray(token.tokens) ? token.tokens : [];
    }
    
    function asLinkToken(token: Token): Tokens.Link | null {
      if (token.type !== 'link' || !('href' in token) || typeof token.href !== 'string' || !('tokens' in token) || !Array.isArray(token.tokens)) return null;
      return token as Tokens.Link;
    }
    
    function renderInlineToken(token: Token, context: CitationContext): string {
      switch (token.type) {
        case 'text':
        case 'escape':
          return 'tokens' in token && token.tokens ? renderInlineTokens(token.tokens, context) : renderTextWithCitations(token.text, context);
        case 'strong':
          return `<strong style="color:#18181b;font-weight:600;">${renderInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token), context)}</strong>`;
        case 'em':
          return `<em style="color:#18181b;">${renderInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token), context)}</em>`;
        case 'del':
          return `<del style="color:#71717a;">${renderInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token), context)}</del>`;
        case 'codespan':
          return `<code style="${INLINE_CODE_STYLE}">${escapeHtml(token.text)}</code>`;
        case 'br':
          return '<br>';
        case 'link': {
          const link = asLinkToken(token);
          return link ? renderLink(link, context) : escapeHtml(token.raw);
        }
        case 'image':
          return `<img src="${escapeHtml(token.href)}" alt="${escapeHtml(token.text)}" style="display:block;max-width:100%;margin:0 auto 18px;border-radius:4px;">`;
        case 'html':
          return '';
        default:
          return escapeHtml(token.raw);
      }
    }
    
    function renderLink(token: Tokens.Link, context: CitationContext): string {
      const url = normalizeHttpUrl(token.href);
      if (!url) return renderInlineTokens(token.tokens, context);
      if (isWechatArticleUrl(url)) {
        return `<a href="${escapeHtml(url)}" style="color:#2563eb;text-decoration:none;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(37,99,235,0.35);">${renderInlineTokens(token.tokens, context)}</a>`;
      }
      const plainText = plainInlineTokens(token.tokens).trim();
      const label = !plainText || token.autolink === true || plainText === url ? referenceSourceLabel(url) : plainText;
      citationNumberFor(url, label, context);
      return `<span style="color:#18181b;font-weight:600;">${escapeHtml(label)}</span>`;
    }
    
    function renderTextWithCitations(value: string, context: CitationContext): string {
      let result = '';
      let lastIndex = 0;
      for (const match of value.matchAll(/\[(\d+)\]/g)) {
        const index = match.index ?? 0;
        const marker = match[0];
        const number = Number(match[1]);
        result += escapeHtml(value.slice(lastIndex, index));
        if (!context.entries.some((entry) => entry.number === number)) result += escapeHtml(marker);
        lastIndex = index + marker.length;
      }
      return result + escapeHtml(value.slice(lastIndex));
    }
    
    function plainInlineTokens(tokens: Token[]): string {
      return tokens.map((token) => {
        switch (token.type) {
          case 'text':
          case 'escape':
            return nestedTokens(token).length > 0 ? plainInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token)) : token.text;
          case 'strong':
          case 'em':
          case 'del':
            return plainInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token));
          case 'codespan':
            return token.text;
          case 'br':
            return ' ';
          case 'link': {
            const link = asLinkToken(token);
            return link ? plainInlineTokens(link.tokens) : '';
          }
          return;
        }
        try {
          await this.db.transaction((transaction) => {
            transaction.insert(workflowPendingActions).values({ id: action.id, workspaceId, runId, nodeRunId, type: action.type, status: 'pending', title: action.title, description: action.description, qrCode: action.qrCode, expiresAt: action.expiresAt, externalOperationId: action.externalOperationId ?? null }).run();
            const [updatedNodeRun] = transaction.update(workflowNodeRuns).set({ status: 'waiting_for_input', error: null }).where(and(eq(workflowNodeRuns.id, nodeRunId), eq(workflowNodeRuns.status, 'running'))).returning().all();
            const [updatedRun] = transaction.update(workflowRuns).set({ status: 'waiting_for_input', currentNodeId: nodeId, updatedAt: now }).where(and(eq(workflowRuns.id, runId), eq(workflowRuns.status, 'running'))).returning().all();
            if (!updatedNodeRun || !updatedRun) throw new RunCancelledError();
          });
        } catch (error) {
          await this.wechatOfficialAccount.cancel(action.id);
          await this.db.update(workflowPendingActions).set({ status: 'cancelled', qrCode: null, updatedAt: new Date() }).where(and(eq(workflowPendingActions.id, action.id), eq(workflowPendingActions.status, 'pending')));
          this.pendingCompletions.delete(action.id);
          if (error instanceof RunCancelledError) return;
          throw error;
        }
        await this.publish(runId, 'node.waiting', { nodeId, nodeRunId, actionId: action.id, type: action.type });
        await this.publish(runId, 'run.status', { status: 'waiting_for_input', actionId: action.id });
        await this.flushCompletedActions();
      }

    type ReferenceEntry = { number: number | null; label: string; url: string | null };
    type CitationContext = { entries: ReferenceEntry[]; numbersByUrl: Map<string, number>; nextNumber: number };
    
    const ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS = {
      accent: '#008d83',
      accentSurface: '#edf7f6',
      accentBar: '#a8d8d4',
      accentUnderline: '#9ed4d0',
      text: '#292b30',
      mutedText: '#777b83',
      neutralSurface: '#f3f5f7',
      neutralHighlight: '#f8f9fa',
      rule: '#d9dee3',
      tableRule: '#dfe3e6',
      tableHeader: '#303943',
      tableHeaderText: '#f8fafc',
      tableRow: '#ffffff',
      tableAlternateRow: '#f5f7f8',
      tableFirstColumn: '#eef1f3',
    } as const;
    const ARTICLE_SHADOWS = { content: '0 2px 9px rgba(28,53,62,0.07)', table: '0 8px 22px rgba(35,43,50,0.09)' } as const;
    const ARTICLE_ROOT_STYLE = `font-family:-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Helvetica Neue','PingFang SC','Hiragino Sans GB','Microsoft YaHei',sans-serif;font-size:16px;line-height:1.9;color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.text};letter-spacing:0.24px;word-break:break-word;`;
    const PARAGRAPH_STYLE = 'margin:0 0 18px;padding:0;text-align:justify;text-indent:2em;';
    const LEAD_PARAGRAPH_STYLE = `margin:0 0 18px;padding:0 0 0 15px;border-left:2px solid ${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.rule};text-align:justify;text-indent:2em;font-size:17px;font-weight:500;line-height:1.82;`;
    const HEADING_LEVEL_STYLES: Record<number, string> = {
      1: `margin:34px 0 16px;font-size:28px;line-height:1.4;color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.accent};font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-0.4px;`,
      2: `margin:32px 0 16px;padding:7px 12px;border-left:3px solid ${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.accentBar};border-radius:0 6px 6px 0;background:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.accentSurface};font-size:19px;line-height:1.5;color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.accent};font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-0.16px;`,
      3: `margin:25px 0 12px;padding-bottom:7px;border-bottom:1px solid ${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.rule};font-size:16px;line-height:1.55;color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.accent};font-weight:600;`,
      4: `margin:22px 0 10px;font-size:16px;line-height:1.5;color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.accent};font-weight:600;`,
      5: `margin:20px 0 10px;font-size:15px;line-height:1.5;color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.accent};font-weight:600;`,
      6: `margin:20px 0 10px;font-size:15px;line-height:1.5;color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.accent};font-weight:600;`,
    };
    const HEADING_UNDERLINE_STYLE = `display:block;width:24px;height:2px;margin-top:7px;background:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.accentUnderline};font-size:0;line-height:0;`;
    const CODE_BLOCK_STYLE = `margin:0 0 22px;padding:14px 16px;background:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.neutralSurface};border-left:3px solid ${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.rule};border-radius:0 8px 8px 0;box-shadow:${ARTICLE_SHADOWS.content};overflow-x:auto;`;
    const CODE_TEXT_STYLE = `display:block;font-family:SFMono-Regular,Consolas,'Liberation Mono',Menlo,monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.7;color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.text};white-space:pre;`;
    const INLINE_CODE_STYLE = `padding:2px 5px;background:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.neutralHighlight};border-radius:4px;font-family:SFMono-Regular,Consolas,'Liberation Mono',Menlo,monospace;font-size:14px;color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.text};`;
    const BLOCKQUOTE_STYLE = `margin:24px 0;padding:15px 18px;background:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.neutralSurface};border-left:3px solid ${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.rule};border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.text};font-size:15px;line-height:1.8;box-shadow:${ARTICLE_SHADOWS.content};`;
    const REFERENCE_ENTRY_STYLE = 'margin:0 0 10px;';
    const REFERENCE_MARKER_STYLE = `margin-right:4px;font-size:13px;line-height:1.55;color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.text};font-weight:600;`;
    const REFERENCE_TITLE_STYLE = `font-size:13px;line-height:1.55;color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.text};font-weight:600;`;
    const REFERENCE_URL_STYLE = `font-size:12px;line-height:1.55;color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.mutedText};word-break:break-all;`;
    
    function markdownToHtml(markdown: string): string {
      const { articleMarkdown, referenceHeading, referencesMarkdown } = splitReferences(markdown);
      const context = createCitationContext(parseReferenceEntries(referencesMarkdown));
      const articleHtml = renderTokens(Lexer.lex(articleMarkdown), context, true);
      const referencesHeading = containsChinese(markdown) ? '相关链接' : referenceHeading ?? generatedReferenceHeading(markdown);
      const referencesHtml = context.entries.length > 0 ? renderReferences(referencesHeading, context.entries) : '';
      return `<section style="${ARTICLE_ROOT_STYLE}">${articleHtml}${referencesHtml}</section>`;
    }
    
    function generatedReferenceHeading(markdown: string): string {
      return containsChinese(markdown) ? '相关链接' : 'Related Links';
    }
    
    function containsChinese(value: string): boolean {
      return /[一-鿿]/.test(value);
    function citationNumberFor(url: string, label: string, context: CitationContext): number {
      const existing = context.numbersByUrl.get(url);
      if (existing !== undefined) {
        const entry = context.entries.find((item) => item.url === url);
        if (entry && !entry.label) entry.label = label;
        return existing;
      }
      const number = context.nextNumber++;
      context.entries.push({ number, label: label || referenceSourceLabel(url), url });
      context.numbersByUrl.set(url, number);
      return number;
    }
    
    function renderTokens(tokens: Token[], context: CitationContext, decorateLeadParagraph = false): string {
      const leadParagraphIndex = decorateLeadParagraph ? tokens.findIndex((token) => token.type === 'paragraph') : -1;
      return tokens.map((token, index) => renderBlockToken(token, context, index === leadParagraphIndex)).join('');
    }
    
    function renderBlockToken(token: Token, context: CitationContext, isLeadParagraph = false): string {
      switch (token.type) {
        case 'space':
        case 'def':
        case 'html':
          return '';
        case 'paragraph':
          return `<p style="${isLeadParagraph ? LEAD_PARAGRAPH_STYLE : PARAGRAPH_STYLE}">${renderInlineTokens((token as Tokens.Paragraph).tokens, context)}</p>`;
        case 'heading':
          return renderHeading(token.depth, renderInlineTokens((token as Tokens.Heading).tokens, context));
        case 'code':
          return `<section style="${CODE_BLOCK_STYLE}"><code style="${CODE_TEXT_STYLE}">${escapeHtml(token.text)}</code></section>`;
        case 'blockquote':
          return `<section style="${BLOCKQUOTE_STYLE}">${renderTokens((token as Tokens.Blockquote).tokens, context)}</section>`;
        case 'hr':
          return '<section style="height:1px;margin:30px 0;background:#e4e4e7;font-size:0;line-height:0;">&nbsp;</section>';
        case 'list':
          return renderList(token as Tokens.List, context);
        case 'table':
          return renderTable(token as Tokens.Table, context);
        case 'text':
          return token.tokens ? renderInlineTokens(token.tokens, context) : escapeHtml(token.text);
        default:
          return escapeHtml(token.raw);
      }
    }
    
    function renderHeading(depth: number, html: string): string {
      const level = Math.min(Math.max(depth, 1), 6);
      const underline = level === 3 ? `<span style="${HEADING_UNDERLINE_STYLE}">&nbsp;</span>` : '';
      return `<h${level} style="${HEADING_LEVEL_STYLES[level]}">${html}${underline}</h${level}>`;
    }
    
    function renderList(token: Tokens.List, context: CitationContext): string {
      const tag = token.ordered ? 'ol' : 'ul';
      const listStyle = token.ordered ? 'decimal' : 'disc';
      const items = token.items.map((item) => `<li style="margin:0 0 7px;padding-left:3px;">${renderTokens(item.tokens, context)}</li>`).join('');
      return `<${tag} style="margin:4px 0 22px;padding-left:1.5em;list-style-type:${listStyle};">${items}</${tag}>`;
    }
    
    function renderTable(token: Tokens.Table, context: CitationContext): string {
      const header = token.header.map((cell) => `<th style="${tableCellStyle(true, cell.align)}">${renderInlineTokens(cell.tokens, context)}</th>`).join('');
      const rows = token.rows.map((row, rowIndex) => `<tr>${row.map((cell, cellIndex) => `<td style="${tableCellStyle(false, cell.align, rowIndex, cellIndex, rowIndex === token.rows.length - 1)}">${renderInlineTokens(cell.tokens, context)}</td>`).join('')}</tr>`).join('');
      return `<section style="margin:8px 0 24px;border:1px solid ${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.tableRule};border-radius:11px;background:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.tableRow};box-shadow:${ARTICLE_SHADOWS.table};overflow-x:auto;"><table style="width:100%;border-collapse:separate;border-spacing:0;font-size:14px;line-height:1.65;text-align:left;"><thead><tr>${header}</tr></thead><tbody>${rows}</tbody></table></section>`;
    }
    
    function tableCellStyle(header: boolean, align: 'left' | 'center' | 'right' | null, rowIndex = 0, cellIndex = 0, lastRow = false): string {
      if (header) return `padding:12px 14px;border:0;border-top:3px solid ${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.accentUnderline};text-align:${align ?? 'left'};background:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.tableHeader};color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.tableHeaderText};font-weight:700;`;
      const background = cellIndex === 0 ? ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.tableFirstColumn : rowIndex % 2 === 1 ? ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.tableAlternateRow : ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.tableRow;
      const bottom = lastRow ? '' : `border-bottom:1px solid ${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.tableRule};`;
      const firstColumn = cellIndex === 0 ? `border-right:1px solid ${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.tableRule};font-weight:600;` : '';
      return `padding:12px 14px;${bottom}${firstColumn}text-align:${align ?? 'left'};background:${background};color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.text};`;
    }
    
    function renderInlineTokens(tokens: Token[], context: CitationContext): string {
      return tokens.map((token) => renderInlineToken(token, context)).join('');
    }
    
    function nestedTokens(token: Token): Token[] {
      return 'tokens' in token && Array.isArray(token.tokens) ? token.tokens : [];
    }
    
    function asLinkToken(token: Token): Tokens.Link | null {
      if (token.type !== 'link' || !('href' in token) || typeof token.href !== 'string' || !('tokens' in token) || !Array.isArray(token.tokens)) return null;
      return token as Tokens.Link;
    }
    
    function renderInlineToken(token: Token, context: CitationContext): string {
      switch (token.type) {
        case 'text':
        case 'escape':
          return 'tokens' in token && token.tokens ? renderInlineTokens(token.tokens, context) : renderTextWithCitations(token.text, context);
        case 'strong':
          return `<strong style="color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.text};background:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.neutralHighlight};font-weight:600;">${renderInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token), context)}</strong>`;
        case 'em':
          return `<em style="color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.text};">${renderInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token), context)}</em>`;
        case 'del':
          return `<del style="color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.mutedText};">${renderInlineTokens(nestedTokens(token), context)}</del>`;
        case 'codespan':
          return `<code style="${INLINE_CODE_STYLE}">${escapeHtml(token.text)}</code>`;
        case 'br':
          return '<br>';
        case 'link': {
          const link = asLinkToken(token);
          return link ? renderLink(link, context) : escapeHtml(token.raw);
        }
        case 'image':
          return `<img src="${escapeHtml(token.href)}" alt="${escapeHtml(token.text)}" style="display:block;max-width:100%;margin:0 auto 18px;border-radius:4px;">`;
        case 'html':
          return '';
        default:
          return escapeHtml(token.raw);
      }
    }
    
    function renderLink(token: Tokens.Link, context: CitationContext): string {
      const url = normalizeHttpUrl(token.href);
      if (!url) return renderInlineTokens(token.tokens, context);
      if (isWechatArticleUrl(url)) {
        return `<a href="${escapeHtml(url)}" style="color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.text};text-decoration:none;border-bottom:1px solid ${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.rule};">${renderInlineTokens(token.tokens, context)}</a>`;
      }
      const plainText = plainInlineTokens(token.tokens).trim();
      const label = !plainText || token.autolink === true || plainText === url ? referenceSourceLabel(url) : plainText;
      const label = !plainText || token.autolink === true || plainText === url ? referenceSourceLabel(url) : plainText;
      citationNumberFor(url, label, context);
      return `<span style="color:${ARTICLE_STYLE_COLORS.text};font-weight:600;">${escapeHtml(label)}</span>`;
    }
    
    function renderTextWithCitations(value: string, context: CitationContext): string {
      let result = '';
      let lastIndex = 0;

Inline styles keep the output usable inside the MP editor.
